The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

items.title: Area–power–delay Optimized RTL-To-GDSII VLSI Implementation of 16-Bit Ve-Dic Multiplier Using High-Speed Adders
items.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis and an ASIC-oriented design of a 16-bit Vedic Multiplier based on the Urdhva-Tiryakbhyam algorithm using Kogge-Stone (KSA), Carry Look-Ahead (CLA), and Carry Save (CSA) adders. The architectures are implemented in Verilog HDL and evaluated across 45 nm, 90 nm, and 180 nm technology nodes using the Cadence suite. Pre-layout synthesis metrics (cell count, delay, and power) are analyzed to study performance trade-offs across nodes. Furthermore, physical design placement and routing at 90 nm confirms ASIC standard-cell feasibility, although detailed post-route parasitic extraction is reserved for future hardware prototyping. Comparisons with FPGA-based works demonstrate significant improvements in speed and power efficiency, making the proposed KSA-based design highly suitable for high-speed, low-power VLSI and DSP applications.

items.title: A privacy preserving federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification and severity estimation using indian field data
items.abstract: This study presents a privacy-aware federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification and severity estimation using heterogeneous field data collected across Indian agricultural regions. Conventional deep learning approaches rely on centralized data aggregation, which raises concerns related to data privacy, ownership, and scalability in distributed farming environments. To address these challenges, the proposed framework integrates a ResNet-18-based convolutional neural network enhanced with a Convolutional Block Attention Module for discriminative feature extraction, along with a model-contrastive federated learning strategy to mitigate client drift under non-independent and identically distributed data conditions. In addition to disease classification, a severity estimation module is incorporated using Otsu-based segmentation to quantify the proportion of infected leaf area, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of disease progression. The framework is evaluated across multiple federated settings with varying numbers of clients to analyse convergence, robustness, and scalability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 95.49% and a severity estimation accuracy of 94.57% in a five-client setup, while maintaining stable performance above 91% and 92%, respectively, even with increased client participation. High macro-averaged F1-scores and well-defined severity confusion matrices further validate the reliability of the model. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enabling scalable, privacy-aware, and severity-informed disease monitoring, making it suitable for real-world precision agriculture applications.

items.title: A flexible language model-assisted electronic design automation framework
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming electronic design automation (EDA) by enhancing design stages such as schematic design, simulation, netlist synthesis, and place-and-route. Existing methods primarily focus these optimisations within isolated open-source EDA tools and often lack the flexibility to handle multiple domains, such as analogue, digital, and radio-frequency design. In contrast, modern systems require to interface with commercial EDA environments, adhere to tool-specific operation rules, and incorporate feedback from design outcomes while supporting diverse design flows. We propose a versatile framework that uses LLMs to generate files compatible with commercial EDA tools and optimise designs using power-performance-area reports. This is accomplished by guiding the LLMs with tool constraints and feedback from design outputs to meet tool requirements and user specifications. The framework is used to evaluate case studies on operational transconductance amplifiers, microstrip patch antennas, and FPGA circuits.

items.title: A Survey on LLMs from a Human-Centric Perspective
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) has positioned them as powerful computational instruments for human-centered research and applications, spanning tasks involving cognition, decision-making, and social interaction. This survey examines LLMs from a human-centric perspective organized around individual and collective levels. We first review LLM competencies across perception, analysis, integration, execution, and social interaction, highlighting both their demonstrated capabilities and the evaluation conditions under which these capabilities are observed. We then explore how LLMs are used across behavioral science, psychology, linguistics, political science, economics, and sociology as research tools, behavioral simulators, and objects of inquiry, covering both individual behavior and collective social processes. Finally, we identify challenges and future research directions, such as improving LLM adaptability, affective-to-behavior evaluation, and cultural sensitivity, while addressing inherent biases and enhancing frameworks for human-AI collaboration. This survey aims to provide a foundational understanding of LLMs from a human-centric perspective, offering insights into their current capabilities and potential for future development.

items.title: A Compact Low Power CCII-Based LIF Neuron with Memristive Synapse Exhibiting Synaptic Plasticity
items.abstract: Biological neural systems perform information processing through the collective operation of neurons and synapses, in which learning is achieved by activity-dependent modification of synaptic strength. Emulating these mechanisms in electronic circuits requires compact, low-power, and scalable implementations of spiking neurons and adaptive synapses. This paper presents a compact, low-power second-generation current conveyor (CCII)- based leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with a memristive synapse exhibiting synaptic plasticity. The proposed neuron operates in the current domain. It employs a CCII to implement weighted summation of presynaptic inputs, leaky membrane integration, and threshold-based spike generation using a low-power comparator and a PMOS-based reset mechanism. Both a resistor and a memristor are used to represent synaptic weights at the neuron inputs. At the same time, a memristive device is employed as the synapse in the learning model to provide continuously variable, emulated memristive conductance. In addition, spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is implemented, in which the relative timing difference between presynaptic and postsynaptic spikes governs the change in synaptic strength. A two-neuron system comprising a presynaptic and a postsynaptic neuron, interconnected via a memristor serving as the synapse, is used to demonstrate long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). During LTP, the memristor conductance increases, whereas during LTD, the conductance decreases, thereby demonstrating synaptic plasticity similar to biological systems. The proposed circuit is designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso using 0.18μm CMOS technology to verify its operational performance. Simulation results validate correct LIF operation, stable learning behaviour, and low power consumption (23 μW) in standard 0.18 μm CMOS technology, confirming the suitability of the proposed neuron-synapse architecture for neuromorphic computing systems.
items.venue: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers

items.title: (A)iSpy: Parasitic Trojans for Machine Learning Infrastructure
items.abstract: Modern machine learning (ML) pipelines depend heavily on third party libraries for graph compilation and hardware acceleration. While current practices audit data and model artifacts or rely on file integrity checks, the execution environment remains implicitly trusted. This blind spot enables active threats where a malicious runtime module interacts directly with live training and inference dynamics: exploiting this interaction allows the Trojan to support complex objectives that are challenging for static code or binary modifications, achieving manipulations impossible for standard data and model level attacks. We expose this vulnerability by presenting AiSPY, a parasitic infrastructure Trojan that subverts MLsystems through an active observe and execute paradigm. Operating within the computation graph, AiSPY monitors transient tensor states to perform targeted, stealthy manipulations with negligible overhead. To violate confidentiality, the Trojan identifies all critical training hyperparameters and covertly exfiltrates them via model weights or output logits. To break integrity, it acts as a gradient amplifier: by observing steganographic triggers, it transforms other- wise weak data poisoning into effective backdoor attacks, increasing success rates from near zero to 100%. We further demonstrate broad extensibility across the machine learning lifecycle by validating auxiliary attacks in the appendix, including subpopulation label flipping, availability disruptions, and inference stage manipulations. Importantly, the evaluated malware scanners do not flag AiSPY because current public rule sets lack coverage for ML runtime Trojans, while the associated poisoned inputs and resulting compromised models bypass state-of-the-art inspection tools. We demonstrate the practicality of this threat with an implementation in the ONNX Runtime training and inference engines.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Starscream: Reimagining LLM Sharding on AMD Instinct GPUs with GPU Partitioning
items.abstract: As GPU accelerators grow larger to meet rising compute demands, they exhibit increasingly pronounced non-uniform memory access (NUMA) characteristics that challenge existing LLM frameworks. Chiplet-based architectures provide a practical path to larger GPUs while mitigating manufacturing yield constraints. Modern GPUs such as AMD Instinct MI300X employs such a multi-die design, and further offer GPU partitioning capabilities, partitioning a single physical GPU into multiple logical devices with NUMA-aware memory domains, promising faster kernel launches, and reduced memory access latencies with improved locality. However, current parallelization strategies, designed for homogeneous GPU topologies, when applied under partitioning, extend its unidimensional sharding causing significant performance degradation. Three bottlenecks emerge: (1) memory redundancy; (2) arithmetic intensity collapse; (3) communication overhead from flat collectives. We present Starscream, a rethinking of LLM sharding for the chiplet era. Rather than stretching inter-GPU sharding thinner, Starscream adds intra-GPU sharding along an orthogonal dimension, grounded in three foundational principles: kernel shape preservation, memory redundancy elimination, and communication overhead minimization. These principles form the basis for extending any sharding strategy into the partitioning regime. We demonstrate their effectiveness using tensor parallelism as a case study. On AMD MI300X and MI355X, exploiting partitioning capabilities yields up to 4x speedup for attention and 1.43x for fused GEMMs compared to chiplet-oblivious baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of chiplet-aware designs. Starscream's principles generalize across sharding strategies and future architectures.

items.title: HARE: Fast Read Disturbance Threshold Profiling in Modern DRAM Chips via Reduced Timing Constraints
items.abstract: Modern DRAM chips are vulnerable to read disturbance, which manifests as bitflips in a victim row physically near an aggressor row that is repeatedly activated. State-of-the-art mitigations rely on accurate and exhaustive profiling of the read disturbance threshold (RDT), i.e., the minimum number of aggressor row activations needed to induce the first bitflip. However, RDT changes significantly and unpredictably over time, motivating online profilers that dynamically adjust a mitigation's RDT configuration. RDT profiling is costly for online profilers (e.g., hundreds of seconds for a 16-bank DDR4 module) because 1) measuring a single DRAM row's RDT requires many activations and 2) each DRAM row can have a different RDT, requiring many rows to be profiled. We introduce HARE, an online RDT profiling technique that intentionally exacerbates read disturbance to quickly profile a DRAM module. HARE's key idea is to reduce the timing constraints between consecutive DRAM commands during profiling. Doing so significantly reduces profiling time by 1) directly reducing the execution time of the profiling command sequence and 2) exacerbating read disturbance such that the first bitflip occurs at a smaller activation count than with the conventional RowHammer sequence. From our characterization of 180 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major DRAM manufacturers, we make three observations. First, HARE measures a DRAM row's RDT 31.2% faster than the RowHammer profiler and a DRAM module's minimum RDT with an average reduction of 21.7%. Second, HARE flips more than 95% of the cells that the RowHammer pattern flips. Third, HARE preserves the RDT ranking of rows well enough such that it can exhaustively reprofile a small set of rows to improve its minimum RDT estimation. Our end-to-end evaluations show that HARE enables significant system performance improvements and outperforms the RowHammer profiler.

items.title: Nonlocal multipolar spin accumulation in altermagnets beyond d-wave
items.abstract: In spin-conserving models of $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, the uniform longitudinal conductivity has no spin-odd component. A point injector reveals higher moments of the Fermi velocity through the nonlocal spin accumulation. Boltzmann theory predicts that the rank $m=2,4,6$ of the first nonzero spin-odd velocity moment sets the leading angular harmonic, its asymptotic radial dependence $r^{2-m}$, and its amplitude scaling $τ^{m-3}$ at fixed distance and injected current. For $g$-wave order, the fourth moment produces a fourth angular harmonic with an asymptotic $r^{-2}$ tail. Quantum transport simulations support the radial profiles predicted by finite-geometry Boltzmann theory without an amplitude fit. Across the three symmetries, the quantum amplitudes exceed the Boltzmann predictions based on the Born scattering time by $15-65$\% in the windows analyzed. In a two-contact ribbon, we detect the $g$-wave fourth harmonic at $6.8\,σ$ in an independent set of 1800 disorder realizations using a preselected radial window. Its amplitude decreases when the altermagnetic splitting is reduced.

items.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
items.abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

items.title: Sub-100KB On-Device CNN Training via Dynamic Sparse Updates and Hardware--Software Co-Design
items.abstract: The increasing demand for real-time processing and personalized deep learning has made edge-device training essential but challenging due to high memory and computational costs. To address this, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training accelerator with a dynamic sparse update mechanism that selectively updates important parameters using a random channel strategy, avoiding costly evaluations. Combined with activation pruning, our approach reduces activation storage to just 3.4\% of the original. Our hardware features a fused forward dataflow that concurrently processes group normalization and convolution, reducing training time by 45\% through computation reordering and efficient zero-skipping. Implemented in TSMC 28nm at FP8 precision, the design operates at 800 MHz, achieving 8 TOPS peak throughput, 31.13 TOPS/W energy efficiency, and 14.8 TOPS/mm$^2$ area efficiency, with power consumption ranging from 257 to 272 mW. The design enables on-device training within a sub-100KB on-chip SRAM budget (95KB in silicon).

items.title: 国产AI算力硬件开源技术手册(V1.0)
items.abstract: 摘要 当前全球AI算力发展受限于芯片热密度、存储带宽、芯粒集成、集群互联四大物理工程瓶颈,海外算力生态形成较强的技术与产业链壁垒。国内芯片、存储、封装、高速互联各领域已经积累大量成熟技术基础,但各主体技术分散,缺少一套统一的顶层工程方案完成体系整合。本手册立足于现有国产产业底座,提出一套开放共享的硬件优化技术框架,分别从芯片热管理、存储同步架构、大规模芯粒集成封装、集群高速场互联四个模块给出设计思路、适配方案、预期技术指标与开源交付内容,提出国内多方产业主体协同合作体的组织模式与分工路径。本手册不绑定特定基础物理概念,只输出可用于工程研讨、原型验证的实施方案,旨在助力国内大模型训练硬件支撑体系建设,推动算力硬件技术自主迭代。 Abstract The development of global AI computing power is currently restricted by four major physical and engineering bottlenecks: chip thermal density, memory bandwidth, chiplet integration, and cluster interconnection. Overseas computing ecosystems have formed strong technical and industrial chain barriers. Although China has accumulated mature technologies in chips, storage, advanced packaging, and high-speed interconnection, technical resources are scattered among different enterprises and lack a unified top-level engineering system for integration. Based on the existing domestic industrial foundation, this manual proposes an open hardware optimization framework covering chip thermal management, memory synchronization architecture, large-scale chiplet integration packaging, and high-speed cluster field interconnection. It provides design principles, domestic adaptation schemes, expected technical indicators, and open-source deliverables, and establishes a collaborative mechanism for domestic industrial participants. Without relying on specific basic physical theories, this manual offers implementable engineering solutions and prototype verification directions, aiming to support the construction of domestic large-model training hardware systems and promote independent iteration of domestic AI computing infrastructure.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar Switch Integration with Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture for Standard Ternary Inverters
items.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

items.title: Use and perceptions of AI tools among Australian general practice registrars: a national survey
items.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used in health care, yet little is known about how often Australian general practitioner trainees (GP registrars) use them or how they perceive the impact of AI on training and clinical care. Aim This study aimed to examine how frequently registrars use AI tools for clinical care and education, types of AI used, the perceived benefits and risks, and training needs. Methods A national cross-sectional online survey conducted from 7 May to 4 June 2024 invited 3743 Australian General Practice Training or Fellowship Support Program registrars to participate. The survey assessed frequency and context of AI use, practice-level adoption, perceived impacts, training exposure, and ethical-legal concerns. Analyses were descriptive. Results Among the 727 respondents (19.5%), frequent use (weekly or more) was uncommon; 7.3% for clinical tasks, 5.0% for education. Practice-level adoption was low, with 10.8% reporting subscription to AI tools. Most registrars anticipated benefits, particularly learning efficiency and administrative workload reduction. However, 25.0% perceived increased medicolegal risk. Formal training was rare, with most relying on self-directed learning, though many rated AI education as important. Among clinical users, common tools included large language models (32.5%), remote patient monitoring devices (28.6%), and voice-to-text tools (26.2%). Large language models predominated in education (63.5%). Discussion In May–June 2024, AI tool use among registrars was limited, although most perceived potential benefit. Enthusiasm was tempered by concerns about safety, ethics, and legal risks. Structured training and guidelines are needed to support safe, effective integration into GP registrars’ practice and education.

items.title: Transferable Machine Learning of Electronic Hamiltonians with Superposition-of-Atomic-Potentials Features
items.abstract: Abstract Machine learning of electronic Hamiltonians offers a unified route to electronic wave functions and physical observables. We introduce a Hamiltonian learning framework built on electronic features derived from the superposition-of-atomic-potentials (SAP) approximation, an efficient self-consistent-field initial guess that captures essential electron–electron screening. SAP quantities define a symmetry-adapted intrinsic atomic orbital learning basis and provide physics-informed inputs to an orbital-based graph neural network that predicts converged Kohn–Sham Fock matrices. To extend the approach to larger basis sets, we further develop a downfolding scheme that predicts large-basis electronic structure from minimal-basis features. On the QM9 data set, the model accurately reproduces frontier and core orbital energies, dipole moments, and the full density of states. For organic charge-transport materials, it yields accurate intermolecular transfer integrals for benzene, tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), and tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) dimers. The model also generalizes to unseen substituted-benzene heterodimers, with a mean absolute error of 4.8 meV. These results establish SAP-based Hamiltonian learning as a transferable and scalable tool for high-throughput electronic-structure prediction.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Thermal annealing effects on total-ionizing-dose radiation hardness in HfO2 /SiC MOS structures
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal annealing is a critical step in fabricating hafnium oxide/silicon carbide (HfO 2 /SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) devices. However, its effect on total ionizing dose (TID) radiation hardness remains unclear. We find that for the unannealed Sample A, γ -ray irradiation (300 krad(Si)) produces a positive flat-band voltage shift (V fb ) of 1.76 V. Compared with Sample A, the annealed Sample B (975 ℃ rapid thermal annealing, RTA) shows a reduction in the interface trap density ( D it ) at the HfO 2 /SiC interface from 1.01 × 10 13 cm -2 ·eV -1 to 3.67 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 , and an increase in the breakdown field strength of the MOS capacitor from 5.28 MV/cm to 6.91 MV/cm. However, Sample B suffers from adverse effects after irradiation, such as a negative V fb shift, a reduction in barrier height ( φ b ), and a degradation of the breakdown field (1.98 MV/cm). Therefore, we propose a pre-annealing step at 550 ℃ for 30 minutes (Sample C) prior to the RTA. This pre-annealing converts the negative V fb shift caused by TID effects into a positive V fb shift. Furthermore, the D it of this sample drops to 1.61 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 after irradiation, while φ b increases from 0.42 eV to 1.18 eV. XPS depth profiling reveals irradiation-induced redistribution of Hf-O coordination and the emergence of an O-Hf-C interfacial component, which we interpret as consistent with oxygen-mediated defect reordering. These findings reveal how thermal annealing influences the TID radiation response of HfO 2 dielectrics and provide critical guidance for the development of radiation-tolerant HfO 2 /SiC devices intended for extreme-environment applications.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: The horizon of artificial intelligence: LLMs and hardware, its current pillars
items.abstract: LLMs and hardware, its current pillars

items.title: The Singularity is 4 Bits: Compiling Bounded Specialist Chains for Local Neuromorphic Execution
items.abstract: Many decisions recur, and when their inputs, state and allowed outcomes can be written down, they do not need a general-purpose model on every call. Borrowing the form of "Attention Is All You Need," this paper proposes that for recurring bounded decisions, meaning decisions with fixed, fully specified inputs and outcomes, one compiled specialist whose stored synaptic weights are four bits is enough. We built an architecture that compiles each such task into a small specialist that runs locally, and links specialists into chains by passing explicit, typed state from one to the next. The compiler derives relational features, such as whether two fields are equal, from the declared types of the task's fields. It then trains a small linear classifier, converts its scores into four-bit synaptic weights, and saves the model with the rules for mapping inputs, reading outputs and ending execution. Only the stored synaptic weight is four bits. Accumulation and host arithmetic use wider integers. Executed in the official simulator of BrainChip's Akida software development kit, the saved four-bit specialists made no errors on 75, 55 and 60 repeated withheld decisions across three finite tasks defined by written rules, each run from five fresh random starting points (initializations), and completed all 15 multi-step trajectories. On a circular-dial task, an ordered relation made no errors on 60 withheld decisions. Equality-only features made 45 errors and raw fields made 59. An exact-arithmetic certificate proves that no linear classifier on either of those two feature sets can strictly separate the training labels. Each saved specialist is a 78,054-byte file, and a chain experiment preserves the capacity-gate trajectory across one, two, four and twelve virtual target placements. Four bits is thus a precision shown to work for compiling recurring decisions into bounded, locally executed specialists. Next come physical execution on a twelve-chip Akida board, larger task suites and chains that span devices.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

items.title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
items.abstract: Spin-orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

items.title: Study planning is better served by Monte Carlo simulation than AI-generated participants
items.abstract: ‘Silicon samples’, AI-generated synthetic data based on demographic profiles, have been proposed to help plan research. Here, I argue that Monte Carlo simulation already does this job transparently, and that generative AI is better used to help write such simulations.

items.title: Structural and electronic properties of oxygen deficient HfO2-x thin films: from insulator to metal
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide (HfO₂) and its oxygen-deficient variants (HfO₂₋ₓ) are key candidates for next-generation electronics, ranging from photonics and photocatalysis to both resistive and ferroelectric memories. Sub-stoichiometric HfO₂₋ₓ reduces the forming voltage in ReRAM devices and stabilizes the orthorhombic ferroelectric phase crucial for non-volatile FeRAM, yet a systematic understanding of its electronic evolution remains elusive. Here, we synthesize a complete series of HfO₂₋ₓ thin films spanning from stoichiometric oxide to pure metal and map their structural and electronic transformations. By combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, resistivity profiling, and Hf L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure, we reveal clear stoichiometry-driven trends in bonding, phase formation, and electronic structure, providing a definitive reference for tailoring HfO₂₋ₓ in advanced memory and photonic applications.

items.title: Single-Tube Eight-Plex Full-Length PCR-NGS for High-Resolution HLA Typing: Assay Validation and Exploratory ADO-Risk Quality Control
items.abstract: Background: High-resolution typing of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genes is a core technology for dissecting genetic polymorphism in the MHC region of the human genome and has important clinical value in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, solid organ transplantation, and tumor immunotherapy. Although full-length HLA typing methods based on next-generation sequencing (NGS) can achieve high-resolution results, long-range PCR amplification carries the risk of allelic dropout (ADO). Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in primer-binding regions may cause the amplification failure of a given allele, leading to heterozygotes being misclassified as homozygotes and resulting in HLA typing errors. Such mistyping during donor selection for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may lead to HLA matching errors between donors and recipients, increasing the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or transplant rejection. Existing NGS approaches generally rely on a single set of amplification primers and lack an independent verification mechanism. Methods: This study designed a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay and performed systematic methodological validation. The assay simultaneously co-amplifies eight classical HLA genes (HLA-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, -DQB1, -DPB1, -DPA1, and -DQA1) in a single tube, with primers anchored in the conserved 5′UTR and 3′UTR regions to capture the complete gene sequences, and high-resolution typing was performed using the HLA-HD software. Sanger sequencing-based typing (SBT) and PacBio/ONT third-generation long-read sequencing served as dual gold standards, and multi-level validation was completed using 92 anonymous peripheral blood genomic DNA samples from the Chinese population and the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line. During primer testing, we found that two samples exhibited allele loss at the HLA-DRB1 locus in the context of SNPs in the primer-binding region, indicating that ADO risk exists in practice; after adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, ADO in these samples was resolved, but the limitations of PCR technology and the high polymorphism of HLA dictate that ADO cannot be fundamentally eliminated by primer adjustment. Accordingly, we further designed, in an exploratory manner, a 6-plex QC assay whose primer-binding regions do not overlap at all with those of the 8-plex system, for proportional spot-checking verification in large-scale sample testing. Typing results were reported and used for consistency statistics primarily at 3-field resolution; the assay can read up to 4-field resolution, but given that the accuracy of 4-field interpretation cannot be independently verified by existing gold standards, 4-field data were retained only as exploratory supplementary results. Results: (1)Validation of the 8-plex system: For the 10 SBT reference samples, the 2-field typing concordance rate was 100%, and 4-field high-resolution results could be output; the 8-plex typing of 10 blinded samples matched the PacBio third-generation sequencing 3-field results 100%; the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line typing showed no discrepancies compared with the official Cellosaurus data. (2) Discovery of ADO risk: During primer testing, two samples that were heterozygous by SBT were misclassified as homozygous by the 8-plex assay; sequence alignment analysis revealed high-frequency SNPs in the primer-binding region of the 8-plex assay for these two samples, suggesting that primer binding may have been affected. After adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, the 8-plex typing results were consistent with SBT, confirming heterozygosity. (3) Exploration of 6-plex QC: Stratified validation included 31 samples in total, comprising 10 samples dually validated by the 8-plex assay and third-generation sequencing, one standard cell line, and 20 randomly sampled clinical samples; the 8-plex and 6-plex typing results were completely consistent for all these samples; the allele depth ratio (ADR) was mostly ≤2.0 across loci in the 6-plex assay. (4) Performance evaluation: The ADR was mostly ≤2.0 across all samples; the ranking of polymorphism abundance at each locus was consistent with the trends in published Chinese population cohorts; the rare allele HLA-DPB1*744:01 was successfully captured and verified by third-generation sequencing (ONT). Conclusions: This study designed and validated a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay, which showed stable amplification, accurate typing, strong rare-allele capture capability, short turnaround time, and controllable batch testing costs in 92 Chinese population samples. During validation, ADO risk was found to exist in practice; adjusting primers for known SNP sites can correct specific ADO events but cannot fundamentally eliminate the risk. The 6-plex independent QC assay designed on this basis showed complete concordance with the 8-plex results in 31 samples, but its ability to correct real ADO events remains a theoretical inference and an indirect validation, and further evaluation through long-term clinical accumulation or large-scale parallel validation is still needed. This method is expected to provide an accurate, economical, and practical new approach for clinical high-resolution HLA typing.

items.title: Simultaneous extraction of multiple buffer-trap parameters in GaN HEMTs via measurement-window sweeping: A TCAD study
items.abstract: Abstract The duration of the measurement window strongly affects the observed current collapse in GaN HEMTs and can obscure the individual contributions of buffer traps. Using TCAD simulations of output measurements following off-state stress, this work tracks trap emission and recapture and develops a multi-exponential time-domain deconvolution method based on measurement-window sweeping. The drain current sampled at the knee voltage is analyzed as a function of the measurement-window duration to extract characteristic time constants and recovery-current amplitudes. Two-trap tests resolve the distinct recovery steps associated with Fe and deeper trap components and quantify their individual contributions. For multi-component responses, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) and time-constant-collapse criteria are used jointly to determine the number of resolvable components and identify overfitting. In the uniform-profile multi-trap test, the fitted time constants of the dominant recovery components agree with the prescribed values within approximately 16%. A further test with a nonuniform Fe profile resolves distinct fast E1 and slow Fe recovery components, with time-constant deviations of −0.85% and −29.3%, respectively. By simultaneously extracting characteristic time constants and relative contributions to the recoverable current-collapse amplitude, the method provides a quantitative basis for assessing the impact of individual trap components and guiding epitaxial and process optimization.

items.title: Silent Data Corruption (SDC) and No Trouble Found (NTF): Ways of Improving Test Towards 0 ppm
items.abstract: The identification and testing of semiconductor components is among the most expensive stages of memory production. Despite multi-insertion testing at several temperatures, customers still report application failures of 20–50 ppm for complex components such as dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), and field failures are often not reproducible in the production flow (no trouble found, NTF). This work examines whether application-based testing under application-representative conditions can expose such failures. Two platforms are used: an FPGA-based tester (RHINOE) with 192 sockets on six tiles, and an Intel CPU-based platform (OCTOPUS) that reproduces a customer memory-controller and BIOS environment. For about 10,000 4 G DDR3 devices, the conventional array test gave about 2% yield loss, whereas the FPGA-based application test gave about 6% at the same 98 °C/110 ms retention guard band. Five of ten customer-returned DDR3 devices, whose failures were not reproduced in the conventional flow, failed on the FPGA platform. In a 32-device cross-tile comparison, five devices that passed under calibrated settings failed when per-tile voltage calibration was omitted. In a one-week test of 1000 DDR4 devices, two transient single-cell events were observed. The results support application-based testing as a complement to production test; a zero-defect rate is not demonstrated, and the mechanisms of the transient events were not identified.

items.title: Self-Specializing Neuromorphic Computer: A Distributed Architecture Beyond the NPU
items.abstract: A concept paper proposing a self-specialising neuromorphic compute architecture built from existing technologies. Core ideas: Hardware that specialises itself through use: a RISC core offloading work to reconfigurable logic and analog memristor crossbars. Task training: specialisation through exposure to a varied class of related tasks, with checkpoints for rollback. Routing learned from results: inter-cell routes weighted by accuracy, speed and round-trip time, giving self-organisation and self-healing. Includes the motivation for departing from digital simulation of neural networks, related work, one illustrative implementation (component budget and power targets), and open questions for the community. Shared to stimulate discussion rather than as a finished design. Feedback welcome.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: replication package (code, results and paper)
items.abstract: Code, result tables, figures, decision and assumption logs, and the working paper for Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree. An open panel of 24,210 listing-months of posted GPU rental prices (NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026), four identification strategies for the age-price profile, asset values and economic life, and a seven-firm earnings restatement. `make all` rebuilds every table, figure and the paper from the archived raw files. The raw files whose sources permit redistribution and the public panel are deposited as a separate Zenodo dataset; the rest are re-fetched by the repository's collectors, with checksums in release/raw_manifest.csv. Code is MIT-licensed; the dataset is CC BY 4.0. See README.md.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: GPU rental-price panel and redistributable raw data
items.abstract: Data deposit for the working paper Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree (Ajai Upadhyaya, November 2026). release/dataset/gpu_rental_panel.csv is the public panel of monthly median posted GPU rental prices (USD per GPU-hour, nominal and in 2025 dollars) for NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026; rows available only from the SkyPilot catalog history, which has no licence, are omitted. data/raw/ holds every raw file whose source permits redistribution: the author's own GPU benchmark runs and hand-recorded prices, Epoch AI hardware data (CC BY 4.0), EIA Form 861M, BLS CPI-U and SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL facts, each with a sidecar recording source URL, retrieval time and HTTP status. release/raw_manifest.csv lists every raw file used by the paper with its SHA-256 and the command that re-fetches the files not deposited here. Code, results and the paper are in the companion software record, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24143074. The panel is CC BY 4.0; third-party files keep their sources' terms.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Reliability of atomic-column localization in scanning transmission electron microscopy under noise, annotation variation, and domain shift
items.abstract: Abstract Reliable atomic-column coordinates are essential for quantitative structural analysis in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), yet strong performance on clean images does not ensure reliable localization under noise or across imaging domains. Localization errors can also propagate into coordinate-based structural measurements. Here, we evaluate automated atomic-site localization using Hybrid-STEMSeg, a compact convolutional neural network (CNN)--Transformer segmentation model, alongside established segmentation and microscopy-specific baselines. We test parent-held-out Sm-doped BiFeO$_3$ images under controlled corruption, examine how localization errors affect nearest-neighbor spacing, compare annotation targets, and assess transfer to external STEM datasets with and without target-domain adaptation. Model rankings depend on corruption, annotation, and imaging domain, showing that clean-image scores alone do not identify the most reliable model. Zero-shot transfer is limited, whereas target-domain adaptation improves held-out localization. This evaluation framework helps determine whether a localization model is suited to the imaging conditions and structural analyses for which it is intended.

items.title: Rapid formation of carbon-related defects in SiC induced by SiO desorption from thermally grown and ALD-deposited SiO 2 /4H-SiC(0001) stacks
items.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigate how retaining SiO 2 on 4H-SiC affects carbon-related defect formation in the near-surface region of SiC during Ar annealing at 1500 ℃. The carbon-related defects in SiO 2 /SiC stacks were characterized by attenuated-total-reflection Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy for the samples in which SiO 2 was prepared by either thermal oxidation or atomic-layer deposition. The peak associated with carbon-containing structures rapidly increased as SiO 2 thickness decreased through the SiO 2 /SiC interfacial reaction generating volatile SiO. Another peak correlated with the structures containing both carbon and oxygen appeared only in thermally oxidized samples. These results indicate that the retained SiO 2 film acts as a reactant to trigger the formation of carbon-related defects in the near surface region of SiC rather than as an inert protective layer when SiO 2 /SiC stacks are annealed at a high temperature.

items.title: Negative differential transconductance in deterministically transferred CVD-Grown monolayer WSe2/MoS2 heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Electrostatic control of the band alignment in two-dimensional van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is a fundamental requirement for realizing low-power tunnelling electronics, multi-valued logic and next-generation functional devices. Yet, its experimental demonstration in scalable chemical vapour deposition (CVD)-grown heterostructures remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a simple heterostructure field-effect transistor based on deterministically transferred CVD-grown monolayers of WSe2 and MoS2. These materials are stacked using a contact-first, transfer-later fabrication strategy that enables localized electrostatic modulation of the heterointerface. The fabricated device exhibits two distinct drain-current minima in its transfer characteristics, with the first minimum occurring at a fixed back-gate voltage, while the second minimum shifts with drain voltage. Analysis around the first current minimum reveals a pronounced negative differential transconductance (NDT), with a peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) of 16 at room temperature, providing a clear electrical signature of band-to-band tunnelling (BTBT). The observed transport behaviour originates from strong electrostatic doping induced by the back gate, which drives the WSe2/MoS2 heterointerface from a staggered (type-II) to a broken (type-III) bandgap alignment, enabling interlayer BTBT under large negative gate bias. As the gate voltage is increased, the loss of the broken-gap alignment terminates the tunnelling process, producing a gate-voltage-pinned current minimum and the associated NDT response. These findings establish that CVD-grown vdW heterostructures can achieve controllable electrostatic band engineering and room-temperature tunnelling phenomena using a simple single-back-gate architecture, providing an experimentally practical pathway towards future low-power tunnelling transistors, multi-valued logic circuits, and electrically reconfigurable two-dimensional electronic devices.
authors: O V Vishnu Vardhan Koundinya Koundinya

items.title: Nanoscale ZnO Coatings on Poly(methyl methacrylate) Submicron Spheres via Low-Temperature Atomic Layer Deposition for Enhanced UV-Blocking Properties
items.abstract: Abstract Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), a synthetic thermoplastic polymer, has been extensively used in our lives due to its advantageous properties such as high transparency, lightweight, and biocompatibility. Although PMMA exhibits great potential in sunscreens, its poor UV-blocking properties hinder its practical applications. In this study, we modified the PMMA submicron spheres (120–150 nm) with nanoscale ZnO using atomic layer deposition (ALD) in a fluidized bed reactor at a low temperature of 40 °C, with diethylzinc (DEZ) and water as precursors. We systematically investigated the ZnO-coated PMMA microspheres using FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, XPS, and TG to elucidate the mechanism of nucleation and growth of ZnO. The results revealed that the ZnO deposited was polycrystalline, displaying a granular morphology on the PMMA surfaces. Specifically, a nanoparticle-coated structure was observed after low-cycle ALD, while a conformal nanofilm was formed after high-cycle ALD on the PMMA spheres, suggesting an island growth mode of ZnO. The analysis of the surface chemical species and functional groups via XPS and in situ FTIR indicated that the fast nucleation of ZnO was attributed to trace amounts of hydroxyl groups and hydrogen-bonded water molecules bound on the surfaces of the emulsion-polymerized submicron PMMA spheres. After ZnO coating, the PMMA microspheres exhibited improved UV-blocking performance. The reflectance within the 280–400 nm UV range dropped sharply from ca. 95% (pristine PMMA) to 19% for the PMMA/ZnO composite which had an optical bandgap of 3.36 eV. Meanwhile, the average visible-light reflectance remained above 93%. Moreover, owing to the physical barrier effect of the ZnO coating, the derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) peak temperature increased by 30 °C and the acetone resistance improved. This study not only provides a feasible strategy for modifying polymeric particle surfaces and fabricating organic–inorganic hybrid materials but could also advance the uses of PMMA spheres in high-end cosmetics.

items.title: Multifunctional vortex magnetic tunnel junctions with optical and radio-frequency inputs for neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Abstract The brain co-locates memory and processing, but many neuromorphic devices need standby power or separate memory from nonlinear computation. Here we show that vortex magnetic tunnel junctions with a non-volatile, thermally programmable storage layer provide two complementary nonlinear channels in one nanopillar. The laser-induced voltage is linear in laser power but cubic in direct-current bias, making the bias current a nonlinear, programmable weight, whereas radio-frequency excitation is rectified into a frequency-dependent voltage. Crossbar simulations using measured responses classify handwritten digits with 95.4\% accuracy using optical inputs and 94.9\% using radio-frequency inputs, comparable to an equal-size digital single-layer network. Microlenses focusing light to sub-micrometre spots, one formed directly on a junction, and a flip-chip-mounted vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser array provide a route to on-chip optical addressing. Operating both channels together could combine optical and radio-frequency inputs within one nanoscale device, making vortex junctions reprogrammable multi-input building blocks for analog neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Multidimensional Bayesian Optimization of Nanosheet Double-Gate LDMOS for Enhanced Power Figure of Merit
items.abstract: Abstract This work investigates and optimizes a nanosheet-inspired Double-Gate Lateral Double-Diffused Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (DG-LDMOS) architecture using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations combined with Bayesian Optimization (BO), addressing the limitations of sequential manual tuning. By progressively expanding the optimization space from individual parameters to a six-dimensional design space, the optimized nanosheet DG-LDMOS intended for switched-mode operation achieves an intrinsic ultra-low specific on-state resistance of 0.17~m$\Omega\cdot$mm$^{2}$ and a breakdown voltage of 11.32~V, corresponding to a power figure of merit (FOM) of 738~kW/mm$^{2}$. The results reveal that FOM enhancement originates from coupled geometrical and doping optimization, which simultaneously shortens the conduction path, redistributes the lateral electric field, and enhances near-interface carrier transport. These findings demonstrate the importance of simultaneous optimization of strongly coupled device parameters and establish the nanosheet DG-LDMOS as a physics-based foundation for subsequent three-dimensional Gate-All-Around (GAA) LDMOS development.

items.title: Morphological Evolution and Optical Modeling of ZnO/Mn/ZnO Multilayer Thin films via Mn Interlayer Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract The influence of Mn on the structural and optical characterization of ZnO/Mn/ZnO multilayer thin films has been systematically investigated. Thin film samples with Mn layer thickness between 0-80nm were prepared by using a combination of atomic layer deposition (ALD) for ZnO, and direct current magnetron sputtering (DC) for Mn interlayer. The addition of Mn between the ZnO layers alters the electronic structure and defect distribution of the system, leading to observable changes in optical response. The thickness, morphology and optical response of the thin films under study were examined via X-Ray reflectivity (XRR), focused on the ion beam (FIB) cross-sectioning, scanning electron microscope (SEM). XRR analysis revealed an increase in surface roughness of the films and Mn layer density with higher Mn thickness, indicating improved Mn layer compactness, while FIB and SEM analysis confirmed the thickness and showed relatively sharp interfaces. From the measured transmittance and reflectance (T& R) spectra, a decrease in the refractive index n and the valence and surface electron energy loss functions ( VELF and SELF ), while an increase in the extinction coefficient k , dielectric constants (\(\:{\epsilon\:}_{1}\) and \(\:{\epsilon\:}_{2}\) ) ,and optical and electrical conductivity (σ opt ) and (σ elec ) ), highlighting the tunability of the optical properties with Mn interlayer thickness. The comprehensive analysis of the optical parameters derived confirms that controlled Mn interlayer provides an effective strategy for tuning the electronic and optical properties of ZnO/Mn/ZnO multilayers, making them promising candidates for advanced optoelectronic and photonic applications.

items.title: Modeling the inner electric double layer using short-range machine learning potentials: A critical assessment
items.abstract: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical interfaces typically require large system sizes and long simulation times to obtain reliable thermodynamic properties. In this context, machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for computationally efficient sampling compared to density functional theory-based molecular dynamics simulations. Although conventional short-range MLIPs are recognized as inadequate for modeling the (potentially nanometer-wide) diffuse layer, they may still be capable of describing the inner electric double layer that is relevant for electrochemical reactions. Here, we evaluate the performance of common (short-ranged) MLIP architectures [the deep potential DP, the (graph) atomic cluster expansion-based models GRACE and MACE, and the pre-trained eSEN-OC25] for charged Au/electrolyte interfaces. In the evaluation, we focus on the effect of message passing and on the potentially adverse effect of data interference when training for a broad range of surface charges. Our results suggest that both local and message-passing models are able to reliably learn the interfacial structure when training on a single charge state. However, when trained on datasets that span multiple charge states, the MLIPs tested yield inconsistent predictions of interfacial water orientation and ion distributions. This behavior can be traced to the MLIPs being "blind" to the actual surface charge. Message-passing models show somewhat greater robustness to mixed-charge training data, likely due to their larger receptive field, but are still prone to artifacts and errors in the description of the interfacial structure. Overall, our results provide practical guidance on the expected accuracy and cross-charge-state transferability of short-ranged MLIPs for the description of the inner layer of electrode/electrolyte interfaces that will be relevant to their use in computational electrocatalysis.

items.title: Maximising photocurrent in ultrathin Nb-doped MoS2 Schottky solar cells
items.abstract: Abstract In ultrathin transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) Schottky solar cells, photocurrent is difficult to control when rectifying-junction formation and hole extraction cannot be optimised independently. Here we separate these functions in Nb-doped MoS2 devices and show that the photogenerated current can be predicted to first order from its optical limit. Using dry van der Waals assembly, we contact p-MoS2 through a heavily doped p+-MoS2/Au hole-extraction layer while independently defining the rectifying interface with Cr or Ag. Scanning photocurrent microscopy localizes the response to the metal/p-MoS2 overlap, and EQE combined with transfer-matrix modelling shows that the spectral photocurrent follows absorptance in the MoS2 layer of the full optical stack. In a before-and-after test on the same device, adding h-BN increases the modelled absorbed-photon limit and the measured photovoltaic output, consistent with h-BN modifying MoS2 absorptance through thin-film interference in the multilayer stack. Across Ag-contacted devices, the experimental photogenerated current density scales with the stack-specific optical-limit current density and is described by an effective AM1.5G-weighted collection factor of approximately 0.86. A representative device reaches 3.0% power conversion efficiency under AM1.5G illumination. These results provide a practical way to predict and improve photocurrent in ultrathin TMDC Schottky photovoltaics from measurable stack parameters.

items.title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. However, it currently relies on specially engineered atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin high- k HfO 2 and ZrO 2 , or high-temperature vapor-phase growth of 2D dielectrics with post-growth transfer process. Here, we report a facile solution-processed 2D dielectric with an ultra-low thermal budget (i.e., at room temperature), while delivering competitive device metrics (e.g., low operating voltage and small hysteresis). This is enabled by an organic-free colloidal ink of montmorillonite (MTM) in environmentally friendly water solvent, eliminating the need for organic ligands or surfactants and thus the post-deposition high-temperature thermal annealing. Specifically, all-solution-processed MoS 2 field-effect transistors with MTM dielectric exhibit a low operating voltage of 1 V and small hysteresis (down to 1 mV). The solution process is generally compatible with diverse n-type and p-type 2D semiconductors such as MoS 2 , MoSe 2 and WSe 2 . Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). The scalable room-temperature solution-processed 2D dielectric offers a route to all-solution-processed and low-voltage 2D electronics.

items.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
items.abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

items.title: Less Deliberate in Teams: Student LLM Use Across Individual and Collaborative Work
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become common in computing courses, we need to understand how the social setting shapes how students use them. This paper reports findings from a semester-long study of 96 undergraduate students who completed six assignments, alternating between individual homework and team project milestones. We tracked LLM usage, prompting habits, and how students verified AI-generated output across all six assignments. LLM usage dropped by 42.7 percentage points when students moved from individual work to their first team milestone, then partly recovered in later team tasks. Students also wrote fewer prompts, used fewer deliberate prompting strategies, and checked LLM output less carefully. The share of students who ran tests on AI-generated code fell by 19.4 percentage points during team assignments and never fully rebounded. A within-student analysis found that 18.9% of students who consistently used LLMs on their own stopped using them entirely in teams, while only 3.2% went the other direction. These results suggest that collaborative context is associated with reduced deliberate LLM engagement beyond what task type alone can explain. The moment students form teams appears to be a critical turning point that may benefit from more explicit instructional support.

items.title: LearnAI: Just-in-Time AI Co-Creation Across Disciplines at a University
items.abstract: As generative AI reshapes professional and educational practice, institutions face a challenge: how to support diverse learners, from non-coders to advanced students, in building confidence and practice with AI-supported problem solving. Most institutional responses bifurcate into conceptual workshops for general audiences or technical courses for computer science majors, leaving few spaces where mixed-ability learners can engage common AI tasks at levels matched to their prior experience. This experience report presents the LearnAI Framework, a two-layer model for just-in-time AI co-creation piloted at a comprehensive teaching university. The Wide-Exposure Layer embeds short presentations in existing courses to build AI awareness at scale, reaching students and faculty across 18 courses in five disciplines. The Customized Co-Creation Layer provides opt-in, one-on-one sessions where clients work with trained undergraduate tutors through a 5-Stage Pedagogical Script: Problem Framing, Tool-Task Mapping, Iterative Co-Prompting, Deployment and Verification, and Ethical Reflection. Over two semesters, 35 clients co-created 36 portfolio websites and over 20 deployed web applications. Interviews with five clients and two tutors suggest a recurring change in how clients described AI use, shifting from treating AI as a passive answer machine to engaging it as a collaborative tool under human direction. A small paired pre/post AI readiness dataset (N=7) provides preliminary descriptive context, and tutor accounts document how the pedagogical script was enacted and adapted across client types. We report on boundary cases including clients who felt overwhelmed and respondents who deliberately rejected AI use. This paper contributes a practical, adoptable framework with initial evidence from a single institution.

items.title: LLM-guided adaptive segmentation of tunnel linings from point clouds
items.abstract: Automated inspection of segmental tunnel linings requires adaptive segmentation from 3D point clouds, yet expert-tuned pipelines often degrade when tunnel conditions vary. This paper presents R4Tun, a large language model (LLM)-driven adaptation framework that extends an expert-designed pipeline (SAM4Tun) with bounded parameter tuning informed by structured context: memory ($m$), state ($s$), and knowledge ($k$). Evaluated on 30 selected Seg2Tunnel subsets (13 regular, 17 complex) across three LLMs, the full $m+s+k$ design raised mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) from 0.18 to 0.43--0.48 and overall accuracy (OA) from 0.42 to 0.59--0.65 relative to the static SAM4Tun baseline, with the near-reference regular (staggered) subsets reaching mIoU 0.784--0.796 across LLMs. Across 270 (30 tunnels $\times$ 3 different LLMs $\times$ 3 context settings) runs, the LLMs showed similar parameter-adjustment trends (with overlapping 95\% CIs on mean gains) and consistently adjusted a shared set of critical parameters. These results support R4Tun as a controlled, label-free, cross-LLM adaptation mechanism in the tested SAM4Tun--Seg2Tunnel setting, demonstrating consistent accuracy gains; we position R4Tun as a mechanism contribution rather than a deployable final-inspection system, in which each bounded parameter change is auditable via logged rationales.

items.title: LLM-Generated Design Problems for Assessing Higher-Order Thinking in Project-Based Learning
items.abstract: Project-based learning (PjBL) is common in computing education, but traditional assessments of PjBL often fail to capture higher-order thinking (HOT), especially in transfer contexts. This study introduces ''design problems'' (DPs): concise, scenario-based prompts that require applying project concepts in new situations, to address this gap. We examined instructor perceptions, the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate DPs, and student experiences. Surveys of 31 instructors, evaluation of 80 LLM-generated DPs, and student performance data showed that while instructors value DPs, creation effort is a barrier. LLMs helped by producing high-quality prompts with strong expert agreement. Students rated DPs from different LLMs similarly, and their performance on DP tasks showed negligible correlation with traditional project grades, suggesting DPs may capture distinct aspects of HOT. Keystroke data also suggested deeper cognitive engagement of students through planning and revision behaviors. Overall, DPs appear to be a useful complement to traditional assessments, especially in situations where AI use or collaboration may undermine individual learning.

items.title: LK-Model-Based TCAD Simulation of Hafnium-Oxide-Based Ferroelectric Memcapacitors for Radiation-Tolerant Neuromorphic Capacitive Synapses
items.abstract: Abstract A W/HZO/HfO2/W/Si ferroelectric memcapacitor was simulated in Silvaco TCAD using the Landau-Khalatnikov (LK) ferroelectric model to examine multilevel capacitance modulation, total ionizing dose (TID) effects, and device-to-system neuromorphic behavior. The simulations show that increasing the write-voltage amplitude strengthens polarization modulation in the HZO layer, producing wider P-V hysteresis loops, clearer switching-current responses, and improved capacitance-state separation. The capacitive memory window (CMW), defined as the zero-bias capacitance-density difference between the upper and lower C-V branches, increases with write voltage, indicating enhanced multilevel capacitance tunability. Under TID irradiation, oxide charge trapping and the associated electric-field perturbation reduce the C-V branch separation and CMW in the adopted model, while distinguishable capacitance states are retained within the investigated dose range. The TCAD-extracted capacitance states were further mapped to synaptic weights for multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based MNIST evaluation. Although irradiation compresses the available capacitance range, the normalized weight states remain sufficiently ordered for stable classification in this simulation framework. These results provide a device-to-system TCAD workflow for evaluating hafnium-based ferroelectric memcapacitors as candidate radiation-tolerant capacitive synapses.

items.title: In-sensor computing paradigms for neuromorphic motion vision
items.abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to autonomous systems and requires the extraction of position, direction, velocity, and acceleration from dynamic visual scenes. Conventional frame-based sensors, silicon event cameras, and position-sensitive detectors provide established solutions, but data transfer and peripheral processing can impose substantial costs in resource-constrained applications. In-sensor computing offers a complementary approach by embedding selected encoding and processing functions in the physical dynamics of optoelectronic devices. This review examines general-purpose motion encoding and task-specific motion processing. Within general-purpose encoding, optoelectronic event motion encoding and fading-memory motion encoding address data redundancy through distinct mechanisms. The former mimics retinal ON/OFF signaling. Programmable bipolar photoresponses provide signals of opposite polarity, while temporal dynamics enable the generation of transient events suitable for processing by spiking neural networks. The latter uses fading-memory devices to retain recent optical inputs as decaying electrical states. When assembled into arrays, these devices act as physical reservoir units that map spatiotemporal inputs into high-dimensional states, from which a trained readout can extract motion information such as trajectories and velocity. For task-specific applications, specialized devices generate collision-sensitive and direction-selective responses at the sensory front end, potentially reducing downstream processing requirements. Finally, we discuss challenges in array uniformity, adaptive operation, peripheral integration, and consistent performance evaluation.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: Implementation of a Speed Optimized Pipelined 32-Bit Floating Point Multiplier for Performance – Critical VLSI Systems
items.abstract: Floating-point multiplication is a critical operation in modern digital systems, including signal processing, scientific computing, graphics processing, and high-performance embedded applications. With increasing computational demands, high-speed and area-efficient arithmetic units are essential. This paper presents the design and VLSI implementation of a 32-bit single-precision float- ing-point multiplier optimized for enhanced performance through architectural improvements. The proposed design improves mantissa multiplication using Ra- dix-4 modified Booth encoding to reduce partial products, thereby lowering switching activity and propagation delay. A Wallace tree reduction structure is employed for fast parallel partial-product compression, significantly accelerating accumulation compared to conventional array multipliers. To further enhance throughput, a pipelined architecture is introduced, dividing computation into bal- anced stages to minimize critical path delay and increase operating frequency. Exponent addition with bias adjustment, along with systematic normalization and rounding units, ensures accurate and stable floating-point computation, including proper handling of edge cases. The design is implemented in Verilog HDL and synthesized using standard VLSI tools. Results demonstrate improved timing performance and optimized hardware utilization compared to conventional archi- tectures, achieving an effective balance between speed, area, and complexity.

items.title: Hybrid Roll‐To‐Plate Printed CMOS Logic Circuits Via an Integrated Gravure‐Flexographic Printing Strategy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Printed electronics offer a scalable route to large‐area, low‐cost, and flexible electronic systems, but multilayer integration remains limited by differences in ink rheology, film formation, and patterning requirements across functional layers. Here, we present a hybrid gravure–flexographic Roll‐to‐Plate (R2P) printing strategy for fully printed single‐walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) thin‐film transistors (TFTs) and complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) logic circuits. Instead of using a single printing method across the device stack, we assigned flexographic printing to the gate and drain‐source (D‐S) electrodes, while using gravure printing for the dielectric, SWCNT semiconductor, and doping layers. The ∼45 nm‐thick flexographic‐printed gate enabled a uniform gravure‐printed BaTiO 3 dielectric with a thickness of 1.8 ± 0.08 µm and an areal capacitance of 13.2 ± 1.2 nF cm − 2 . The resulting p‐ and n‐type SWCNT‐TFTs exhibited mobilities of 0.08 and 0.05 cm 2 V − 1 s − 1 , respectively. Flexographic D‐S printing also reduced threshold‐voltage variation, improving device uniformity for circuit integration. Using these complementary transistors, we fabricated a fully printed CMOS ring oscillator operating at 60 Hz and a D‐Latch at 5 Hz, demonstrating the potential of layer‐specific hybrid printing for scalable printed CMOS electronics.

items.title: How and When Incivility Unfolds in Online Heatwave Communication: Characterizing Public Discussions on Reddit
items.abstract: The increasing frequency of heatwaves has sparked widespread concern and emotionally charged, often uncivil, discussions on social media. Drawing on heatwave communication and online incivility research, this study investigates the patterns and antecedents of incivility in Reddit threads from 2023 to 2024 about heatwaves. Specifically, it examines how incivility unfolds across comment threads and how emotional expressions and topics shape uncivil comments. Using natural language processing (i.e., topic modelling and emotion analysis) as well as a large language model-assisted incivility detection approach, we analyzed 1,369 posts, 10,800 firstlayer comments, and 7,297 second-layer comments from eight climate-and country-related subreddits. Results revealed incivility was more prevalent in comments than posts, with firstlayer incivility significantly predicting second-layer instances, hinting at a contagion effect that intensified in deeper threads. Comments expressing anger, disgust, sadness, or surprise were more likely to be uncivil, and controversial topics like climate change attribution, geopolitical conflicts, and regional impacts strongly correlated with higher incivility. Theoretical and practical implications were discussed.

items.title: Hope for the helpless: Unveiling the drivers of sense of community in cluster housing—Insights from nowdapara Guchchhogram, Ishwardi, a district-level city in northwestern Bangladesh
items.abstract: Climate-induced displacement has intensified the use of state-led resettlement housing as an urban environmental intervention across the Global South. While such programmes are typically evaluated using housing delivery and risk-reduction metrics, their socio-environmental consequences for everyday community life remain poorly understood—particularly in secondary cities. This study examines Sense of Community (SoC) as an emergent outcome of built–environment interactions within a government-developed climate-resettlement settlement in north-western Bangladesh. Using an explanatory single embedded case study of the Nowdapara Guchchhogram 1 (GG), the research adopts a mixed-methods approach that combines household surveys (n = 100), semi-structured interviews (n = 27), field observations, and statistical analyses in IBM SPSS version 21. Physical attributes of the built environment are analysed with respect to housing layout, pedestrian conditions, shared open spaces, and material performance. These are considered alongside psychological mediators operationalised as community attachment, social bonding, perceived ownership, and connectedness. The results indicate that physical design factors are not directly associated with SoC; instead, they appear to shape everyday socio-spatial practices that operate through psychological pathways, though causal claims require longitudinal validation. Community attachment and social bonding exert stronger direct influences on SoC than housing attributes alone, reframing SoC as a relational, socio-environmental outcome rather than a by-product of housing provision.
