The study advances scholarship on city–environment interaction by examining the potential relevance of everyday spatial experience to SoC within institutional arrangements shaping climate-resettlement, while underscoring the need to integrate pedestrian networks, shared spaces, and participatory management into resettlement policy to support sustainable community formation in secondary cities.

items.title: Holey Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanofiltration Membranes: Microstructure–Transport Relations and Enhanced Fractionation of Complex Streams
items.abstract: Abstract Membranes based on two-dimensional nanomaterials such as graphene oxide (GO) and reduced GO (rGO) are increasingly investigated for nanofiltration applications involving complex biomass-derived streams. However, GO membrane performance is limited by extended transport pathways and restricted flux arising from the tortuous alignment of impermeable nanosheets. We report a systematic study of reduced “holey” graphene oxide (rhGO) membranes, fabricated by controlled oxidative etching of GO nanosheets, to investigate the effect of in-plane nanopores on water and solute transport. Membranes with varying degrees of hole sizes and densities, as well as two distinct film thicknesses (70 and 130 nm), were evaluated systematically for pure water permeation and rejection of ionized and neutral solutes. Concurrently, the microstructural features of the nanoflakes and membranes (hole size distribution, flake size distribution) were characterized quantitatively with extensive AFM and TEM statistical measurements. The membrane permeation and microstructural data allowed the parametrization and validation of an extended transport model that allows the prediction of flux and solute rejection trends that account for the presence of holes in the membranes. Compared to nonholey rGO membrane controls, rhGO membranes demonstrated enhanced water flux and 3-fold increase in throughput during nanofiltration of a complex feedstock (kraft black liquor) while maintaining high lignin rejection (>95%) and similar divalent salt exclusion as nonholey rGO membranes. This study underscores the potential of nanosheet defect engineering as a scalable strategy for tuning microstructure–transport relationships in 2D-material-based membranes for harsh-environment separations.

items.title: GraphAgents: Knowledge Graph-Guided Agentic AI for Cross-Domain Materials Design
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate discovery by reasoning across the ever-expanding landscape of scientific knowledge. Yet, as the reservoir of knowledge grows, the challenge is no longer access to information but rather the ability to connect it in meaningful, domain-spanning ways. In materials science, where discoveries and new hypotheses emerge from bridging insights across disciplines and demand the integration of concepts from molecular chemistry to mechanical performance, this challenge is especially acute. Neither human researchers nor single-agent LLMs can contend with this torrent of information, with the latter often producing brittle reasoning and hallucinations. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a multiagent framework guided by large-scale knowledge graphs to address the urgent challenge of finding sustainable substitutes for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of synthetic chemicals widely used in industrial and consumer applications that are the subject of increasing regulatory scrutiny due to concerns raised in scientific literature and evolving policy efforts to ban certain PFAS compounds. Agents in the framework specialize in problem decomposition, evidence retrieval, design parameter extraction, and graph traversal, uncovering latent connections across distinct pockets of scientific knowledge that support downstream hypothesis generation for PFAS-free materials. Our ablation studies show that the full multiagent pipeline outperforms single-shot prompting, underscoring the value of distributed specialization and relational reasoning. We show that by tailoring graph traversal strategies, the system can alternate between exploitative searches that focus hypothesis generation on domain-critical outcomes and exploratory searches that surface emergent cross-connections in the broader network. Shown through the exemplar of biomedical tubing, the framework generates sustainable material alternatives to PFAS-based tubing that balance tribological performance, thermal stability, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility. This work establishes a framework that combines knowledge graphs with multiagent reasoning to expand the materials design space and reveal interdisciplinary connections. We showcase several initial PFAS-free design candidates to demonstrate the approach.

items.title: Generative AI adoption and scientific output: Quasi-experimental evidence on heterogeneous changes across 26 disciplines
items.abstract: Using monthly OpenAlex data on 92 million publications across 26 academic fields (2015–2025), we examine publication growth associated with large language model (LLM) adoption through a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences design around ChatGPT’s release. The pooled estimate is statistically indistinguishable from zero. However, fields with one standard deviation higher pre-existing AI intensity show 4.52 percentage points greater output growth per percentage point of measured adoption ( 𝑝 = 0 . 0 1 0 ). Expanded keyword definitions reduce this estimate to 1.21–1.75 percentage points. Computer Science shows an estimated cumulative output increase of 8.7% by late 2025. These findings indicate heterogeneous field-level publication responses, with magnitudes sensitive to how adoption is measured.

items.title: Gap‐Filling Stencil Lithography for Precise and High Yield Patterning of Two‐Dimensional Materials
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional materials (2DMs) are considered revolutionary candidates for manufacturing electronics because of their atomically thin nature and exceptional electrical properties. Lithography is essential for patterning 2DMs and fabricating electronic devices. However, conventional water‐based processes such as photolithography fail to achieve high‐yield production because of 2DM delamination from the substrate. Although non‐water‐based stencil lithography is an alternative, the inherent gap between the mask and substrate causes blurring, obscuring high‐precision definition. In this study, we present gap‐filling stencil lithography (GSL), which introduces a protective layer to eliminate this gap, thereby suppressing blurring and enabling precise patterning for 2DMs. Pattern arrays fabricated through multialignment GSL achieved an exceptional 100% yield, compared to the 79.2% yield obtained through photolithography. GSL was implemented on various 2DMs to validate its universality, demonstrating repeatability by maintaining consistent dimensions after consecutive GSL cycles without mask degradation. Finally, the electrical performance of edge‐contact field‐effect transistors fabricated using GSL was evaluated, which confirms GSL as a practical approach to manufacture electronic devices utilizing 2DM. Consequently, this GSL method is expected to emerge as a promising patterning candidate for 2DM because it can overcome the critical processing vulnerabilities of conventional lithography to ensure high‐yield production.

items.title: Exploring the Value of Diverse LLM Explanations in Introductory Programming
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown the potential to generate code explanations that surpass those of peers in quality, offering promising opportunities for computer science education. While these explanations may not yet match the depth and clarity of instructor-provided explanations, research in computational creativity highlights that the quantity and diversity of ideas can often outweigh a singular focus on quality. Inspired by this, we explore whether combining multiple diverse explanations, each emphasizing distinct aspects (e.g., function, concept, goal), can enhance students' understanding of programming exercises compared to generic explanations that do not emphasize distinct conceptual aspects. In our study 971 first-year computing students were randomly assigned either diverse or generic LLM-generated explanations for two programming exercises. Students completed multiple-choice and open-ended questions for each exercise, followed by Likert-scale questions and open-ended reflections. Our findings outline patterns in student performance and perceived cognitive load across the two explanation conditions. These findings highlight how variation in explanation emphasis may relate to learner engagement and understanding. Across participants, open-ended response accuracy was consistently about 7.7% higher when students received diverse explanations, with no difference in perceived cognitive load.

items.title: Evaluating Prompting Frameworks for Enhancing ChatGPT-Assisted Literature Reviews and Ethical and Pedagogical Implications
items.abstract: Students use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools for academic writing, but there is still little understanding of how students can prompt ChatGPT to write literature reviews, how structured prompting frameworks affect their outputs and what the implications are of such use of GenAI in teaching practices. Prompts and literature reviews written by seven students were collected before and after the introduction of three prompting frameworks (COSTAR, POSE, and Sandwich) and analysed. Following the intervention, students’ prompting became more focused and efficient, although they did not use all the elements of the frameworks, except for Sandwich. While literature review scores improved, approaching near-full marks, they lacked critical thinking and originality. Therefore, more training and understanding of prompting frameworks and fundamental knowledge about literature reviews are still needed. Plagiarism checks demonstrate a reasonable degree of similarity, although recurrent citation mistakes were found. These findings highlight pedagogical and ethical risks associated with GenAI use, which may be mitigated by alternative approaches to evaluating literature reviews that place greater emphasis on paper selection and topic choice. Although the small sample precludes generalisation, this study provides an initial exploration of how prompting frameworks influence GenAI-assisted literature reviews and what the ethical and pedagogical implications are.

items.title: Evaluating AI performance on end-to-end data science projects
items.abstract: Generative AI is used for knowledge work but many current AI evaluations focus on isolated tasks and constituent parts such as writing code, rather than end-to-end workflows. We test whether AI models can generate end-to-end data science projects. This requires AI models to select a dataset, develop a research question, write code to download, clean, and test data, create figures, and write a reproducible paper. To do this we collect 40 real end-to-end data science projects, then grade them according to a rubric. We use these to build an automated grading pipeline that evaluates data science projects and aligns with the grades that human graders give. For each of nine AI models we then generate five projects and use the automated grader to evaluate them. We find the extent to which generative AI models can complete end-to-end data science projects varies considerably by model. Most recent models did well on structured tasks, but there were considerable differences on tasks that needed judgment such as explaining measurement, writing abstracts, and citing sources. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 averaged 87 per cent and OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 averaged 85 per cent, both around the level of an A for an undergraduate. No model was consistently the best across all aspects of the rubric. These findings suggest that while AI models could soon approximate entry-level data scientists on routine tasks, they require consistent verification and evaluation.

items.title: Enabling single-exposure metal logic with high-NA lithography
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of pitch 20 nm (P20) and pitch 18 nm (P18) metal logic designs, including regular tip-to-tip (T2T) and logic structures using bright-field masks in combination with dry metal-oxide resist. Patterning performance is evaluated across multiple source configurations and resist process conditions. For P20 T2T, we demonstrate a ∼13 nm T2T-CD (critical dimension) with local CD uniformity (LCDU) below 3 nm. For P18, single high-NA EUV exposure enables 18 nm T2T-CD with LCDU<3 nm. Further scaling is achieved using a directional etch at resist, reducing T2T-CD to ∼9 nm while maintaining LCDU ∼3 nm in P18 structure. To assess manufacturability, large-area defectivity is investigated using e-beam inspection after etch into hardmask for P20 metal logic structures. These results demonstrate the feasibility of single-patterning approaches for advanced metal logic and support the adoption of High-NA EUV for damascene integration.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: Designing against isolation: urban planning, public space, and social connection at Elizabeth Quay, Perth, Australia
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines how urban design can function as social infrastructure by creating opportunities for co-presence, participation, shared experiences, incidental encounters, repeated public-space use, and activity across different periods of the day. Using Elizabeth Quay in Perth, Australia as a case study, it explores how waterfront redevelopment can move beyond aesthetics to address the growing global challenge of social isolation. Drawing on quantitative observational and spatial analysis based on 10 site visits and 7 observation points, the study examines how key design and planning features such as cross-sector partnerships, mixed-use development, walkability, cultural programming, public art, green and blue infrastructure, and intergenerational activities, shape opportunities for social interaction and the social value of the built environment. The analysis suggests that these elements may contribute to social cohesion, a sense of safety, and more inclusive forms of public life, while also highlighting the importance of built environment. The findings indicate that successful public spaces are defined not only by visual quality, but by their capacity to support physical design and create opportunities for movement, play, physical activity, and informal social interaction. The paper explores how human-centered urban design and placemaking can create conditions that may strengthen civic identity, public health, and community wellbeing while also supporting economic and cultural vitality. The study highlights the potential of the built the environment as preventative social infrastructure, while distinguishing observed spatial and behavioral patterns from broader social outcomes that remain theoretically inferred rather than empirically measured.
items.venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

items.title: Demystify, Use, Reflect, Assess (DURA): An Experience Report on LLM Integration in CS2
items.abstract: In this Experience Report we share our DURA framework (Demystify-Use-Reflect-Assess) and materials we used to restructure our CS2 course to allow the use of LLMs. We first demystified LLMs, then provided guidance on use with required attribution. We also added reflections related to LLM use at three points throughout the semester to encourage student meta-cognition around LLM use. We increased the value of proctored assessments in tandem with allowing retakes and including questions that explicitly assess skills from programming assignments. Students reported using LLMs for clarifying course concepts, debugging, understanding assignment guidelines, and determining test cases, but also still sought assistance via office hours and TAs, monitoring Piazza, and reviewing course content. Students articulated thoughtful and strategic approaches to LLM use and also valued the instructional content and guidance from course staff. Student use of office hours increased slightly this semester and student perceptions that the instructor cares about them and their learning improved.

items.title: Dataset for A Single Volatile VO2 Memristor for Neuromorphic Perception, Learning, and Temporal Signal Processing
items.abstract: This is the dataset for the manuscript "A Single Volatile VO2 Memristor for Neuromorphic Perception, Learning, and Temporal Signal Processing" in Advanced Electronic Materials.

items.title: Complementary Resistive Switching and IMPLY Logic Operations in Single Active Switching Material Standalone Memristive Devices
items.abstract: Complementary resistive switches (CRSs) are promising for nonvolatile memory, logic computing, and in-memory computing, but conventional implementations typically require two anti-serial memristive units, increasing device count and integration complexity. Here, the large surface-to-volume ratio of Ga2O3 nanowires is exploited to generate strong surface depletion effects. Coupled depletion regions between laterally bridged nanowires form an effective back-to-back depletion configuration, enabling complementary resistive switching in a single active switching material standalone memristive device. A Linear Technology Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (LTSpice) model is further developed to reproduce the measured electrical characteristics and verify Implies (IMPLY) logic operations, offering a compact route toward wide-bandgap oxide memristive logic, in-memory computing, and future electronics applications.

items.title: Comparative performance and safety of three large language models in pediatric paracetamol poisoning management
items.abstract: Abstract Background Paracetamol overdose is a common reason for pediatric poisoning consultations and emergency department visits, and. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for clinical decision support, but evidence on pediatric poisoning is scarce. We compared the performance and safety of three contemporary LLMs for managing pediatric paracetamol poisoning using guideline-based simulated scenarios. Methods In this cross-sectional, comparative, scenario-based study, 30 hypothetical pediatric paracetamol poisoning scenarios were presented to ChatGPT 5.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash via their public browser-based interfaces, with a standardized single-turn prompt (90 responses). Blinded to model identity, a three-clinician expert panel scored each response by consensus using a study-specific Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Score for Clinical Poisoning Vignettes (AIES-CPV; range 5–25), an eight-item key-action checklist (0–8), the Global Quality Scale (GQS; 1–5), reference-standard concordance, and the presence of critical safety errors, against a predefined reference algorithm derived primarily from the Australia and New Zealand guidelines. Models were compared using the Friedman test (with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and a Bonferroni correction for pairwise comparisons) and the Cochran Q test for critical error rates. Results than ChatGPT 5.5 and Gemini 3 Flash (Friedman p < 0.001 for all); ChatGPT 5.5 and Gemini 3 Flash did not differ significantly. Claude Sonnet 4.6 produced no critical safety errors and was concordant with the reference standard in all responses, whereas one critical error occurred with ChatGPT 5.5 (1/30) and three with Gemini 3 Flash (3/30); the difference in critical-error rates was not statistically significant (Cochran Q = 4.67, p = 0.097). Conclusions Among three LLMs evaluated on pediatric paracetamol poisoning scenarios, Claude Sonnet 4.6 showed the highest guideline-based accuracy, key-action performance, and overall quality, with no critical safety errors. Contemporary LLMs may serve as adjunctive decision-support tools in pediatric toxicology, but given inter-model safety differences and the risk of confident errors in high-stakes decisions, they should be used only under expert supervision and with clinical verification.

items.title: Commenting with Copilot: A Taxonomy and Multi-Year Analysis of Student Code-Generation Specifications
items.abstract: As AI code tools become integrated into programming environments, students increasingly describe intended behavior in natural language and rely on these tools to generate code, shifting emphasis from code writing to specification. Yet little is known about the comments students write as specifications in AI-assisted programming tasks. We analyze a four-year dataset of undergraduate programming submissions and reflections from tasks in which students wrote comments to guide code generation and refined solutions using test-case feedback. We introduce a taxonomy spanning three dimensions: comment type, code expression level, and code construct. Using automated classification, we examine how these dimensions vary across attempts and how students describe the process in their reflections. Our findings show that students mostly wrote natural-language What comments, shifted toward How comments for more procedural constructs, and focused more on verifying generated code than on repeatedly rewriting comments.

items.title: Collaborative governance and leadership: Community-led models and socio-religio-academic mentoring in countering violent extremism: A comprehensive analysis of the UK model with lessons for Pakistan
items.abstract: This article explores how community-led models are applied to counter violent extremism (CVE), as well as how the Socio-Religio-Academic Mentoring (SRAM) CVE model is applied in the UK. This study examines a unique British model, developed by Dr Toaha Qureshi, where all four elements of community involvement, religious discourse, societal values and academic interventions are combined in a mentoring framework i.e. SRAM to prevent violent extremism. This research uses mixed-methods study techniques including qualitative analysis from CVE programmes in the UK and a quantitative survey of 500 students from different universities across Punjab Province, Pakistan, and offers deep insights into what works and what doesn't when it comes to CVE strategies. The results show that community-led CVE programs are successful in providing higher participation (82%) and higher trust (87%) than government-led programs (52% and 45% respectively). The SRAM model is very effective in increasing educational attainment, employability and the reduction of reoffending. Students in Pakistan are very aware of the causes of extremism (78%) but have low conceptual understanding and moderate interest in the engagement of the students (55%) indicating the need for culturally sensitive approach to CVE teaching.

items.title: Chatgpt Acceptance among Students: An Information Systems Perspective in the Era of Generative
items.abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing university students’ acceptance and use of ChatGPT from an information systems perspective in the context of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). As AI technologies become more common in society, their adoption within higher education has been rapidly increasing․ Students are utilizing tools such as ChatGPT for a variety of purposes, including information retrieval, writing support, and comprehension of complex academic topics․ Despite their educational potential, concerns about academic integrity, accuracy, and their effect on students' critical thinking have been raised. This study adopts a quantitative approach using a survey method to collect data from 650 undergraduate students of the Faculty of Management Studies and Commerce at the University of Jaffna (UOJ), Sri Lanka․ This study is based on information systems success theory and technology acceptance model․ This model depicts the impact of information quality, system quality, service quality, trust in service and self-confidence on system use, user satisfaction, and student achievability, as well as the effect of on student perceived benefits․ In order to test the relationships above, the data was analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach via the SmartPLS software․ Furthermore, system quality, service quality, trust, and self-confidence significantly influence user satisfaction and system use. Student achievability and user satisfaction were found to have a strong positive impact on perceived student benefits․ However, information quality did not significantly influence system use, satisfaction, or achievability. Overall, the findings underscore the importance of both technological and psychological factors in shaping students' experiences and attitudes towards generative AI tools, providing valuable insights for educators and institutions interested in utilizing these technologies responsibly and effectively in higher education contexts․
items.venue: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance

items.title: Charge‐Trapping Multilayer Electrets for Partial Discharge Mitigated AlN Substrates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High electric fields within power devices can trigger partial discharge (PD), which can gradually degrade insulation materials, such as ceramic substrates and encapsulation compounds. This work counters and reduces electric fields using multilayer thin‐film electret structures incorporating , , , and AlN to mitigate PD in WBG power electronic packages. The proposed thin film structures can be conductively charged, allowing charges to be injected and trapped within the thin film stack. The stored charges generate electric fields and reduce intensified local fields that cause PD. The proposed electret design allows in‐situ conductive charging, unlike previous electrets that required pre‐charging through an external charging system. To evaluate the electric field suppression capabilities, PD measurements were performed under steep (high‐dV/dt), high‐voltage pulse excitations. The results show a decrease in PD activity, indicating a successful electric field reduction. Finite‐element simulation of the measured structure shows that the retained charge reduces the field at the triple point by about 32, and the measured apparent charge decreases in almost all conditions above the inception voltage. Overall, the proposed approach provides a promising way to improve insulation performance in high‐voltage WBG power modules.

items.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
items.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Biologically inspired neuromorphic algorithms for low power learning
items.abstract: While neuromorphic computing offers a potential low power alternative to current resource-hungry AI, it requires fresh algorithmic approaches. The field needs a new generation of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that have not evolved with conventional hardware but instead align with characteristics of nascent neuromorphic platforms. With this goal in mind, we research biologically inspired networks that expand by incorporating fresh neurons to facilitate continual learning. This architectural plasticity is largely overlooked as a technique in conventional machine learning and is inspired by biological adult neurogenesis. To underpin our research, we provide a unifying definition and mathematical formulation for a group of associative memory networks that expand during learning. Our formulation enables theoretical network optimisation which demonstrates greater than 10,000 times improvement in memory capacity compared to previous work. We then direct our focus on the learning step itself and propose several new neurogenesis learning strategies that increase in memory recall accuracy from 69% to 96%, while retaining a fixed resource budget. Furthermore, through application of our findings to the more complex task of Class Incremental Learning (CIL), we are able demonstrate that dedicating separate resources to the independent learning of each class can help to regulate learning. Our consolidated findings include: methods to increase accuracy by reducing bias towards specific memories during learning; methods to reduce the computational cost of architectural plasticity during learning; and empirical demonstration that a modular network topology can be exploited to optimise neurogenesis. In summary, we extend existing neuromorphic research through the formal articulation, assessment, and advancement of learning strategies that incorporate architectural plasticity. The research responds directly to calls from the neuromorphic research community for original approaches to progress neuromorphic algorithm development.

items.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research Trends on Simulation Studies of AlGaN/GaN High-Electron-Mobility Transistors Using the Scopus Database
items.abstract: Abstract As the design space of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) grows increasingly complex, simulation has become an indispensable tool for understanding device physics and optimizing performance before fabrication. However, few studies have measured and analyzed the scientific publications on AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation from a global perspective. In this bibliometric study, our aim was to evaluate the global research trends in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation areas based on publication outputs, co-authorships among countries, and co-occurrences of author keywords. Using the Scopus database, a total of 4,492 journal articles and conference papers published between 1997 and 2026 were retrieved and analyzed using VOSviewer. Results have shown that since 2001, the number of publications has increased steadily, with the highest annual output recorded in 2025 (490 articles), resulting in a steady increase in the cumulative total publications. China (1,284 articles) and India (961 articles) are the leading contributors, followed by the USA (695 articles); however, Belgium, the UAE, and Singapore exhibit the highest rates of international collaboration. A keyword co-occurrence analysis of 61 keywords revealed six distinct thematic clusters, dominated by power/thermal management, device/HEMT core, modeling/RF, TCAD/gate, electric field, and machine learning. The most recently active keywords include TCAD simulation, gate leakage current, power amplifier, and S-parameter, suggesting a growing emphasis on simulation-driven design and RF performance in recent years. In conclusion, recent progress in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation research includes the following (but not limited to): (i) integration of advanced TCAD and physics-based models for trap dynamics and self-heating; (ii) AI-driven and machine learning approaches for device modeling; and (iii) continued exploration of p-GaN gate and enhancement-mode structures for high-power and high-frequency applications.

items.title: Beyond Two Queries: A Sharp Robustness Constant and a Three-Query Qubit–Qutrit Separation for Centrally Symmetric Quantum Correlations
items.abstract: Companion to the preprint “A Qubit–Qutrit Equivalence for Centrally Symmetric Two-Query Quantum Correlations” (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24093433), which proved that for two fixed binary measurements without shared randomness, a qutrit is never better than a qubit at reproducing centrally symmetric target tables. This note settles two questions left open there. Approximately symmetric targets (two queries). If a qutrit fits a table with worst-cell error ε₃, a sharp qubit pair fits it with error at most ε₃ + δ/2, where δ measures the asymmetry of the table. The constant is proved to be best possible. Three queries. The equivalence fails. Every qubit triple of binary measurements satisfies a simple inequality I ≤ 9, which follows from an identity on 3×3 correlation matrices. A triple of projective qutrit measurements reproduces an eight-point centrally symmetric table exactly with I ≥ 9.0505, so every qubit needs worst-cell error larger than 9.7×10⁻⁴ on it. This is a computer-assisted proof based on exact rational certificates, checked by two independent programs. The qutrit advantage is small: about 10⁻³ in worst-cell error. Numerically, the best qutrit value found is I* = 9.0507284088558548…. A candidate minimal polynomial of degree 13 is reported, confirmed to 3000 digits. Its symbolic derivation and the global optimality of I* remain open, and are labelled as numerical findings. Files: the preprint (PDF), and a reproducibility archive (ZIP) with all exact certificates, the original scripts, an independent audit, the full research record including failed and superseded runs, and a SHA-256 manifest. Quick check after unpacking: python3 -I audit/verify_certificates.py . (pure Python, about 1 s). Not peer reviewed. A large language model assisted with derivations, computations, certificate scripts and drafting; the author takes full responsibility for the content.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Beyond Qubit Count: A Comparative Review of Quantum Chip Architectures, Error Correction, and the Path to Fault-Tolerant Computing
items.abstract: Quantum processors are often compared by the number of physical qubits they contain. That number, however, does not by itself indicate whether a processor can execute a useful computation reliably. Qubit coherence, gate and measurement fidelity, connectivity, control infrastructure, fabrication yield, and the overhead of quantum error correction all influence practical capability. This paper presents a structured comparative review of six major quantum-computing modalities: superconducting circuits, trapped ions, photonic systems, silicon-spin qubits, neutral atoms, and topological approaches. It examines their physical implementations, operational strengths, engineering constraints, and prospects for scaling. Particular attention is given to surface-code error correction and the 105-qubit Willow processor result reported by Google Quantum AI, which demonstrated below-threshold surface-code memory and a logical-error suppression factor of 2.14 ± 0.02 when code distance increased by two. The paper also considers cryogenic control, wiring, modular interconnects, fabrication variability, real-time decoding, and the Indian National Quantum Mission. The review finds that progress towards fault tolerance is best assessed through logical performance and system-level engineering rather than physical-qubit count alone. No modality currently removes the need to address scaling overhead, reliable operations, and application-level advantage
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

items.title: BF-IMNA: A Bit Fluid In-Memory Neural Architecture for Neural Network Acceleration
items.abstract: Mixed-precision quantization, which assigns precisions per-layer, per-network, per-channel, or per-parameter, is gaining traction for efficient Neural Network (NN) realization with higher throughput and lower energy. Unlike conventional fixed-precision accelerators, BF-IMNA advances the mixed-precision design space through an AP-based in-memory implementation. We present BF-IMNA, a bit fluid IMC accelerator for end-to-end Convolutional NN inference supporting static and dynamic mixed-precision without run-time reconfiguration overhead. At its heart are Associative Processors (APs), bit-serial word-parallel SIMD-like engines. We evaluate ImageNet inference with AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 across SRAM and ReRAM CAM cells, mixed-precision configurations, and supply voltages. To demonstrate bit fluidity, we apply HAWQ-V3's published ResNet18 schedules to the BF-IMNA cost model and pair them with HAWQ-V3's published accuracies and model sizes. The results reveal an accuracy–Energy-Delay Product trade-off. The high-latency point is \(1.16\) points below INT8 accuracy with \(1.13\times\) better EDP, while the low-latency point has \(1.91\times\) better EDP and a \(45.5\%\) smaller model at a \(3.00\) -point accuracy reduction. At 500-MHz, true-batch-one comparison, BitFusion provides lower absolute energy and latency, while BF-IMNA provides lower average power at all five operating points, \(2106\times\) greater on-chip weight capacity ( \(32.8\times\) per unit modeled area), and larger relative energy reductions at aggressive INT4 and low-latency HAWQ points.
items.venue: ACM Journal on Emerging Technologies in Computing Systems

items.title: BCAT: A Block Causal Transformer for PDE Foundation Models for Fluid Dynamics
items.abstract: Background: Foundation models have demonstrated remarkable generalization in vision and language, but their accurate use for scientific computing remains challenging. For two-dimensional fluid-dynamics prediction, current transformer-based models are often hindered by limited context and rigid causality information, as they typically map fixed windows to the next step. Objectives: We aim to develop a unified architecture for heterogeneous fluid-dynamics families. The goal is to better capture the complex spatio-temporal dependencies inherent in nonlinear fluid dynamics. Methods: We introduce BCAT, a block-causal transformer for autoregressive prediction of two-dimensional fluid-dynamics solutions. Our approach adapts block-causal attention to next-frame prediction, leveraging previous frames as contextual priors. The model is trained on 69K trajectory sequences from PDEBench, PDEArena, and CFDBench using the Muon optimizer. Results: BCAT achieved an average relative 𝐿 2 error of 1.18% across the six evaluated fluid families, reducing error by 45% relative to a 3.4-times-larger baseline. In ablations, next-frame prediction was 3.5x more accurate than the corresponding nexttoken variant. A five-seed analysis, noisy-input stress test, long-rollout analysis, and physics diagnostics further characterize the model. Conclusions: The block-causal framework captures spatial interactions within frames while enforcing temporal causality across frames. BCAT provides an accurate and computationally efficient model for the two-dimensional fluid-dynamics benchmarks considered here.

items.title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry with Emulated Double-Precision Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
items.abstract: The evaluation of exact exchange and the treatment of electron correlation remain major computational challenges in electronic-structure theory. Over the past decade, GPU computing has substantially accelerated these calculations, extending the scale and complexity of electronic-structure problems that can be addressed computationally. More recently, GPU architectures developed to meet the demands of artificial intelligence have introduced new opportunities for acceleration, with Tensor Cores providing reduced-precision arithmetic throughput far exceeding that of native double-precision (FP64) operations. Exploiting this performance advantage while preserving the numerical accuracy required in quantum chemistry remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate the Ozaki-I and Ozaki-II floating-point emulation schemes in the RI-HF, RI-MP2, and RI-CCSD implementations of EXESS on NVIDIA GB200 GPUs. We demonstrate that Ozaki-II at 52-bit precision achieves numerical accuracy comparable to native FP64, delivering complete calculation speedups of up to 1.26× (cc-pVDZ) and 1.50× (cc-pVTZ) for RI-HF, 2.55× and 3.01× for RI-MP2, and 3.11× and 2.15× for RI-CCSD. The energy to solution improves by 1.22× and 2.21× for the representative RI-HF and RI-MP2 cc- pVTZ calculations and by 2.37× for the RI- CCSD cc-pVDZ calculation. Reducing the precision to 47 bits provides further acceleration while maintaining total energy deviations below 0.1 kcal mol -1 across all systems examined.

items.title: AI-Assistant Thermal Hotspot Prediction and Chip Placement Optimization for Semiconductor Packages
items.abstract: Semiconductor packages are becoming more complex due to the increasing integration of multiple chips and chiplets within a single package. This can lead to higher heat generation and uneven temperature distribution, resulting in the formation of thermal hotspots. Excessive temperature can affect the performance and reliability of semiconductor devices. Conventional thermal analysis methods generally require repeated simulations to evaluate different chip placement arrangements, which can increase the time and computational effort. This project proposes an AI-based thermal hotspot prediction and chip placement optimization system for semiconductor packages. The proposed approach uses HotSpot thermal simulation to generate temperature data for different chip placement configurations. The generated dataset is processed using Python or MATLAB and used to train a Machine Learning model. The trained model predicts the maximum temperature and identifies possible thermal hotspot regions for different placement arrangements. Based on the predicted temperature, suitable chip placement configurations are selected and validated using HotSpot simulation. The proposed system aims to reduce the effort required for evaluating multiple placement configurations and support improved thermal-aware chip placement
authors: Prathiksha P, Shamini Genisia D, Dhecika M
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.title: AI ethics by design: implementing customizable guardrails for responsible AI development
items.abstract: This paper explores the development of an ethical guardrail framework for AI systems, emphasizing the importance of customizable guardrails that align with diverse user values and underlying ethics. We address the challenges of AI ethics by proposing a structure that integrates rules, policies, and AI assistants to ensure responsible AI behavior, while comparing the proposed framework to the existing state-of-the-art guardrails. By focusing on practical mechanisms for implementing ethical standards, we aim to enhance transparency, user autonomy, and continuous improvement in AI systems. Our approach accommodates ethical pluralism, offering a flexible and adaptable solution for the evolving landscape of AI governance. The paper concludes with strategies for resolving conflicts between ethical directives, underscoring the present and future need for robust, nuanced and context-aware AI systems.

items.title: AI Agents and Agentic AI in Medicine: An Autonomy-Centred Scoping Review and Research Agenda
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence agents—software systems that perceive, reason, plan and act over multiple steps with limited human intervention—are moving from research prototypes towards clinical deployment. Recent reviews map what has been built; this one asks what would have to hold for such systems to be deployed safely. We conducted a scoping review reported according to the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews, searching eight bibliographic sources from January 2017 to June 2026, admitting foundational computer science and regulatory literature alongside clinical applications. Five architectural paradigms recur—tool-augmented large language model agents, multi-agent systems, offline reinforcement learning agents, embodied robotic agents and autonomous monitoring agents—nearly all sharing a common four-layer stack. We introduce a six-level scale of clinical agent autonomy that grades systems by where human judgement enters relative to the reasoning, and by whether the resulting action remains reversible. The scale exposes an inversion in the evidence base: demonstrated patient benefit concentrates at high autonomy in narrow, bounded domains, whereas research effort concentrates at intermediate autonomy, where prospective outcome evidence is absent and automation bias is the dominant risk. We further propose seven evaluation dimensions specific to agency, a mapping of evaluation requirements to autonomy level, and a ten-item failure mode taxonomy assigned to the architectural layer at which each is addressable. Deploying agentic systems safely requires prospective multi-site validation, reporting standards adapted to agency, equity-aware design, and regulatory obligations indexed to autonomy rather than algorithm class. We conclude with an eight-point research agenda.

items.title: ADAPTATION AND EVALUATION OF THE MEMBRAIN SYSTEM FOR PROFILE-GUIDED DATA PLACEMENT ON INTEL XEON MAX PROCESSORS
items.abstract: We investigate the efficient utilization of tiered HBM and DDR memory on Intel Xeon Max processors under constrained high-bandwidth memory capacity. Unlike conventional capacity-expansion architectures (DRAM + CXL/NVM), tiered memory management with an integrated HBM tier remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we adapt the MemBrain automated profile-guided data placement framework for Intel Xeon Max servers: implementing interprocedural allocation-site function cloning in the LLVM compiler, hardware monitoring of last-level cache misses via PEBS, and guided user-space memory placement via the Intel UMF library. We study data placement optimization strategies based on an exact combinatorial optimization model (knapsack problem) and heuristic selection algorithms. Experimental evaluation on the LULESH 2.0 and Graph500-BFS benchmarks demonstrates that profile-guided data placement achieves up to 98.4%–99.9% of pure HBM performance while utilizing only a fraction of its physical capacity.

items.title: A manually curated resource of PD-L1 regulatory mechanisms in cancer cells with AI-assisted biocuration benchmarking
items.abstract: This repository contains a manually curated dataset of 985 experimentally supported PD-L1 (CD274) regulatory interactions from 362 primary research articles involving cancer cells. The dataset captures regulatory relationships, intermediate regulators, protein complexes, and PD-L1 molecular target forms. It also provides materials used to benchmark three AI research tools (Claude, ChatGPT, and Elicit), including study retrieval results, prompts, expert feedback, edge extraction outputs, and evaluation results.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A Tool to Map AI Programs in the U.S.: A Snapshot from April 2026 and an Analysis of Requirements for AI Majors and Minors
items.abstract: In this work, we locate and analyze existing undergraduate Artificial Intelligence (AI) programs in the United States in Spring 2026, creating a historic record at a time of great change in this area. To create this record, we developed a tool to detect, scrape, and display data from 361 undergraduate AI programs--majors, minors, concentrations, and certificates--at 4-year universities. Our tool, available at https://cicmap.ai, searched 563 institutions to locate these programs, a sample that represents 87% of all undergraduate Computer Science (CS) graduates in the U.S in 2025. This tool allows prospective students, guidance counselors, administrators, and faculty to easily access AI program requirements and is designed to continually update as new programs emerge. To the best of our knowledge, this survey represents the most comprehensive snapshot of the state of AI programs in the U.S. to date. With this work we offer three important contributions: 1) a record of AI programs in the U.S. at a time of great upheaval; 2) a tool to explore AI programs and their requirements; and 3) an analysis of the courses required for 66 AI majors and 87 AI minors. Our analysis of majors and minors shows great variability in the size and the requirements of these degrees, but we note two takeaways. First, not all majors require a general AI course, but if they don't, they do require a Machine Learning (ML) course. Second, more than a third of majors require an Ethics in AI course but only 24% of minors do.

items.title: A Scalable 5 kW Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) Source for Next-Generation EUV Lithography: Design, Thermal Management, and Spectral Purity Analysis
items.abstract: The semiconductor industry's reliance on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is currently bottlenecked by the Laser-Produced Plasma (LPP) source, which suffers from low conversion efficiency (CE~5%), tin debris, and massive power consumption (>1 MW). In this paper, we propose a scaled-up Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) source as a possible alternative. By scaling a laboratory microwave-discharge approach to a 5 kW microwave input, we outline a design that delivers between about 5 W and 110 W of in-band EUV power, depending on a conversion efficiency (0.5% to 10%) that is not yet verified for xenon. We address the main engineering bottlenecks of MDPP through three solutions: (1) a water-cooled aluminium nitride (AlN) capillary, transparent to microwaves, to manage a 4,500 W thermal load, (2) magnetic confinement and a magnetic nozzle to shrink the emitting column and reach a geometric etendue of about 1.0 mm²·sr, and (3) a Zr filter and two Mo/Si mirrors that reach a spectral purity above 99.99% under stated assumptions. A source-to-machine analysis shows that, for a 20 W target at the intermediate focus, a 5 kW source needs a conversion efficiency of at least about 3.6% with hemispherical collection, and about 81% with the closed end-on capillary, so the source geometry must be chosen from the optics requirement. Our calculations also expose open problems: the plasma density needed for efficient 13.5 nm emission is far above what a 100 mTorr, 2.45 GHz discharge is known to reach, and the Zr filter and the collection geometry limit the usable power. The design is therefore a concept for further modeling and experiment, not a demonstrated source.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A Centrifuge-Free Method for Cell Culture Passaging and Collection Compatible with Automated Liquid Handling Systems: A Conceptual Methodology Framework
items.abstract: Standard cell culture passaging and collection workflows predominantly rely on centrifugation to pellet cells and replace liquid media. While effective, centrifugation introduces severe mechanical complexity, high hardware costs, and severe integration bottlenecks within automated liquid handling workstations. This paper introduces a conceptual, centrifuge-free methodology that replaces conventional centrifugal sedimentation with controlled size-exclusion filtration using standard syringes and syringe-mounted porous membranes. By standardizing a multi-step fluidic workflow—from cell dissociation, aspiration, and gentle membrane filtration to filter removal and replating—this approach provides an elegant solution for closed-system, low-shear cell handling. Furthermore, we outline its architectural compatibility with high-throughput laboratory automation (such as the Hamilton Microlab STAR platform), eliminating the need for robotic centrifuge integration, automated doors, and complex plate-balancing mechanisms. This conceptual framework establishes a streamlined foundation for future automated cell culture engineering.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A 1.25‐GS/s SAR ADC With Scalable Input and 3–6‐Bit Reconfigurable Resolution for Operation Unit‐Based RRAM–CIM Architectures
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The operation unit (OU)‐based architecture is widely adopted in resistive random access memory‐based compute‐in‐memory (RRAM–CIM) macros. As the OU size may vary across different designs and under different workloads, the resolution‐reconfigurable analog‐to‐digital converters (ADCs) are required for better energy efficiency. To this end, this paper presents a 3–6‐bits reconfigurable asynchronous successive approximation register (SAR) ADC with an input‐scalable architecture. The proposed design supports resolution reconfiguration by scaling the bitline current that charges the sampling capacity dynamically according to the required computing resolution. Moreover, we utilize the upper‐plate sampling method to reduce settling time during the most significant bit phase and introduce an asynchronous control scheme combined with a high‐speed dynamic comparator to enable a short decision period. The proposed single‐channel SAR ADC is designed with a 28‐nm process, achieving 1.25‐GS/s sampling rate at 1‐V supply with only 0.85‐mW power consumption. Compared to the fixed‐resolution ADC, the proposed design achieves 13%–43% power savings by reducing comparison cycles and enabling early termination.
items.venue: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications

items.title: SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20$μ$s, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering. We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.abstract: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.abstract: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.abstract: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.abstract: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

items.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.abstract: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. In particular, for all three properties, TabPFN applied to Chemprop's own embedding is more accurate than Chemprop's predictions. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying "both are bad" rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model's share of decisive votes is flat. The rise holds within the same voter and on the same pair, and across arrival cohorts from their first recorded vote. It holds with prompt controls, in every major language, for dated vendor snapshots, open-weight models and models with stable answer length, and between interface changes. The drift is shared across models: month effects estimated from other models' pairs remove it from each model's own pairs. Platform-wide, the average model would be expected to score 78% against the 2023 average, yet the share of "both are bad" votes ended near where it began. The pattern fits a standard that follows the category's progress, so a product that stands still is judged as declining. Absolute verdicts on AI drifted while relative comparisons held steady, an evaluation drift that matters for LLM leaderboards and for the human feedback used to train models.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.abstract: Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale. Performance simulation offers a lower cost alternative, yet controlled comparisons among existing simulators remain difficult because they differ in the training stages they model and the workloads on which they are evaluated. We introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators. The framework decomposes simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule level aggregation, connecting execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets. Following this framework, we profile 23 model settings from 10 dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM families on an Ascend Neural Processing Unit (NPU) cluster. The resulting dataset contains 348 feasible configurations that jointly vary five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation, with six views spanning configuration, rank, operator, event, and kernel granularity. Evaluations of representative training simulators demonstrate how LM-SimBench supports comparisons of prediction accuracy, assessment of configuration selection, and diagnosis of prediction errors. Matched GPU-NPU experiments validate the cross-platform applicability of the collection and evaluation protocol and demonstrate NPU-guided GPU configuration selection.

items.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
items.abstract: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained Knowledge Graph (CKG) generated automatically from asset-specific reference documentation. CoP addresses failure-sensor association from textual engineering knowledge. The CKG stores diagnostic chains connecting failure modes, changes in physical quantities, and monitoring sensors. During inference, semantically similar graph paths are retrieved for each question and used as both information and in-context examples for the reasoning process. Candidate failure modes are extracted from the question and analysed independently through dedicated LLM calls, which generate plausible failure-to-observation chains. A final decision module compares these chains with the available answer choices. CoP is evaluated on the FailureSensorIQ benchmark across four industrial asset classes and three LLMs. Compared with direct prompting and conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CoP improves diagnostic accuracy across all evaluated models, with gains ranging from 7.8 to 19.6 percentage points and from 11.7 to 18.2 percentage points, respectively. The results show that structured engineering knowledge can improve LLM-based diagnostic reasoning when graph retrieval is combined with in-context examples of fault propagation.

items.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
items.abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a reserved Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value declaring agent traffic, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration to a class served after best-effort traffic, and a rate-limited priority queue. VATC was compared with static Differentiated Services (DiffServ), a dedicated class that trusts the marking, and fq_codel, a per-flow fair-queuing scheduler, in two simulators and on a real Linux kernel. VATC matched DiffServ under steady load. In a constructed burst it cut mean agent queuing delay by 98% relative to DiffServ in simulation (assuming an immediate verdict), at a 12% increase in human delay; most of the gain came from the separate class. Under a spoofed flood in the kernel, the rate limit held human latency 11 times below DiffServ's. Without verification, DiffServ and a tightly configured fq_codel gave legitimate agents lower latency than VATC; a live four-feature classifier then demoted all 20 bulk-shaped spoofers and gave agents 0.30 ms, but missed six spoofers that copied the agent pattern. With emulated network delay, a timing feature of the classifier stopped separating agent from human flows. In real agent harnesses on a congested link, router queueing took 13% to 63% of task time, depending on harness and assumed model latency. The traffic was synthetic or sandbox-scale.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.abstract: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). Error analysis reveals that Qwen failures reflect derivation errors within formatted responses (conditional accuracy drop of $-11.4$ pp), whereas in LLaMA $22.2\%$ of discordant losses lack a final answer format line (conditional gap narrows to $-5.0$ pp). These findings demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are particularly vulnerable to concentrated structural disruptions, providing empirical benchmarks for fault tolerance in transformer architectures.

items.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model
items.abstract: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. HaiRuo pairs two components with a clear division of labour: (1) HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global satellite-altimetry observations, which supplies the 15-day physical fields and masks (+0.14 field skill and +1.1 mIoU points under the same decoder) and further lowers 15-day centre error by 1.2 km frozen (1.35 km over training from scratch); and (2) XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that samples the evolving forecast in each eddy's co-moving polar frame and refines the 15-day path across three look-ahead rounds, removing 2.5 km on HaiRuo-1B (2.9 km with joint fine-tuning) and 2.5-3.3 km via its object attention across six published backbones. Under one pre-registered global evaluation over the whole ocean, HaiRuo improves on fourteen methods on every endpoint (25.2 vs. 30.6 km 15-day centre error, -18%), holding its margin outside the labelled regions and through both phases of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), while reproducing westward drift, 50-60 deg S eastward reversal and poleward cyclone-anticyclone deflection. Over ten days through one fixed tracker, HaiRuo's forecast field cuts the eddy-centre error of WenHai and XiHe by 37-43% (-2.8 km vs. day 0 while they degrade +4.3-8.7 km), and its object trajectories cut pipeline error by 77-78% globally. Open-weight checkpoints, code and project page: https://github.com/xkqin/HaiRuo

items.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
items.abstract: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening. The prover streams the model layer by layer on one GPU. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, Sable proves all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B in 92.5 s for 4,096 tokens and 398 s for 16,384 tokens, and covers Qwen3-32B and the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-30B-A3B (4,096 tokens in 121.8 and 84.7 s). A proof costs 41 to 50 times the serving time, or 6.4 cents per 4,096-token request at public GPU prices, and 40 to 64 times less time per parameter and token than zkLLM. On WikiText-2, F_O's greedy token matches the BF16 model's at 86.3% of positions; on Qwen3, F_O is within 1.6 points of BF16 on MMLU and 1.7 points on GSM8K. A verifier with a compiled core checks a proof on one CPU core in 19 to 56 s. In the random-oracle model, the interactive proof has round-by-round soundness error 2^-103. The proof is not zero-knowledge, so the system targets open-weight models. Code: https://github.com/moonmath-ai/Sable

items.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
items.abstract: Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to''. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails.
