We argue that positionality -- the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said -- is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? Against the vendors' answer of nowhere and the seductive possibility of everywhere, we argue that when a model is taken as-if speaking, it speaks from somewhere, and this means positionality can describe models, and the way they are believed beyond their warrant, even though they are not accountable speakers. A model's positionality is laminar -- laid down across corpus, tuning, system prompt, application and the live conversation. We separate three sets of factors: the positionality of a model's creators, the behaviour they intend for it, and the behaviour it enacts, and situate current work within this matrix. This lets us highlight what each stratum inherits from the one below, with ruptures and collapses where that inheritance is disavowed. We then return to where models speak from, and discuss the implications for how models are made, read and held accountable.

items.title: MISO-BR: An Open Corpus for Misogyny Detection in Brazilian Portuguese
items.abstract: Misogyny is among the most prevalent forms of online hate speech directed at Brazilian users, yet open and auditable resources dedicated to it in Brazilian Portuguese remain scarce. We introduce MISO-BR, an open, documented and versioned corpus of 896 balanced social media texts annotated for binary misogyny, released with its construction protocol and reproducible baselines. The corpus combines lexicon- and target-guided scraping from X with items imported from OLID-BR, a large language model triage stage whose prompt and decoding parameters are released, and manual annotation by three annotators following a written guide. Inter-annotator reliability reaches a Fleiss' kappa of 0.788 over 816 items. Under a single fixed protocol we compare four classical classifiers (Multinomial and Bernoulli Naive Bayes, a linear SVM and a random forest) with fine-tuned BERTimbau Base and Large. The classical models cluster between 0.651 and 0.676 macro-F1 and are precision-oriented but recall-poor. The transformers reach 0.833 macro-F1 and accuracy (Wilson 95% CI for accuracy [0.77, 0.88]), a gap of roughly 16 points, while Base and Large are indistinguishable on the test set despite a 2.6x difference in training cost. We argue that the value of the resource lies less in its headline scores than in the auditability of its pipeline, and we state three limits that users must reckon with: the artificial class balance, whose effect on precision under realistic prevalence we quantify; the association between provenance and label, which the released source field makes measurable; and the selection bias induced by lexicon-guided sampling and automatic triage. The corpus, annotation guide, models and experimental scripts are publicly available.

items.title: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents
items.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous builders of biomedical models, but existing benchmarks are small, near saturation or open to leaked information. We present BioXArena-Pro, 64 research-level modelling tasks from eight biomedical domains, each rebuilt from a published study; most hold out whole biological units such as species or cohorts. Across 22 agent configurations, the best scores 55.1 of 100, and the scaffold matters almost as much as the model. We re-ran a published method for every task: where the published recipe applies unchanged, the best agent and the methods tie; on rebuilt tasks the methods trail by 8.2 points, suggesting that agents gain by adapting to new data. Pretrained models (including biological foundation models) matter where the strongest agent uses them: forbidding them decreases its score on those tasks by 9 points. Every task was audited in several AI-assisted rounds and a final human review.

items.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
items.abstract: Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

items.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
items.abstract: Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reasoning on later segments. To address these limitations, we propose TreeAgent, a structure-aware agent that uses the input hierarchy to guide both segment-wise context processing and access to past information. Specifically, TreeAgent constructs segments from complete subtrees and groups of adjacent sibling subtrees to preserve local structural relationships. We provide theoretical guarantees on segment counts to guide token budget selection toward matching the segment count of fixed-length segmentation. We further attach structural paths to the segments for the agent to identify their ancestors and hierarchical positions. We also introduce residual memory links from the segments of low-level children to the segments of high-level parents, enabling direct information flows beyond successive memory updates. We evaluate TreeAgent with four representative memory agents on eight retrieval and aggregation tasks. The inputs are derived from real-world application data in JSON, HTML, YAML, and JavaScript and range from 8K to 1M tokens. TreeAgent improves the average score across the four datasets for all four agents, with 3.61% performance gain on average.

items.title: TAPCO-G: LLM-Guided Design-Adaptive Timing and Power Co-Optimization with Graph-Based Physical Priors
items.abstract: Post-placement timing and power co-optimization is critical to meeting setup timing targets and reducing power within placement constraints. A cell replacement can improve timing along one path while increasing power or reducing slack on others. Conventional optimizers follow fixed rules for scheduling and accepting repairs, limiting their ability to address design-specific bottlenecks. A large language model (LLM) can propose changes to these rules, but on its own it cannot reliably estimate how a cell replacement affects endpoint slack and power. TAPCO-G combines LLM-guided optimizer adaptation with graph-based physical priors to evaluate candidate cell replacements. The outer loop tunes tool settings using physical-design feedback and revises executable repair policies when tuning stalls. The inner loop anchors delay estimates to static timing analysis snapshots, accounts for upstream driver-load changes, and propagates delay shifts to timing endpoints. It combines these estimates with coarse-to-fine power screening to prioritize candidates for physical trials. TAPCO-G produced placement-legal, logic-equivalent implementations and outscored CERBERUS on all eight ASAP7 benchmarks from the MLCAD 2026 Contest, with a mean quality score gain of 5.516 points, and scored 21.648 points higher than TAPCO on average. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed co-optimization framework.

items.title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
items.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.

items.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
items.abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

items.title: Uncovering the Memory Hierarchy of Modern NVIDIA GPUs for Accurate Simulation
items.abstract: Emerging artificial intelligence workloads, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), place unprecedented demands on GPU memory systems. Consequently, architectural innovations increasingly target the memory system to alleviate these bottlenecks. However, existing works still rely on outdated memory hierarchy models that fail to capture the complexities of modern hardware. This fidelity gap leads to inaccurate characterization and could misguide optimization strategies. To bridge this gap, we present GemAtlas, the first systematic reverse engineering of the memory hierarchy in modern NVIDIA GPUs. By developing fine-grained SASS-level benchmarking, we expose critical, previously undocumented micro-architectural details across different cache levels, including cache set associativity, slice-routing and set-indexing hash functions, replacement policies, coherence behavior, and interconnect topologies. We integrate these discovered micro-architecture details into the state-of-the-art GPU simulation framework. The final results demonstrate that GemAtlas reduces the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 31.69% to 22.24% on average across four GPUs. Specifically, GemAtlas reduces the MAPE from 34.04% to 23.98% for real-world LLM operators.

items.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
items.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

items.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

items.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
items.abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at https://github.com/buraksusam/AutoManifold_NeurIPS2026.

items.title: FedVP: Federated Learning across Heterogeneous Models by Pooling Locally Trained Verifiers
items.abstract: Conventional federated learning relies on the shared model backbone to aggregate client updates, limiting collaboration among institutions that deploy large language models (LLMs) from different families and at different scales. We propose Federated Verifier Pool (FEDVP), a new federated learning paradigm that enables heterogeneous clients to collaborate through shared verification rather than parameter aggregation. Each client trains a verifier using local data and responses generated by its chosen LLM backbone. The server pools these independently trained verifiers and combines their judgments to select answers without merging model parameters. This allows both LLM backbones and verifiers to differ in architecture and size, while keeping the LLM backbones frozen and deriving collaborative gains from improved answer selection. We evaluate FEDVP across five public medical question-answering datasets treated as federated clients, using Qwen and LLaMA backbones ranging from 3B to 14B parameters. FEDVP consistently improves performance across all five clients and outperforms the strongest conventional federated baselines by 1.46-5.79 percentage points in mean accuracy.

items.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
items.abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating and optimizing hardware circuits, ensuring the correctness of AI-generated designs becomes more important. Meanwhile, advances in AI lower the barriers to developing and applying formal methods, creating new opportunities to automate and improve hardware verification. This invited paper presents an overview of the methodologies and applications of hardware formal methods in the AI era. First, we examine how agentic AI advances hardware formal methods across three levels: specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines. Second, we discuss how formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization. We review representative research alongside our recent contributions, highlighting key technical advances and insights from experimental results. Finally, we discuss future research opportunities toward proof-native hardware development, where formal reasoning could become an integral part of autonomous hardware design.

items.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
items.abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).

items.title: Zero-shot performance of a concept-grounded chest radiograph foundation model depends on the evaluation dataset: a preregistered external evaluation of CLEAR and CheXzero
items.abstract: Abstract CLEAR, a concept-grounded vision-language model presented as auditable, scores chest radiographs through 368,294 radiological concepts. It reportedly outperformed CheXzero in zero-shot classification, but only on developer-chosen test sets, without a subgroup analysis or a systematic check of the concepts behind its zero-shot predictions. In a preregistered comparison on the NIH ChestX-ray14 test split (25,592 images, 2,797 patients), macro-AUROC over 14 findings was 0.695 for CheXzero, 0.635 for CLEAR's concept route and 0.700 for direct scoring with CLEAR's encoder. Neither model showed evidence of a sex gap (female minus male: CheXzero + 0.005, 95% CI − 0.015 to + 0.022; concept route − 0.008, − 0.029 to + 0.011) or an age gap under any of four prompt templates. Prompt wording alone reversed the ranking of CLEAR's direct route against CheXzero (− 0.038 to + 0.031). The concept space was nearly collapsed (participation ratio 2.95, against 11.18 for the image features), and one held-out-selected concept outperformed the concept route for every finding. On 15,000 VinDr-CXR radiographs the concept route led CheXzero by 0.057 (0.050 to 0.064), in the reported direction, but by only 0.023 where sex was recorded and 0.009 where age was recorded, the images carrying most of the disease. On the Indiana University collection, one of CLEAR's own test sets, it trailed CheXzero by 0.015 (0.007 to 0.024), using report indexing terms as labels. CLEAR's zero-shot advantage depended on the dataset, and the concept step added no accuracy over the image encoder. Developer-reported zero-shot gains and concept explanations need independent testing before health systems adopt them.

items.title: ZEBRA‐Prop: A Zero‐Shot Embedding‐Based Rapid and Accessible Regression Model for Materials Properties
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit substantial potential across diverse scientific disciplines, including materials science. A property prediction framework, ZEBRA‐Prop (Zero‐Shot Embedding‐Based Rapid and Accessible Regression Model for Materials Properties), is presented here as an extension of LLM‐Prop. In contrast to LLM‐Prop, which requires task‐specific fine‐tuning of the LLM, ZEBRA‐Prop keeps the text encoder frozen and eliminates task‐specific fine‐tuning of the LLM, thereby reducing computational cost and enabling rapid model training. The framework employs MatBERT, a language model pretrained on materials science literature, to enhance predictive capability. Multiple textual embeddings are incorporated through a learnable weighting mechanism, which alleviates the context‐length constraints inherent in LLM‐Prop and facilitates effective integration of diverse textual representations. Evaluation is conducted using two datasets: the TextEdge dataset (~140,000 entries) and an in‐house dataset (~2000 entries) derived from the Materials Project database, with physical properties obtained from first‐principles calculations. The predictive performance of ZEBRA‐Prop is close to that of LLM‐Prop, while the training time is reduced by approximately 95%. The performance improvements are attributable to three principal factors: domain‐specific LLM utilization, diversified textual descriptions, and systematic text preprocessing. ZEBRA‐Prop is a scalable, computationally efficient framework that supports accelerated materials discovery, particularly under limited computational resources.

items.title: Where Correction Stops Paying: Error-Correction Energy for Memory at Fleet Scale
items.abstract: Error-correcting code (ECC) memory costs energy three ways: extra stored bits, patrol scrubbing, and correction logic on every access. This paper prices those costs at fleet scale from published inputs (DRAM soft-error rates from the large-fleet studies of Schroeder et al. 2009, Sridharan et al. 2013/2015 and Meza et al. 2015, which span orders of magnitude; ECC overhead fractions for SECDED (64+8) and a stronger device-correcting code (128+32); DRAM access energy from Horowitz 2014) and prices what correction buys under a plainly stated energy valuation of a prevented crash (1.2e6 J: a 500 W server restarting for 600 s plus re-executing half of a 1 h checkpoint interval, with one uncorrected error in 1e4 taken to cause a crash; silent corruption is assigned no energy value). For a reference fleet of 100,000 servers with 512 GiB each (54.98 PB), SECDED draws a continuous 707759.3 W (6.204 GWh per year), 97.09% of it the background power of the extra stored bits; scrubbing draws 114.53 W and logic 450.0 W. At a representative 25000 FIT per Mbit the fleet corrects 4.2290e-3 errors per joule of ECC energy (236.46 J per correction, against 2.8836e-9 J for the correction act itself) and the avoided crash energy is 0.5075 times the energy spent. SECDED breaks even in energy at 49263.0 FIT per Mbit, at the top of the published range; the stronger code breaks even against SECDED only at 2539132.7 FIT per Mbit, far above any published fleet rate. Conclusion: ECC is not an energy-saving measure at any published error rate; it is a continuous capacity cost paid for correctness. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF and markdown, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Wafer-to-Wafer Bonding-induced Fingerprints and Their Interaction with Optimal Choice of Field Layout for Backside Lithography
items.abstract: Wafer-to-wafer bonding schemes requiring backside lithography absorb bonding-induced distortions into the target wafer, directly affecting the achievable on-product overlay after thinning. While scanner correction models can compensate a large fraction of this distortion content, the influence of litho-graphic field layout on correction efficiency remains insufficiently understood. In this work, experimentally measured (backside-) distortion maps from hydrophilic fusion-bonded wafers with densely distributed alignment markers are used as inputs to large-scale correction-per-exposure (CPE) simulations. More than 6600 virtual field layouts are evaluated using a common six-parameter intra-field correction model. The results show that residual overlay varies by more than a factor of two across the investigated field-layout space despite identical input distortion fields and identical correction methodology. Several geometric descriptors are introduced to quantify the interaction between exposure fields and a localized annular bonding-induced fingerprint. The study demonstrates that field-layout selection constitutes a significant optimization variable for backside lithography. The proposed descriptor framework provides physical insight into the interaction between lithographic exposure fields and bonding-induced distortion fingerprints, and underlines the need for practical guidelines for minimizing residual overlay when low-order field-wise correction models are employed.

items.title: Understanding Advances in Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Over the Past Ten Years: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Abstract Computational Cognitive Neuroscience (CCN) is an interdisciplinary field that uses computational models to understand how the brain gives rise to cognition. Although the field has grown substantially over the past ten years, no review has systematically mapped the major advances achieved during this period. This review therefore aims to map advances in CCN over the past ten years by analyzing the most frequently used computational models, the cognitive domains investigated, and the computational tools employed, and by determining the predominant emphasis of the studies, whether theoretical, translational, or integrated. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the methodology proposed by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and reported following PRISMA-ScR. Searches were performed in PubMed, Embase and IEEE Xplore between 24 and 28 April 2025, and were complemented by a supplementary relevance-ranked Scopus search and by expert-informed identification of additional records. A total of 104 studies were included. Recent progress in CCN was found to be predominantly theoretical, with research focused on memory, learning, language and communication, and decision-making. Recurrent neural networks and Bayesian models emerged as the most widely adopted frameworks. Although CCN has advanced rapidly over the past ten years, the field continues to face critical challenges, notably concerning neurobiological plausibility, model integration, limited external generalizability, and a pressing need for more translational research. Beyond the reviewed corpus, the review discusses emerging AI paradigms, transformers, foundation models, large language models, and neuromorphic computing, as prospective directions informed by complementary literature.

items.title: Tri-Stack-PIM: A Heterogeneous Multi-Die 3D-Integrated Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Efficient LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference during autoregressive decoding is fundamentally memory-bandwidth-bound. Existing three-dimensional (3D) stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures alleviate the off-chip bandwidth wall, yet remain constrained by several limitations: physical layer (PHY), controllers, and direct memory access (DMA) engines compete with arithmetic units for advanced-node base-die area; hybrid-bonding keep-out zones fragment the base-die floorplan and impede physical design; compute tiles built in a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) process are restricted to low logic density, capping achievable throughput; and nonlinear operations offloaded to the host reintroduce a communication bottleneck. We present Tri-Stack-PIM, a heterogeneous three-die architecture that resolves these tensions by dedicating a top DRAM die to storage, a middle buffer die on a mature process node to PHYs, DMA engines, and near-memory compute units, and a bottom base die on an advanced node exclusively to single-instruction-multiple-data (SIMD) multiply-accumulate (MAC) arrays. We further introduce a Unified Buffer-Aware Ready-based (UBAR) hardware out-of-order micro-operation scheduler that enforces cross-die dependency correctness at runtime while maximizing issue-slot utilization through a multi-term priority function, recovering up to 90% of the cycles that an in-order policy would forfeit. A joint architecture-dataflow co-exploration identifies Pareto-optimal configurations that reduce the energy-delay product (EDP) by 33-66x over naive parameter selection. Evaluated across multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention (MHA, GQA, MQA) mechanisms with batch sizes 1-32, Tri-Stack-PIM achieves geometric-mean speedups of 4.95x, 2.57x, and 1.68x across all three attention mechanisms and batch sizes over a graphics processing unit (GPU) baseline, AttAcc, and H2-LLM, respectively.

items.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of Open Challenges, Opportunities and Benchmarks
items.abstract: Frequency-domain analysis has emerged as a powerful paradigm for time series analysis, offering unique advantages over traditional time-domain approaches while introducing new theoretical and practical challenges. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of spectral methods from classical Fourier analysis to modern neural operators, systematically summarizing three open challenges in current research: (1) causal structure preservation during spectral transformations, (2) uncertainty quantification in learned frequency representations, and (3) topology-aware analysis for non-Euclidean data structures. Through rigorous reviewing of over 100 studies, we develop a unified taxonomy that bridges conventional spectral techniques with cutting-edge machine learning approaches, while establishing standardized benchmarks for performance evaluation. Our work identifies key knowledge gaps in the field, particularly in geometric deep learning and quantum-enhanced spectral analysis. The survey offers practitioners a systematic framework for method selection and implementation, while charting promising directions for future research in this rapidly evolving domain.

items.title: Thermodynamic and Infrastructural Implications of Spatial State Computation for Synthetic Intelligence
items.abstract: Thermodynamic and Infrastructural Implications of Spatial State Computation for Synthetic IntelligenceAuthor: David P. Reichwein (Asymmetric Intelligence & Innovation, November 2026) Executive Summary & Core Premise The Energy Wall: Contemporary AI inference relying on dense matrix multiplication (GEMM) over continuous weight tensors faces severe infrastructural limits, driven by high-bandwidth memory (HBM) traffic, long planar interconnects, and facility-scale power demands reaching hundreds of megawatts. Software guardrails add an additional 20% to 100% tax in latency and power without altering the dominant energy terms. The Spatial Substrate Alternative: This paper examines an alternative architecture defined in the AI² corpus: a finite three-dimensional lattice where computation is a field configuration rather than a token string. Architectural Specifications (S₁) The object is defined as S₁ := ⟨ Q_64³, L_codex, Π_PCR, T ⟩, comprising: The Body (Q_64³): A face-centered-cubic parity sublattice consisting of 131,072 sites with a 12-neighbor stencil (||δ||₂ = √2) and a graph diameter of 94 hops. Dual-Bus Registers: Every site carries two distinct registers: a cognitive symbol C(v) typed in Codex-1, and an authorization state E(v) ∈ {⊥, IDLE, COND, ⊤}. The authorization field is monotone non-increasing between exogenous grants, meaning changes in C cannot produce an ascent in E. Language & Clock (L_codex & Π_PCR): Codex-1 is a total, bounded language where every rewrite declares a domain, budget, and effective bound (T_eff). The Permission Control Runtime (Π_PCR) operates with states of DENY, PAUSE, and RUN (where Deny dominates), serving as the sole clock on which any configuration can become an external effect. Thermodynamic Shifts & Structural Implications Primitive Transformation: Replacing dense GEMM with local neighborhood operators under a total language eliminates long-distance data movement in favor of short stencil communication (√2 lattice units). Energy Scale Reduction: Elementary local CMOS transitions on short interconnects dissipate on the order of 10 aJ to 100 fJ, compared to 0.5 pJ to tens of pJ per FLOP for FP16 tensor-core operations with memory traffic. Control Without a Tax: Because authorization lives on the same geometry via a disjoint bus and is evaluated as a meet (unsigned minimum) over a declared domain, supervision does not require a second model inference pass. What is Proved vs. Open (Track E) Proved (Structural Safety): Structural safety results (such as finite body bounds, deny-dominance, non-autonomous recovery, and the separation of cognitive and authorization registers) hold independently on ordinary binary CMOS using a two-bit encoding per site; a native quaternary device (Quadzistor™) is an optional implementation rather than a prerequisite. Open Measurement Obligations (Track E): The paper explicitly notes that no numerical equivalence between one lattice sweep and one transformer token has been established yet. Order-of-magnitude performance claims or representation capacities remain open measurement obligations until empirical mapping of Codex-1 terms to field regions is completed. Pattern > Noise Hardware > Hope Fail-safe is not a feature. It is our duty.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Thermal annealing-induced charge storage enhancement in WO3/β-Ga2O3 nanowire heterostructures for MOS capacitive memory
items.abstract: This paper examines non-volatile metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) capacitive memory based on WO3/β-Ga2O3 heterostructure nanowire arrays. The WO3/β-Ga2O3 vertical oriented axial heterostructure nanowires (VAHNWs) were synthesized using glancing angle deposition (GLAD) technique installed in an RF sputtering system. The fabricated VAHNWs were also subjected to air annealing at 600 ˚C for 1 hour. The interface trap density (D_it) decreased from 1.7×10^10 〖eV〗^(-1) 〖cm〗^(-2) (as-deposited) to 1×10^10 〖eV〗^(-1) 〖cm〗^(-2)(annealed) which is consistent with a reduction in electrically active interface states. The MOS capacitor exhibited a significant memory window of approximately 5.35 V at ± 8 V and stable endurance over 2000 programming/erasing cycles. Moreover, a charge retention duration as long as 3.5×10^(4 ) s was observed after annealing. These enhanced parameters can be ascribed to the annealing-induced modification of electrically active defects together with improved interface quality. The results demonstrated the thermally annealed WO3/β-Ga2O3 VAHNWs as a promising candidate for future non-volatile memory technologies..

items.title: Thermal Budgets of AI Accelerators from First Principles: The Thermodynamic Floor, Present Practice, and the Cost of Moving Data
items.abstract: A first-principles thermal budget for AI accelerators. The Landauer erasure floor at 300 K is compared with the energy per operation of a current flagship accelerator at vendor peak throughput and thermal design power (a gap of about eight orders of magnitude), totalled over a published frontier training run of 3.8e25 operations with its heat-rejection requirement, and decomposed with published per-access energies showing that data movement, not arithmetic, dominates. All numbers are produced by the deposited computation script from published constants and specifications. Model calculations: simulated, not measured.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Thermodynamics of Copying Information: Accuracy, Not Erasure, Sets the Price
items.abstract: Copying a bit, unlike erasing it, has no Landauer floor: copying a known bit onto a blank target is logically reversible, and the minimum copy energy is set by accuracy. In an antipodal discrimination model against Gaussian thermal noise the minimum is 1.31e-19 J per bit at an error probability of 1e-15 at 300 K. DNA replication copies at 8.30e-20 J per bit with a final error rate of 1e-10 per base (2.00004 ATP equivalents per base, including proofreading and mismatch-repair costs), within a factor of 1.92 of the accuracy floor per copied symbol. Silicon copying costs 4.50e-11 J per bit (DRAM to DRAM with SECDED error correction), 2.17e-10 J per bit (solid-state drive to drive) and 8.52e-9 J per bit (hard disk to hard disk), that is 3.45e8 to 7.03e10 times the floor, because a silicon bit is a macroscopic object. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its output (results.json).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Price of Being Right: Energy per Correct Bit in Ribosomal Proofreading
items.abstract: The ribosome incorporates amino acids at an error rate near 1e-4 per residue, although equilibrium codon-anticodon discrimination alone gives near 1e-2. Kinetic proofreading buys the difference with GTP hydrolysis. From published inputs at 310 K (cellular GTP hydrolysis 50 kJ/mol, one proofreading step, 4 high-energy phosphate equivalents per elongation cycle), the proofreading step adds 8.3027e-20 J per amino acid on a total cycle cost of 3.3211e-19 J. One Hopfield step predicts the observed error exactly: (1e-2)^2 = 1e-4. The gain is 6.644 bits of error exponent but only 0.1214 Shannon bits per residue. Total energy per correct bit is 7.6876e-20 J, 25.91 times kT ln2 at 310 K; extra energy per exponent bit is 1.2497e-20 J (4.21 Landauer units) and per Shannon bit gained 6.8406e-19 J (230.58 units). A silicon DRAM access at 2.0e-11 J per bit costs 2.60e8 times more per bit. The trade-off is linear in the logarithm of the error improvement: half a GTP per decade at the stated discrimination. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. Deposit includes paper PDF, computation script and outputs.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Iwakuni Base Resilience Protocol: Engineering Physical, Neural, and Economic Buffers for 300-Year Autonomous Civilizational Units (邦題:岩国ベース・レジリエンス・プロトコル:300年を見据えた「余白」の設計論 — 不揮発知能・熱力学的自律性・自動経済防衛の統合実装)
items.abstract: Abstract (English): Modern lean-efficiency engineering lacks structural buffers against non-linear climatic extremes—spanning both severe thermal waves exceeding 40°C and sudden sub-zero cold snaps. Triggered by empirical motor burnout failures in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi, Japan, this monograph establishes the Iwakuni Base Resilience Protocol (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24094981), a comprehensive blueprint for a 300-year autonomous civilizational unit maintained at a net operational expenditure (OpEx) under 2,000 JPY/month. The architecture integrates four foundational pillars: (1) Non-Volatile Edge Intelligence, deploying Renesas RA8D1 (Cortex-M85) MCUs with embedded STT-MRAM Processing-in-Memory (PIM) and Everspin xSPI MRAM black-box loggers executing 10 kHz TinyML anomaly prediction (Motor-Guard) immune to thermal charge leakage up to 125°C and power-loss volatility; (2) Thermodynamic Autonomy (Tri-Generation), cascading a 700 W Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC, 55% LHV electrical efficiency) with a compact LiBr-water absorption chiller (Yazaki Aroace, 5 USRT), a 1,000 L 2.0G-seismic GRP thermal/water buffer tank (~58 kWh thermal capacity), and IntelliThaw freeze-protection tracing to achieve 85–90% total exergy efficiency; (3) Automated Economic Shielding (Resilience as a Service, RaaS), combining objective index-triggered parametric catastrophe insurance with low-friction P2P mutual aid pools (Frich) backed by cryptographic/MRAM waveform evidence; and (4) A 300-Year Material Shell utilizing deeply carbonized Yakisugi (Shou Sugi Ban) cladding for zero-repainting salt-air and biological durability. 要旨(日本語): 短期的な効率最大化を目的としリソースを極限まで削ぎ落とす現代の設計思想は、40℃超の酷暑と突発的な氷点下の寒波(小氷期リスク)が共存する非線形な気候変動に対して構造的な脆弱性を抱えている。本論文(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24094981) は、山口県岩国市におけるモーター焼損事象を工学的教訓とし、実質月額維持コスト(OpEx)2,000円以下で300年間自律機能する文明の最小単位「岩国ベース・レジリエンス・プロトコル」の包括的実装仕様を提示する。本システムは以下の4層で構成される。(1) 不揮発な神経系(MRAM PIM):125℃の高温下でも電荷リークを起こさず瞬時起動(インスタント・オン)を実現するRenesas RA8D1(内蔵MRAM)およびEverspin xSPI MRAMを採用し、10kHzサンプリングのTinyML予兆検知アルゴリズム「Motor-Guard」をエッジ実装する。(2) 熱力学的自律性(Tri-Gen+物理タンク):発電効率55%のSOFC(エネファーム type S)の高温排熱を小型吸収式冷凍機(矢崎総業 Aroace)で冷熱変換し、水平震度2.0G対応の1,000L GRP製断熱パネルタンク(熱容量約58kWh)とIntelliThaw凍結防止機構を連成させることで総合エクセルギー効率85〜90%を達成する。(3) 経済的セーフティネットの自動化(RaaS):気象・地震指標連動のパラメトリック保険(テールリスク移転)とMRAM波形ログを証跡とするP2P互助(Frich:小口設備損害補填)のリスク・サンドイッチ構造を構築する。(4) 300年外殻:塩害・腐朽菌・紫外線に耐える本焼き「焼杉」外壁によりライフサイクルコストを極小化する。
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Four Sovereignty Invariants: Quantifying Single-Point Chokepoints Across the Global AI Compute Supply Chain
items.abstract: Executive Abstract: Between 2024 and 2026, nation-states and Fortune 500 enterprises committed over $1.4 trillion to 'Sovereign AI' initiatives under the assumption that purchasing domestic GPU clusters or training national foundation models confers strategic autonomy. This working paper demonstrates why that assumption is structurally false. By mapping 12 physical and jurisdictional layers of the global AI compute stack, we show that single-vendor or single-region concentration exceeds 70% to 100% at six non-substitutable bottlenecks—including 100% of High-NA EUV lithography (ASML), 92% of CoWoS advanced wafer packaging (TSMC), 90% of ultra-high-purity crucible quartz (Spruce Pine, USA), and extraterritorial cloud IAM kill-switches. We formalize the Four Sovereignty Invariants from The Sovereign Illusion to provide policymakers and CTOs with a quantitative framework for auditing supply-chain resilience. Companion Volume & Open Dataset: Book (Amazon Kindle / Print): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HMS4JJ1R (ASIN: B0HMS4JJ1R / Paperback: B0HMX59GSQ / Hardcover: B0HMZRG96T) Open Chokepoint Dataset & Interactive Simulator: https://github.com/digbijoylabs/the-sovereign-illusion Publisher Portal: https://digbijoylabs.com
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Braille Volume Bound: Why a Textbook Becomes a Shelf, and What Fits in a Schoolbag
items.abstract: Braille is spacious. From the standard cell geometry, this paper computes characters per page, the page count of a stated 400,000-character textbook in Braille, its thickness and its mass. The bound explains, in numbers, why Braille textbooks arrive as multi-volume sets and why a pupil cannot carry a term's reading in one bag. Any access plan that ignores the volume bound will fail at the school gate; refreshable displays and audio are priced in the discussion against this bound. Computed results: chars_per_page = 1148, braille_pages = 348, thickness_m = 0.09, mass_kg = 4.2, volumes_of_100_pages = 3.5. Every number in this paper is produced by the accompanying script `compute.py`. SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Technical Note TN-2026-HBN-02: Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Fabrication and Open-Surface ALD Protocol for h-BN Protective Linings in Ultra-High-Gradient PWFA Capillaries
items.abstract: This technical note details the Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Architecture and Open-Surface Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) protocol for depositing 50.0 nm hexagonal Boron Nitride (h-BN) protective linings inside high-gradient Plasma Wakefield Accelerator (PWFA) capillary channels. To overcome precursor gas diffusion limits (Knudsen transport bottleneck) in ultra-high aspect ratio micro-channels (up to 2,000,000:1), matching semi-circular micro-grooves are precision-machined onto planar synthetic sapphire blocks. This leaves the surface completely open during deposition, guaranteeing zero precursor depletion and uniform 50.0 nm h-BN atomic layer growth across the entire 1.0-meter channel length prior to optical contact fusion. Key Specifications & Results: - Substrate: High-purity synthetic sapphire (0001 c-plane planar slabs) - Capillary Baseline Length: 1000.0 mm (1.0 meter) - Groove Radius / Post-Bonding Inner Bore: r = 250.0 nm, width w = 500.0 nm (ϕ_ad = 500.0 nm) - Surface Roughness: R_a < 0.5 nm (CMP polished optical standard) - Protective Liner Thickness: t_hbn = 50.0 nm ± 1.2 nm - Assembly Method: Direct solid-state thermal fusion at 1100°C in UHV after cleanroom optical contact alignment Includes full fabrication process steps, metrology requirements, and prototype non-recurring engineering (NRE) cost estimates.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Tailor‐Made 3D‐Nanoprinted Microchannel Plate Detector Functionalized by Atomic Layer Deposition Showing Electron Multiplication
items.abstract: ABSTRACT With the establishment of two‐photon polymerization in additive manufacturing, the precise fabrication of arbitrarily shaped 3D features has become possible on the microscopic and even on the nanometric scale. The unsurpassed design freedom of this technique enables wide‐ranging applications across multiple research areas, such as microfluidics, photonics, life science, and micro‐electromechanical systems. Herein, the fabrication of a tailor‐made microchannel plate (MCP) generated by 3D‐nanoprinting (3DN) based on two‐photon polymerization is explored. A workflow for the 3DN‐MCP scaffold fabrication and subsequent functionalization by atomic layer deposition is presented. First strategies for print time reduction are proposed that allow for a 65% faster scaffold production, currently at the cost of microchannel shape accuracy. For the proof‐of‐concept experiment, a picoampere current is supplied by a carbon‐nanotube‐based field emitter to the 3DN‐MCP. An amplification factor in the order of 10 2 is measured for the 3DN‐MCP, which can likely be enhanced by microchannel dimension adjustments and further tuning of the surface coatings’ electrical properties in the future. Based on this study, innovative 3DN‐MCP designs may be explored, as the developed 3DN processing route is not limited to the conventional microchannel shape of glass‐based MCPs.

items.title: Supporting Materials for Observability in Agentic Coding
items.abstract: This record contains supporting research materials for the thesis “Observability in Agentic Coding: Evaluating Practitioner Requirements and Existing Tools.” The study draws on 12 semi-structured practitioner interviews and thematic analysis to identify ten observability requirements. Materials included in this record are described in the file list. Interview recordings and any personal or identifiable information are excluded from public access unless sharing has been explicitly authorised.
authors: Dhanush Janapareddy; Gubala Haribabu Laasya Sai
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Structural and electronic properties of (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ phases from first principles
items.abstract: (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ material system is promising for ferroelectric devices, owing to their compatibility with the existing electronics manufacturing processes. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations can be used for the device design and optimization, but the predictive power of TCAD device simulations depends on the quality of the material parameters. These are still surprisingly poorly understood, also for the metastable ferroelectric phase, largely owing to the difficulties in synthesizing phase-pure samples. Here, we carry out high-quality first-principles calculations to extract reliable lattice parameters, dielectric constants, and band gaps for six of the most common phases of HfO$_2$, Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$, and ZrO$_2$. We compare results from GGA, meta-GGA, and hybrid functionals to shed light on the sensitivity of the results on the level of theory and to connect the results to earlier literature. In the case of band structures, we also consider $GW$ corrections as well as the effects of temperature-induced band gap renormalization and excitonic effects. Finally, we use these results in TCAD simulations for (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ FeCAP to demonstrate the effect that non-ferroelectric interlayers could have on the hysteresis curves and band diagrams.

items.title: Structural Analysis of Sparse Model Architectures: Hidden Gaps, Recurring Patterns, and Five Open Paradigm Candidates for Next-Generation LLMs
items.abstract: Version 5.1 corrects: the omission of prior work on adaptive computation (Adaptive Computation Time, Universal Transformers, Mixture-of-Depths, Mixture-of-Recursions, early exit), dynamic and zero-computation expert routing, adaptively sparse attention, neural architecture search, learned addressing for N-gram memory (Lngram), and writable or editable conditional memory (Memorizing Transformers, User as Engram, Writability and the Pathway, EngramEdit). A related-work section is added. Per-token skipping, adaptive depth, learned numbers of active experts and learned or searched architecture are established, and writes into hash-addressed Engram rows have been demonstrated when the fact and its trigger are supplied from outside, mainly by gradient optimization and with precomputed overrides applied per request at serving time; gradient-free variants have been tried with limited success. The gap and novelty statements of Gaps 1, 2, 4 and 5, Candidates 1–5 and the corresponding open questions are narrowed accordingly to what remains open: writes into hash-addressed tables that the model itself triggers from its hidden state during generation, with collision handling in a shared table, and an effective gradient-free write; a per-token choice between memory lookup and computation; an allocation search that includes the conditional-memory axis; and learned memory-specific structural decisions. “Open” in the title refers to this restricted sense. One table entry that attributed shared experts to the original Mixture-of-Experts layer, and two author lists in the bibliography, are corrected. The previous version is 10.5281/zenodo.19312203; this version supersedes it. We present a structural analysis of sparse model architectures, identifying five gaps in the current paradigm, documenting recurring meta-patterns across major AI breakthroughs, and proposing five candidate architectures for the next paradigm shift. This version integrates discussion of Titans and UMoE as related work. This paper presents no experimental results; it presents a structural argument for where to look next. Files. structural_analysis_v5.1.pdf (paper), structural_analysis_v5.1.tex (LaTeX source).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Situating virtue ethics and consequentialism in European AI guidelines for journalism
items.abstract: The rapid development of AI in journalism, particularly following the emergence of generative AI, has intensified the need for ethical guidance, prompting news organisations and self-regulatory bodies to produce a growing body of guidelines and recommendations.Drawing on a moral pluralist perspective, this paper investigates how virtue ethics and consequentialist reasoning interact with duty-based approaches across a corpus of 65 texts published by European newsrooms, professional organisations and self-regulatory actors.The analysis examines how virtues such as prudence, authenticity and vigilance, alongside outcome-oriented considerations such as harm prevention, public trust and societal impact, are operationalised in practice.The findings show that ethical reasoning in AImediated journalism is frequently hybrid and context-dependent: duties establish normative boundaries, while virtues and consequences guide contextualised judgement and decision-making.These results suggest that the ethical challenges posed by AI cannot be adequately addressed without a pluralist approach integrating rules, consequences and professional judgement, highlighting how guidelines transform ethical journalism into an interpretive structure in which these elements become operational mechanisms.

items.title: Secure AI Agent Infrastructure
items.abstract: Reproducible research prototypes addressing one question: can an autonomous agent be trusted with a security decision, and would you know if it could not? Contains an agent verification harness that scores whether each claim in an LLM's output is supported by the documents it retrieved, a per-class smart-contract vulnerability benchmark with audited negative controls, and an LLM audit agent. Results files record measured runs against SHA-256-pinned sources; metrics that the evidence does not support are withheld with a machine-readable reason rather than reported.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Secondary switching ratio: an electrical probe of polarization switching evolution in HZO/ZrO2 hybrid bilayers
items.abstract: The ferroelectric-to-antiferroelectric (FE–AFE) crossover in HfO 2 -based capacitors produces multi-step switching responses that cannot be fully described by conventional hysteresis parameters. Here, we introduce the secondary switching ratio, R sec , extracted from transient switching currents, to electrically probe the FE–AFE switching character and its evolution in HZO/ZrO 2 hybrid bilayer capacitors, in which a ferroelectric HZO layer and an antiferroelectric ZrO 2 layer are combined with systematically varied composition and thickness ratios. Importantly, R sec is not interpreted as an absolute orthorhombic/tetragonal phase fraction, but as a functional measure of the relative secondary-switching contribution associated with antiferroelectric-like recovery under a defined pulse protocol. Across the hybrid stack series, R sec evolves systematically from the FE-dominant to the AFE-dominant limit, is qualitatively corroborated by GIXRD signatures, and captures hold-time-, temperature-, cycling-, bias-, and bilayer thickness-ratio-dependent changes in the switching response. Hold-time and delay-time measurements from 83 K to 353 K reveal history-dependent secondary-switching relaxation with a finite low-temperature component, supporting a field-driven contribution with additional thermal assistance at higher temperatures. Temperature-dependent measurements and XPS depth profiling indicate that the wake-up evolution is mainly associated with field-driven switching-state reconfiguration, while oxygen-vacancy redistribution acts as a secondary contributor in the present hybrid bilayer system. This framework establishes R sec as a practical electrical probe for tracking FE–AFE switching evolution in hafnia-based hybrid bilayer capacitors.

items.title: Scoring consistency of teachers and artificial intelligence algorithms in written expression assessment: a comparative quantitative study
items.abstract: Written expression assessment at the secondary school level involves complex interactions among text genre, evaluator type, and student characteristics. The present study examined the degree of agreement, divergence, and patterning between scores produced by four large language model (LLM)-based algorithms, ChatGPT, Grok, Minimax, and Gemini, and those assigned by human teachers when rating texts composed by secondary school students. A total of 122 students (63 female, 59 male), aged approximately 11–14 years and enrolled in grades 6, 7, and 8 at a public secondary school in Turkey, participated in the study and composed their texts in Turkish. Each student produced one text in a randomly assigned genre: folktale, poetry, or biography. All raters, both human teachers and AI algorithms, evaluated the texts using an identical five-dimensional analytic rubric. Inter-rater agreement was quantified via Pearson correlations and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), while score differences across evaluator type, text genre, and gender were examined using mixed-design ANOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted paired-samples t-tests for pairwise comparisons and independent-samples t-tests. ChatGPT demonstrated the highest alignment with teacher scores ( r = .78, ICC = 0.78). In contrast, Minimax showed the weakest correspondence ( r = .71). Text genre did not exert a statistically significant main effect on scores (F(2, 119) = 0.81, p = .445, partial η 2 = 0.01); however, a statistically significant evaluator-by-genre interaction was detected (F(8, 476) = 3.77, p < .001, partial η 2 = 0.06), such that human teachers scored poetry markedly lower than the other genres. In contrast, AI systems did not show this pattern. Gender-related score differences were observed exclusively in teacher evaluations (d = 0.50), whereas no statistically significant gender differences were detected in any of the four AI algorithms’ scores (all p ≥ .198). These findings indicate that LLM-based algorithms hold promise as formative feedback tools particularly ChatGPT, whose scores aligned most closely with teacher judgments across dimensions and genres, making it best suited to generating rapid, low-stakes draft feedback that students and teachers can use to guide revision while also revealing algorithm-specific limitations, most notably Minimax’s weaker alignment with teacher scores, that preclude direct substitution for human judgment in high-stakes writing assessment.

items.title: Rubric-anchored large language model feedback for academic argumentation revision
items.abstract: Generative AI can provide rapid, detailed feedback for student writing, yet its organization may affect how students use feedback during short classroom revision windows. This study examined descriptive outcome and process patterns across rubric-anchored LLM feedback (RA), non-anchored LLM feedback (NA), and an active criteria-aligned self-revision comparison in a four-week intact-class quasi-experiment with 105 Chinese second-year Economics students (three classes, one per condition). Two practice tasks used Draft-Review-Revision cycles, whereas baseline (T0) and posttest (T1) assessments were completed without feedback. Rubric-scored argumentation performance was summarized using covariate-adjusted posttest means, with a maximum possible score of 24. Descriptive adjusted means were highest under RA (14.64), followed by NA (14.21) and Control (14.05). The naive individual-level ANCOVA did not yield a statistically significant Condition term. Descriptive revision-activity summaries based on words added, words deleted, and net word change showed greater textual change under RA across both practice tasks on several indicators. In an exploratory subsample of 24 students, the proportion of suggestions targeting Claim, Evidence, Reasoning, or Counterargument that were adopted or partially adopted was descriptively higher under RA (75.0%) than NA (69.0%). Given the one-class-per-condition design and condition-specific prompts, these findings do not isolate a causal effect of rubric anchoring. Within the GPT-4o-based implementation examined here, rubric-aligned organization warrants further investigation as a design feature for time-limited classroom revision.

items.title: Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Logic Circuits Driven by Ion‐Mediated Organic Electrochemical Diodes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of data‐intensive computing has exposed the physical limitations of conventional hardware architectures. While accumulative multistate memory devices offer low‐power alternatives, incorporating multistate reconfigurability into switching devices enables fully integrated, multifunctional neuromorphic operations across both logic and memory. Herein, we report programmable multistate logic circuits based on organic neuromorphic devices. By leveraging the intrinsic learning capability of organic electrochemical diodes (OECDs), multiple logic functions are realized within a single diode‐resistor configuration. The channel conductance of each OECD is dynamically modulated by the polarity and frequency of the input voltage, enabling seamless reconfiguration to execute custom logic operations (e.g., AND/OR and XOR/unknown). Furthermore, we demonstrate a functional half‐adder by cascading two multistate logic circuits as a proof‐of‐concept neuromorphic computing architecture. These results establish a promising pathway toward on‐chip, learning‐based digital circuitry with potential relevance to future neuromorphic computing applications.

items.title: Q-Planner: A Harness System for Quantum Chemistry Agents
items.abstract: Abstract LLM-based agents for computational chemistry commonly place the model inside an accumulating execution loop, causing context growth proportional to workflow length, unpredictable token costs, and degraded plan reliability at scale. We present a chemistry computation harness that confines LLM invocations to three semantically bounded stages─compound identification, planning, and reporting─while delegating all tool dispatch, parallel scheduling, arithmetic derivation, and artifact routing to a deterministic LangGraph executor that consumes zero LLM tokens during execution; a library of domain skill modules injects specialist quantum chemistry protocols into the planner context at planning time without enlarging the execution context. Across five representative quantum chemistry workflows, the planning, calculator, and reporting calls averaged 9700–25,300 tokens per run, with zero execution-stage tokens in every case─more than 93% fewer tokens (before caching) than loop-based multiagent systems─and, on a high-throughput single-point-energy scaling benchmark, a full-scheme plan representation sustained 100% plan-structural correctness across all 30 runs from N = 10 to 100 compounds of one workflow type, generating a 200-node graph of 100 independent single-point jobs from a single planning call. On the workloads tested, harness design made quantum chemistry automation more robust and its cost more predictable; the model ablation shows that model capability still matters.

items.title: Power Optimized High Speed Sense Amplifier for 6T SRAM
items.abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) is used in a wide range of applications in modern VLSI like processors, microcontrollers, embedded systems and SoC due to its High Speed data access and reliable operation. A standard 6T SRAM cell is composed by 6 MOS transistors, two cross coupled inverters and two access transistors. While reading data there is a small voltage difference between complementary Bit Lines (BL and BL̅) which needs to be correctly sensed using a Sense Amplifier. Problems faced by traditional sense amplifiers can include increased levels of power consumption, slower sensing speeds and reduced reliabilities especially during low voltages. This project proposes a Power Optimized High Speed Sense Amplifier for 6T SRAM. The system uses a 6T SRAM Cell, Bit Line Precharging Circuit and Optimised Sense Amplifier. LTspice was used to create the design. The circuit was analysed by using transient waveforms of voltage and currents. Key parameters were looked at such as power consumption, speed and Read Delay. This should give us a fast data sensing circuit with reduced power consumption and reliable reading. The design would be useful for Low Power VLSI memory applications.
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines
items.abstract: DeepSeek-V4.1's 203 GB of Engram n-gram tables sit in host DRAM today, taking 190 of the 223 GiB a 4-GPU serving process uses. Row indices depend only on input tokens, so reads can start with each step and overlap earlier layers. V4.1's two Engram layers have windows that differ by 30x (0.3 vs. 9.3 ms). We show that this deadline, together with session reuse and contention on a shared device, decides which tier each table can use and which layers need cache, and we give a model that predicts the resulting slowdown from measured read times. Agent and chat traffic reuse rows within sessions, and static hot sets transfer poorly. We build SlackTier, a table tier for SGLang that issues all lookups at step start. It reads the short-window layer first and splits a small GPU row cache across layers. The path runs inside the decode CUDA graph and is bit-exact with the original gather. Layer 14's table can go to NVMe uncached with no measurable decode cost. With both tables on four NVMe disks, mean time per output token on agent and chat replays rises at most 1.4% over unmodified SGLang, and host memory falls from 212 to 34 GiB. Both tables need no cache when read over RDMA (remote direct memory access) from another node's memory; one copy serves two instances. On a KV-constrained agent workload, using the freed memory as host KV cache at the same memory budget raises median throughput by 36% and cuts median p90 time to first token from 38 to 24 s.

items.title: Physics-Aware Co-training to Overcome Device Non-idealities in Canted SOT-MTJ Arrays for In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: Abstract The physical non-idealities inherent in emerging spintronic devices, such as device-to-device variations, stochastic switching, and nonlinear conductance responses, pose fundamental challenges for their deployment in in-memory computing architectures. Here, we investigate the integration of canted spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs) for deep learning applications and propose a hardware-aware deep learning framework that embeds into the training process experimentally extracted device characteristics, which are faithfully resolved via a dedicated three-terminal SOT testing scheme that effectively suppresses spin-transfer torque, halves the switching threshold voltage, and eliminates parasitic drifts to minimize measurement-induced fluctuations and reveal intrinsic 1010-cycle endurance, thereby directly facilitating robust hardware–software co-optimization. By tuning a normalized conductance factor gnorm, we achieve a median classification accuracy of 88.9% on the Wine dataset using a 13 × 13 SOT-MTJ array, surpassing baseline software-to-hardware weight mapping. Incorporating hardware-aware co-training further elevates the median accuracy to 94.4%, demonstrating substantial robustness against device imperfections. Overall, our results highlight that explicitly modeling device variability at both the physics and algorithm levels can enable spintronic hardware based on SOT-MTJ arrays to function as compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic platforms, allowing device stochasticity to be incorporated as a learnable constraint, ultimately recovering hardware inference accuracy to within a few percentage points of the ideal software baseline.

items.title: Photodetectors Based on Two‐Dimensional Materials: From Sensory Health Monitoring to Cognitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Driven by advances in wearable electronics and artificial intelligence, photodetectors have become central to modern sensing technologies. Two‐dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as promising platforms for advanced optoelectronics, owing to their atomic‐scale thickness, widely tunable bandgaps, strong light‐matter interactions, and inherent mechanical flexibility. Although sensory health monitoring and cognitive neuromorphic computing are currently evolving as distinct domains, they represent a continuous technological trajectory from passive data acquisition to active in‐sensor processing. This review provides a comprehensive overview of 2D material‐based photodetectors, bridging flexible healthcare devices and advanced artificial visual systems. First, fundamental photodetection mechanisms, advanced synthesis methods, and device performance enhancement strategies are systematically elucidated. Subsequently, recent progress in flexible photodetectors for health monitoring is summarized. To overcome the power, latency, and data‐transfer limitations of conventional von Neumann architectures, neuromorphic optoelectronic devices are further discussed, particularly artificial optical synapses capable of emulating biological perception‐memory‐processing pipelines for low‐power biomimetic vision and in‐sensor computing. Finally, future challenges are critically assessed, including scalable manufacturing, long‐term stability in biointegrated environments, stretchable devices for suppressing motion artifacts, and multimodal sensory fusion. This review delineates a promising path toward physiological cognitive computing and imperceptible intelligent optoelectronics for precision medicine and edge‐AI diagnostics.

items.title: Phase Transition Regulation and Properties of Transition Metal Oxide SrCoOx
items.abstract: Transition metal oxide SrCoOx (2.5 ≤ x ≤ 3.0) has attracted considerable attention owing to its reversible topotactic phase transition between the brownmillerite SrCoO2.5 phase (BM-SCO, an antiferromagnetic insulator) and the perovskite SrCoO3−δ phase (PV-SCO, a ferromagnetic metal). This phase transition is driven by continuous changes in oxygen stoichiometry and is accompanied by dramatic reconstruction of the valence state, spin state, and electronic ground state of cobalt ions, giving rise to order-of-magnitude differences in magnetic, electrical, optical, and thermal properties. This review systematically summarizes the crystal structures, physical properties, and regulation rules of oxygen vacancy channels (OVCs) in BM-SCO and PV-SCO. It summarizes recent advances in phase-transition regulation strategies, including ionic liquid gating, epitaxial strain engineering, topotactic redox, protonation/hydrogen intercalation, and triboelectric/mechanical-energy induction, with emphasis on frontier achievements such as in situ imaging of freestanding membranes, reduction-mediated oxidation, stepwise oxidation by water vapor, and neutron diffraction determination of magnetic order. Furthermore, the application potential is discussed in terms of resistive switching and memristive behavior, magnetoionics, optical electrochromism, and neuromorphic computing, along with key challenges and future directions concerning cycling stability, room-temperature ionic migration rate, and multi-parameter synergistic regulation.

items.title: Performance Prediction Techniques for Deep Learning Systems: A Survey
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning models has led to their widespread application across various domains; however, this has resulted in a significant increase in both hardware and software costs, necessitating optimizations for resource efficiency. To address this issue, performance prediction techniques evaluate the performance impact of corresponding optimizations on deep learning systems to maximize performance gains. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of performance prediction techniques for deep learning systems, categorizing them into allocation, cluster, and accelerator levels based on the system level at which their corresponding optimizations are situated, ranging from high to low. Allocation-level techniques primarily construct the relationships between resource configurations and their performance, cluster-level techniques model the optimizations within deep learning frameworks at given configurations, while accelerator-level techniques assess the efficiency of specific hardware. We point out that prediction techniques at different levels exhibit a hierarchical relationship rather than operating in isolation. High-level prediction techniques can incorporate the results from low-level techniques into their performance models to accommodate more low-level optimizations and improve their prediction accuracy. However, this will slow down the construction and execution speed of performance models, requiring trade-offs for specific use cases. Finally, we discuss future challenges and research directions in performance prediction techniques for deep learning systems.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization

items.title: PILLARS OF SILICON: FROM SAND PHYSICS TO ALGORITHMIC CONSCIOUSNESS A Comprehensive Journey Through Semiconductor Physics, Computer Architecture, Computational Theory, Artificial Intelligence, and the Future of Computing
items.abstract: PILLARS OF SILICON: FROM SAND PHYSICS TO ALGORITHMIC CONSCIOUSNESS Summary This comprehensive work traces humanity's greatest material transformation: how inert silicon sand becomes the foundation of algorithmic consciousness. Spanning eighteen chapters across six major parts, the book constructs a unified narrative connecting quantum mechanical properties of silicon atoms to the emergence of artificial intelligence and post-silicon computing paradigms. Part One explores semiconductor physics, from silicon crystal lattices and band theory to MOSFET transistors and EUV lithography manufacturing. Part Two examines computational structures, progressing from Boolean algebra through computer architecture to parallelism and hardware optimization. Part Three ascends to computational theory, covering Turing machines, algorithmic complexity, and the P versus NP problem. Part Four delves into artificial intelligence, from machine learning foundations through transformer architectures and reinforcement learning. Part Five surveys future paradigms including quantum computing, neuromorphic systems, and brain-computer interfaces. Part Six explores post-silicon frontiers and ultimate boundaries. The revised edition introduces critical additions: the hard problem of consciousness and Integrated Information Theory, hardware security vulnerabilities (Spectre, Meltdown), the thermodynamic footprint of modern computing, and explicit connecting threads maintaining narrative unity throughout. Licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0 for academic use with commercial licensing reserved, this work provides foundational understanding for navigating computing's past, present, and future.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of Large Language Model (LLM) inference systems has led to significant improvements in serving efficiency. However, our systematic analysis reveals that current evaluation methodologies suffer from fundamental flaws that mask critical performance issues and impede scientific progress.
