Through a comprehensive examination of recent systems, we identify recurring pitfalls in evaluation practices across three key dimensions: Baseline Fairness, Evaluation Setup, and Metric Design. These pitfalls are uniquely problematic for LLM inference due to its dual-phase nature combining prefill and decode operations, heterogeneous workloads, and strict temporal requirements. We demonstrate how implementation differences frequently obscure algorithmic contributions, how workload selection often fails to represent production scenarios, and how metric normalization can hide substantial performance variability that directly impacts user experience. Traditional metrics derived from the classical machine learning serving setup fail to capture the autoregressive generation characteristics essential to LLM inference, leading to misleading conclusions about system performance. To address these challenges, we provide a comprehensive checklist of best practices and methodological recommendations for robust LLM inference evaluations. To demonstrate the practical application of our methodology, we present a case study of speculative decoding evaluation - a technique whose non-uniform token generation patterns with bursts during accepted predictions and delays during verification failures fundamentally confound conventional metrics. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for evaluation methodology that can accelerate progress in LLM inference systems by ensuring meaningful comparisons, reproducible results, and metrics that reflect real-world requirements.

items.title: Novel Modeling Approach for Arc Routing Problems
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper introduces a novel modeling approach for arc routing problems (ARPs) which is easily applied to multiple ARP variants (e.g., capacitated ARPs, multiple depot ARPs, heterogeneous fleets). Our approach tracks the order in which arcs are serviced, rather than explicitly tracking deadheading, and couples the sequence of serviced arcs to the cumulative demand collected along the route. As each route is defined solely by the order of serviced arcs, our approach does not use vehicle indices to represent individual vehicles/routes, but rather the vehicle type, which makes our approach agnostic to vehicle fleet size and thereby suitable for solving ARPs with large fleets and capable of solving ARPs with heterogeneous fleets with unknown distributions of vehicle type without significantly increasing model size compared to ARPs on the same graph with a homogeneous fleet. We also propose a novel method of formulating “return‐to‐facility” (RtF) constraints in location arc routing problems (LARPs) by using a “tagging” system built into the flow variables to ensure each vehicle route returns to the depot it departed from. Our “tagging” method does not add depot indices to flow and binary variables, nor does it add constraints with separate binaries assigning arcs to depots, leading to a more compact model for LARPs. Using a proposed four‐step solution algorithm, we can solve several benchmark LARP instances to optimality, and are often able to obtain solutions of comparable or better objective value than those found by heuristics. We demonstrate the application of our modeling approach not only on the basic CARP and LARP, but also on the LARP with capacitated depots, CARP with time windows, and multi‐depot CARP.

items.title: No Request Left Behind: Tackling Heterogeneity in Long-Context LLM Inference with Medha
items.abstract: Deploying million-token Large Language Models (LLMs) is challenging because production workloads are highly heterogeneous, mixing short queries and long documents. This heterogeneity, combined with the quadratic complexity of attention, creates severe convoy effects where long-running requests stall short, interactive ones, degrading system responsiveness. We present Medha, a serving system that eliminates these convoys by introducing fine-grained, preemptive scheduling to LLM inference. Medha makes preemption practical with a co-designed set of mechanisms – including Adaptive Chunking and Stream Pipeline Parallelism – that overcome the perceived inefficiencies and scaling challenges of chunking. Additionally, we present a new parallelism strategy KV-Cache Parallelism to reduce the decode latency and afford interactivity despite very long context. These mechanisms are orchestrated by a Length-Aware Relative Slack (LARS) scheduler, a deadline- and heterogeneity-aware scheduling policy that prevents both the convoy effect and the starvation that plagues simpler policies. Under a heterogeneous workload, Medha improves throughput by 5.7 × while reducing median and 90th-percentile latency by 30 × and 174 ×, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art non-preemptive systems.

items.title: Neuromorphic Chips
items.abstract: Neuromorphic Chips by Claude
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: NIF-VIO: Visual--Inertial Odometry Across Inertial and Non-Inertial Reference Frames
items.abstract: Conventional visual--inertial odometry (VIO) assumes that observations from cameras and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) are jointly consistent in an inertial reference frame. However, this assumption breaks down under non-inertial conditions. Inside accelerating or rotating carriers, visual observations of the interior reflect carrier-relative motion, while IMU measurements contain additional carrier-induced components, which can compromise conventional fusion. We therefore present NIF-VIO for localization relative to the local environment across inertial and non-inertial reference frames. It adapts visual--inertial fusion based on measurement consistency. As inertial conditions change, early constraint isolation is combined with local reoptimization to limit error propagation before inconsistency confirmation and repair the affected local geometry. Under non-inertial conditions, a compact model with temporally shared parameters is introduced to account for carrier motion while preserving inertial information that complements visual constraints. Experiments on public benchmarks and a self-collected dataset demonstrate that NIF-VIO achieves competitive performance under inertial conditions and improved localization accuracy and availability under non-inertial conditions.

items.title: MosaicKV: SLO-Aware KV-Cache Virtualization for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving in the Cloud
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving has become a first-class cloud workload. The dominant cost driver is no longer compute alone. The key-value (KV) cache consumes tens of gigabytes per replica. It forces providers to either over-provision GPU memory or reject long-context requests. Existing high-throughput engines largely optimize within a single server. They assume KV stays resident in GPU HBM. Under multi-tenancy, HBM is routinely oversubscribed. Naive offloading (e.g., CUDA Unified Memory paging) then creates severe p99 TTFT spikes. These spikes break service-level objectives (SLOs). This paper presents MosaicKV, a KV-cache virtualization layer for multi-tenant LLM inference on shared GPU servers. MosaicKV exposes KV as a schedulable and migratable resource. It jointly optimizes GPU-memory partitioning across tenants. It decides which KV pages stay on HBM versus spill to host DRAM. It also times prefetch and micro-batching to hide PCIe DMA transfer latency. The key insight is that decoding has a predictable layer-by-layer access pattern. By co-designing page layout with a slack-aware scheduler, MosaicKV turns KV offload from reactive paging into a planned pipeline. On an 8-GPU server (8 × H100 SXM 80 GB) serving Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen2.5-32B, and Mixtral-8x7B under a 64-tenant mixed workload, MosaicKV improves goodput-under-SLO by 1.93–2.31 × under the same SLO contract (p99 TTFT ≤ 400 ms for interactive tenants; p99 completion ≤ 2 s for best-effort tenants) while reducing peak HBM KV footprint by 38%. Under flash-crowd bursts, MosaicKV keeps interactive-tenant p99 TTFT at 378–386 ms (within SLO). Unified Memory spikes to 1,055 ms (∼ 2.6 × SLO). MosaicKV achieves these gains without model changes. Runtime overhead remains modest (2.9–6.2%). This enables operators to safely run long-context and bursty tenants on shared GPU fleets.

items.title: MetaMatch: Reconciling Metadata for Aggregating Music Difficulty Annotations
items.abstract: The inconsistency of metadata across sources is a persistent problem for large-scale music research. The variety of approaches to documenting even basic elements such as artists’ names and work titles makes it difficult to aggregate data across different sources. This paper presents a comparative analysis of approaches to this problem, combining the OpenRefine Reconciliation pipeline with LLM-based strategies for entity matching. We also explore one potential application of this pipeline in sheet music difficulty classification. By gathering difficulty labels from established music exam board syllabi and matching them to corresponding IMSLP entries, we link expert difficulty annotations to sheet music available through IMSLP for automatic sheet music difficulty classification. The resulting piano dataset consists of 7,737 repertoire-list entries, of which 2,389 are automatically matched to 1,210 distinct IMSLP work identifiers. Our method produces data that combine high-quality expert annotations with the scale more typically associated with crowd-sourced corpora, and can be extended to additional instruments. We release the matching pipeline, dataset, and code at https://meganelisabethfinch.github.io/metamatch to support further work on cross-corpus music analysis, both for this use case and for the many others which depend on robust metadata alignment at scale.

items.title: Memory as a Temporal Resource: Lifetime Contracts for Multi-Retention Systems
items.abstract: Computers move and rewrite data whose useful lifetimes range from inner-loop iterations to years, yet memory systems usually hide retention as a fixed physical property. We argue that required lifetime should become a first-class resource across algorithms, programming systems, controllers, and devices. Building on prior lifetime-aware placement, we propose an event-based validity contract that links application completion events to retention-class selection and renewal of protection. Applications would be enabled to express semantic contracts such as ``until this tile completes'' and the system will map data to homogeneous arrays engineered for ephemeral, epoch, or durable retention and preserve correctness through margins, ECC, refresh, migration, or recomputation. We present a trace-based simulator and FPGA prototype that exercises class migration.

items.title: Memory Materials on One Budget: The Physics of Retention Media Compared
items.abstract: Six retention media (DRAM, NAND flash, magnetic disk and tape, phase-change memory, FeRAM, and MRAM) are compared on a single physical budget: retention mechanism, physical failure channel, characteristic energy barrier from the literature, retention time at 300 K computed by anchored Arrhenius scaling, and holding energy per bit-year computed from published device figures. DRAM is the only medium with second-scale retention and a large continuous holding cost (1.38e-4 J per bit-year); every nonvolatile medium retains unpowered at zero holding energy, with computed 300 K retention from 1.52 years (end-of-life NAND flash) to 9.88e7 years (phase-change memory). Magnetic tape on a shelf is cheapest per bit-year at scale; phase-change memory is most stable per joule. Model calculations are simulated, not measured. Computations and drafting were performed with Dave, an AI research system.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Measurement Is Not Free: The Energy Ledger of a Measure-Record-Erase Cycle at the Thermodynamic Floor and in Practice
items.abstract: The standard Szilard-Bennett accounting holds that measurement can in principle be free and that the unavoidable cost of an information cycle sits in erasing the record, at the Landauer floor k_B T ln 2 per bit. This paper tests that accounting for a stated measurement chain. The minimum energy to acquire one bit at error probability p_e against thermal noise is derived for a thermal-noise-limited sampler as E = 2 k_B T [Q^-1(p_e)]^2; at p_e = 1e-6 and 300 K this is 1.87e-19 J per bit, 65.20 times the Landauer floor, and acquisition exceeds erasure at the floor for every error probability below 0.2780. A Texas Instruments ADS1115 converter (16-bit, 860 SPS, 150 microA, datasheet SBAS444E) spends 3.60e-8 J per measured bit in practice. With published DRAM and NAND per-bit energies, the full measure-record-erase cycle costs 1.90e-19 J at the floor (98.49% acquisition) and 3.60e-8 J in practice with a volatile record (99.89% acquisition). The standard claim fails in the stated regime, at the floor and in practice. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Mapping the Ecosystem of Large Language Models’ Implementation in the Public Sector: A Systematic Evidence Map
items.abstract: This study examines the implementation of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the public sector through a systematic literature review. Despite growing scholarly attention, existing knowledge remains fragmented, lacking a comprehensive map of empirical evidence. Following PRISMA guidelines, 26 studies from academic databases were analysed using thematic analysis for qualitative synthesis and descriptive statistics to identify patterns across the literature. Four core themes emerged from the analysis: applications of LLMs across government functions; architectures enabling deployment; governance mechanisms shaping implementation; and challenges impeding adoption. Key research trends reveal that scholarly attention concentrates heavily on citizen-facing and policy domains, while operational areas remain underexplored. The field remains in an exploratory phase, with General GenAI/LLM studies dominating compared to enterprise platforms, multi-agent, and multimodal typologies. Internal organisational frameworks emerge as the predominant governance mechanism examined. Technical performance challenges motivate most scholarly inquiry, yet sovereignty and equity concerns appear least often as initial drivers yet recur as barriers in practice. Finally, architectural complexity inversely relates to adoption: basic architectures predominate while complex deployments remain limited, confirming that advanced configurations demand infrastructure, capacity, and resources concentrated in specialised research teams rather than widespread practice. As its central contribution, the study proposes a conceptual phased implementation framework accompanied by a comprehensive guideline tool designed to help public sector organisations navigate the complexities of LLM adoption. Two additional outputs are developed: a practitioner-oriented guide offering LLM implementation tools/checklists, and a research-oriented agenda outlining theoretical gaps for future inquiry.

items.title: Low-Rank Adaptation with a Single Matrix
items.abstract: Abstract Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has become a cornerstone of parameter-efficient fine-tuning for large pretrained models, augmenting frozen pretrained weights with a low-rank update formed by the product of two smaller matrices. Recent research indicates that scale mismatches between these two factors frequently induce unstable training dynamics, leading to suboptimal performance. Here, we reformulate low-rank adaptation by parameterizing the weight update as a single low-rank matrix multiplied by its own transpose. This formulation, which we term SingLoRA , eliminates inter-matrix scale conflicts by construction, thereby promoting stable optimization, while approximately halving the number of trainable parameters. Through the lens of the efficient feature learning framework, we show that SingLoRA is provably stable by design while retaining the expressive capacity of LoRA within the transformer architecture. Extensive experiments on multiple tasks validate these benefits. Extensive experiments on multiple tasks validate these benefits. In common sense reasoning, fine-tuning LLaMA-7B on MNLI with SingLoRA achieves 91.3% accuracy—surpassing LoRA (89.1%) and LoRA+ (90.2%)—while using only 60% of their parameter budget. In image generation, fine-tuning Stable Diffusion with SingLoRA significantly improves image fidelity on DreamBooth, achieving a DINO similarity score of 0.151, compared to scores of 0.148 and 0.143 for DoRA and LoRA, respectively.
items.venue: Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision

items.title: Location-Controlled Ge Grain Growth via Nanoscale Cooling-Hole-Assi-sted Laser Crystallization for Low-Thermal-Budget Monolithic 3D Integration
items.abstract: Abstract Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) integration requires high-performance channel materials processed under strict thermal budgets (<400 °C). While germanium (Ge) is a promising candidate, the stochastic nature of grain boundaries (GBs) in conventionally crystallized films severely degrades carrier transport and device uniformity. In this work, we demonstrate a deterministic location-controlled grain (LCG) growth technique for Ge thin films utilizing a nanoscale “cooling hole” architecture combined with green nanosecond laser crystallization (GNSLC). Transient thermal simulations and microstructural analyses reveal that the nanoscale cooling holes act as localized thermal sinks, inducing lateral crystallization while maintaining the underlying substrate temperature below 240 °C. Furthermore, the incorporation of a silicon nitride (SiNx) capping layer modulates thermal dissipation and exerts stress-mediated growth, yielding highly ordered, single-crystal-like Ge domains up to 1.2 μm with GBs precisely confined between the nanoscale cooling holes. Back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible FinFETs fabricated within these deterministic grains exhibit superior electrical characteristics and significantly tightened performance distributions. Notably, the standard deviation of the subthreshold swing (SS) is reduced by more than 50% compared to conventional polycrystalline devices. By effectively eliminating random GB scattering from the active channel, this LCG platform significantly suppresses device-to-device variability. Ultimately, it provides a robust nanoscale material engineering solution for advanced heterogeneous M3D integration.

items.title: Linguistic Markers of Self-Representation Reflect Daily Emotional Experiences in an Expressive Writing Study
items.abstract: The words people use provide important insights into their emotional experiences. Several measures for tracking emotions through language have been developed, including sentiment (i.e., the positivity and negativity of language) and I-usage (first-person singular pronoun use, thought to reflect negative self-focus). However, emerging research using large language model embedding techniques has quantified not just if people use “I” but how they use it, yielding a measure of self-representation (i.e., how strongly people see themselves as “good” and “able” rather than “bad” and “unable”). This measure tracks mental health outcomes in psychotherapy. Given that emotions and emotion regulation are intimately connected to how we view ourselves, linguistic self-representations may also offer a means for assessing emotional experiences. Here, we examined the associations between participants’ linguistic self-representations and daily emotional experiences in a 14-day expressive writing study (N = 53). Within-person associations showed that on days when participants’ self-representation embedding scores were closer to “good” or “able,” they reported more positive and less negative emotions. At the between-person level, people with self-representations overall closer to “good” experienced lower negative emotional reactivity to expressive writing. These findings suggest that linguistic markers of self-representation hold promise as a tool for assessing emotional experiences, extending prior work linking it to mental health. Translations of these findings could contribute to earlier identification of changes in emotional functioning and provide new ways of assessing metrics of mental health through everyday language.

items.title: LLM Analysis of 150+ Years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals a Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade
items.abstract: Abstract Migration has been a core topic in German political debate, from postwar expellee displacement to labor migration and recent refugee movements. Large-scale analysis of such political discourse has traditionally required extensive manual annotation, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative. Using a theory-driven annotation scheme, we examine how well LLMs annotate subtypes of solidarity and anti-solidarity in German parliamentary debates and whether the resulting labels support valid downstream inference. We first evaluate multiple LLMs across model size, prompting strategies, fine-tuning, historical versus contemporary data, and systematic errors. The strongest models, especially GPT-5 and gpt-oss-120B, achieve macro-F1 scores comparable to human agreement, although their systematic errors can bias downstream results. We therefore combine soft-label model outputs with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL) to reduce bias in long-term trend estimates. Beyond the methodological evaluation, we interpret the resulting annotations from a social-scientific perspective across the Reichstag (1867–1933), West German Bundestag (1949–1990) and Re-Unified German Bundestag (1990–2025) corpus to trace trends in solidarity and anti-solidarity toward migrants, with detailed analysis of postwar Germany (1949–1957) and contemporary Germany (2009–2025). We find relatively high levels of solidarity in the postwar period, especially in group-based and compassionate forms, and a marked rise in anti-solidarity since 2015. We argue that LLMs can support large-scale social-scientific text analysis, but their outputs require rigorous validation and, where systematic errors are present, statistical correction.

items.title: LHEMO: LLM-based heuristic evolution for multi-objective sensor-weapon-target assignment
items.abstract: The multi-objective sensor–weapon–target assignment (SWTA) problem requires the coordinated allocation of heterogeneous sensing and action resources under conflicting objectives such as mission effectiveness, resource consumption, and response time. Existing SWTA solvers, including classical multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and recent large language model (LLM)-based automated heuristic design (AHD) methods, either rely heavily on hand-crafted search components or transfer poorly to SWTA because of its heterogeneous entities, strict feasibility requirements, and Pareto-oriented feedback. To address these challenges, we propose LHEMO, an LLM-based heuristic evolution framework for multi-objective SWTA. LHEMO adopts a bi-level architecture: an outer level evolves executable heuristic programs through LLM-guided operators, and an inner multi-objective solver evaluates each candidate. Two reconstruction operators expand exploration through line- and module-level code regeneration, a validation-and-repair mechanism recovers invalid candidates, a cross-generation reflection mechanism reuses evolutionary experience, and a seeded initialization anchors early-stage search. A Pareto-oriented fitness built on per-instance normalized hypervolume and a feasibility penalty guides the evolution toward high-quality trade-off solutions. Experiments on a benchmark ranging from 8 to 320 targets show that LHEMO attains the best hypervolume among nine compared methods on every instance with at least 64 targets and improves upon the strongest hand-crafted baseline by up to 178.9%. Heuristics evolved on a single 12-target training instance retain about 85% of this performance on instances up to 26.7 times larger. These results establish LLM-driven heuristic evolution as a practical paradigm for constraint-intensive multi-objective resource allocation.

items.title: L2LBM — PPoPP 2027 Artifact
items.abstract: This artifact accompanies the PPoPP 2027 paper “L2LBM: Model-Guided L2 Cache Temporal Blocking for GPU Lattice Boltzmann Solvers.”It includes CUDA solver source code, a model-guided tile-size and temporal-depth selector, archived cross-GPU measurements, evaluation and analysis scripts, prebuilt Linux x86-64 executables, and the paper and supplementary material.The workflows cover single-GPU FP32 BGK experiments with D3Q15, D3Q19 and D3Q27, including correctness checks, performance comparisons, parameter selection, and cache/DRAM profiling. The README provides setup instructions, expected outputs, runtimes, resource requirements, reuse examples and limitations. Archived-data reanalysis is distinguished from new GPU measurements.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Inter-Site Fluctuation Mechanics in the ADC Single-Trap Random Telegraph Signal (RTS) Regime: Closed-Form Characteristic Functions and Non-Gaussian Quantization Dynamics
items.abstract: In our foundational treatment of direct-sampling Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) and software-defined radio (SDR) front-ends, we established the macroscopic Gaussian ensemble limit where large populations of interfacial traps validate the Central Limit Theorem and Hooge-like resistance flicker. However, in cryogenic quantum-readout ADCs operating at millikelvin temperatures and deeply scaled nanoscale FinFET/GAAFET sampling switches, defect freeze-out and constrained active gate areas frequently reduce the active trap population to the few-trap or single-trap limit. In this work, we abandon the Law of Large Numbers (LLN) and formulate a rigorous first-principles theoretical framework for the Single-Trap Random Telegraph Signal (RTS) regime. Modeling the individual interfacial trap as a continuous-time two-state Markov jump process, we derive exact closed-form marginal and two-time joint characteristic functions. We prove that macroscopic Gaussian exponential damping is replaced by exact trigonometric interference, leading to periodic spur nulling, asymmetric phase rotation, and discrete Lorentzian harmonic sideband skirts. Finally, we establish the composite master characteristic function bridging ensemble Gaussian flicker with discrete non-Gaussian RTS dynamics.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Impact of a Process-Induced Interfacial Layer on Ferroelectric Switching and Reliability in AlScN/β-Ga₂O₃ MFS Capacitors
items.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate AlScN-based metal-ferroelectric-semiconductor capacitors directly integrated on a heteroepitaxial β-Ga2O3. Structural analysis reveals the presence of a process-induced amorphous intermixed layer at the AlScN/β-Ga2O3 interface. The fabricated devices exhibit ferroelectric switching behavior, characterized by counterclockwise hysteretic current-voltage loops with an on/off current ratio of >102, which is limited by the intermixed interfacial layer. Piezo-response force microscopy measurements confirm the intrinsic polarization switching capability through phase reversal and butterfly-shaped amplitude loops. Furthermore, positive-up-negative-down measurements indicate polarization switching while revealing a switching current asymmetry. We identify that this asymmetry originates from the internal electric field and charge trapping associated with the interfacial defect layer. This interfacial instability primarily affects the device performance observed during retention (103 s) and endurance (5×103 cycles) tests, suggesting significance of interface engineering for stable ferroelectric operation in AlScN/β-Ga2O3 devices.

items.title: Hyperdimensional Photonic AI Computing
items.abstract: We discuss our work on hyperdimensional photonic AI accelerators, that leverage time-space- and wavelength-division multiplexing towards enhancing compute power and energy efficiency. We benchmark their performance against state-of-the-art GPUs, demonstrating superior throughput and low-energy operation
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: How undergraduate physics students use generative AI for computational modeling
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (genAI) is becoming increasingly prevalent and capable in physics, particularly for programming-related tasks. How, then, does genAI affect students' computational modeling? We interviewed 19 undergraduate students who had recently completed an open-ended computational assignment that encouraged the use of genAI, asking them how they used it. We then conducted a thematic analysis of these interviews using a framework for computational modeling in physics. We found that genAI significantly impacts several aspects of students' computational modeling, such as the planning, implementing, and debugging of computational models. GenAI can also help students find resources and introduce them to new computational tools. Productive use of genAI was associated with students limiting its use to small steps in the modeling process and consistently double-checking the formulas, explanations, and code it provided. We also identified challenges students faced due to an over-reliance on genAI, such as working from false model assumptions and not spending time learning the fundamentals of computational modeling, especially debugging. Finally, we discuss implications for teaching, such as the need to teach students how to use genAI productively and to urge them to plan before they code. We also highlight the continued value of low-stakes assessment and teaching assistants for teaching computational modeling, as the task remains difficult even with the introduction of genAI.

items.title: Holding a Qubit: The Retention Price of Quantum Memory
items.abstract: Classical retention costs almost nothing: a bit in DRAM costs 1.57e-8 J per bit-hour in self-refresh, a bit in flash at most 5.70e-14 J per bit-hour as an amortised rewrite bound, and a bit on tape on a shelf costs nothing. This paper prices the quantum analogue: holding one logical qubit, with no computation performed on it, below a cumulative failure probability of 1% for one hour, one day, and one year. Because bare qubits survive only microseconds (superconducting) to minutes (trapped ion), retention requires continuous surface-code error correction at a 100% refresh duty cycle, with code distance growing as the interval lengthens. Holding one logical qubit takes 15,741 W, 17,569 W, and 20,784 W continuously on the superconducting platform (physical error rate 1e-3, 1 microsecond cycles, distances 27/31/37, 10 kW fixed cryostat plant included) and 2,721 W, 3,057 W, and 3,681 W on the trapped-ion platform (1 ms cycles, distances 19/23/29). The energy per logical-qubit-hour exceeds the classical DRAM bit-hour by a factor of 6.23e14 to 4.76e15, the flash bit-hour by about 1e21, and is unbounded against tape on a shelf at zero holding cost. Quantum memory with present architectures is not a storage medium but a continuous power commitment. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF and markdown, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, DFT Calculations, Development by 3² Factorial Design, and Evaluation for Solubility and Anticancer Activity of Neratinib–3-Hydroxybenzoic Acid Co-Crystals
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives Neratinib, a pan-HER tyrosine kinase inhibitor for HER2-positive breast cancer, suffers from extremely poor aqueous solubility (< 0.002 mg/mL), severely limiting oral bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy. This study aimed to develop and optimize neratinib cocrystals using rational co-former selection and factorial design to enhance solubility, dissolution, and anticancer activity. Methods Five potential co-formers were screened at 3 molar ratios (1:1, 1:2, 1:3) using SynthonDock software. Electronic properties and interaction energetics were characterized using density functional theory (DFT) calculations at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) level. Neratinib–3-hydroxybenzoic acid cocrystals were prepared by solvent evaporation and optimized in 3 2 factorial design using the concentration of co-former (24.8–74.4 mg) and stirring time (30–90 min) as independent variables. The PXRD, FTIR, DSC, SEM and Hirshfeld surface studies were carried out to characterize the compounds. MTT assay was used to evaluate in vitro cytotoxicity against SK-BR-3 cells. Results 3-Hydroxybenzoic acid showed the best binding energy (− 10.05 kcal/mol with a ratio of 1:3) and highest co-crystal score (90.5). Increased reactivity was established using density functional theory (DFT) with the calculation showing diminished HOMO–LUMO gap (0.4324 eV vs 3.3072 eV for pure drug). The 12.4-fold solubility enhancement (0.112 mg/mL vs 0.009 mg/mL) and 4.6 times better dissolution (84.6% vs 18.4% at 60 min) was reached using the third batch PF9 (74.4 mg of 3-hydroxybenzoic acid, 90 minutes.) Cytotoxicity studies showed enhanced anticancer activity (IC 50 = 18.46 µg/mL vs 24.18 µg/mL for pure neratinib) toward HER2-positive breast cancer cells. Conclusion The optimized neratinib–3-hydroxybenzoic acid cocrystal is a clinically relevant pharmaceutical approach to enhance oral bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy in HER2-positive breast cancer for subsequent biological exploration in vivo.

items.title: Highly Reliable Sub-2-nm Hafnia Ferroelectric Tunnel Junction via All-Atomic Layer Deposition Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.

items.title: Harnessing melanin as a marine natural product: a new perspective on food industry applications
items.abstract: Derived from the Greek word “melanos”, melanin is a biopolymer that can be extracted from various sources, including animals, plants, and microorganisms. Four types of melanin have been identified based on their color and synthesis pathway: (i) dark-brown to black allomelanin, (ii) black-brown eumelanin, (iii) dark-brown neuromelanin, and (iv) yellow to reddish-brown pheomelanin. Melanin is widely recognized as a photoprotective, antimicrobial, and antioxidant agent, and has gained increasing attention for its potential applications in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, environmental remediation , and food industries. The growing demand for healthier food products in the modern food industry has driven research and development in areas such as nutraceutical food ingredients, advanced packaging technologies, natural-based additives, and improved production technologies . Although several reviews have discussed various aspects of melanin, studies specifically focusing on melanin derived from animal sources and its applications in the food industry remain limited. Therefore, this review aims to summarize the extraction methods of melanin from animal sources and discuss its potential functions and applications in the food industry. These insights provide guidance for researchers in developing sustainable extraction and application strategies, support the industry in replacing synthetic additives with natural alternatives, and inform consumers about functional, health-promoting food innovations.

items.title: HARDWARE INTEGRATION OF NFNS AND SBNS NUMERAL SYSTEMS IN A FAULT-TOLERANT NEUROMORPHIC PROCESSOR ARCHITECTURE
items.abstract: This paper investigates the microarchitectural principles and technological prospects of designing a fundamentally new class of computing devices – a hybrid fault-tolerant neuromorphic processor. The feasibility of deep hardware integration of the New Fibonacci Numeral System (NFNS) and the Scaled Bergman Numeral System (SBNS) on a single semiconductor die is substantiated. It is demonstrated that due to the identical nature of their underlying mathematical principles (representation of weights via fractions, Fibonacci confluent/convoluted rules), both systems can share up to 85–90% of the physical area of the arithmetic logic unit (ALU) and utilize a unified hardware parity filter. A mechanism for dynamic on-the-fly switching of the computational basis within a single clock cycle via a configuration register depending on the specific application task is described. A technological forecast is formulated, according to which the integer NFNS mode ensures noise immunity and error control (bit-flips) in critical discrete environments (aerospace, cryptography), while the SBNS mode, leveraging the Truncation Symmetry Theorem, eliminates the accumulation of rounding errors and optimizes the bit-width of the significant register mantissa, serving as an ideal foundation for neuromorphic AI accelerators.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Graphene/Si Heterojunction Platform with a Multifunctional Atomic Bridging Layer for Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction
items.abstract: Abstract The facile integration and stability of Si-based photoelectrode architectures are the remaining challenges in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) conversion of CO2 to fuels. In this work, the single-atomic-layer graphene is used as a functional bridging layer to integrate both Si photocathodes and photoanodes, which enable the direct electrodeposition of metal-based electrocatalysts (Cu, Ag, and In–Sn alloys) and a semiconductor-based catalyst Ni–Fe layered double hydroxide (Ni–Fe LDH) on graphene/Si heterojunction electrodes for PEC CO2 reduction and O2 evolution reactions, respectively. We demonstrate a PEC device with a full-cell configuration consisting of an In–Sn/graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and a Ni–Fe LDH/graphene/Si heterojunction photoanode, exhibiting a reduced photovoltage of ∼1080 mV compared to the electrochemical counterparts. A self-powered PEC CO2 reduction with a solar-to-fuel conversion efficiency of 3.2% can be obtained by integrating the graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and photoanode with a Si photovoltaic. In addition, in situ PEC X-ray absorption spectroscopy analyses show that the electrodeposited catalysts on the graphene layer lead to the transport of photogenerated electrons and preserve durability throughout the reaction. Utilizing graphene as a chemically inert atomic bridging layer enables the seamless integration of Si photoelectrodes with various catalysts, providing a platform for the PEC CO2 reduction reaction.

items.title: FlowWise: Stateful Fast-Slow Model Serving for Streaming Traffic Intelligence
items.abstract: Network traffic analysis in cloud and internet service provider (ISP) networks increasingly relies on machine learning (ML) models, as encryption and service consolidation make rule-based classification unreliable. At high flow-arrival rates, however, new flows can arrive faster than end-to-end analysis pipelines can process. Unlike typical cloud inference workloads, packets from the same flow arrive over time and require per-flow state. This streaming, stateful setting limits naive scale-out with stateless workers. This paper presents FlowWise, a serving system for streaming, stateful flow intelligence on commodity CPU/GPU servers that jointly selects (i) how many packets to collect and (ii) which model(s) to apply for each flow to balance latency, service rate, and accuracy. Across three representative tasks, inference time across candidate models differs by 1.8x–141.3x, while packet waiting time can exceed feature computation and inference by 6–8 orders of magnitude at the tail. FlowWise exploits these gaps with an uncertainty-driven fast-slow cascade: it issues early predictions from a one-packet model and escalates only uncertain flows to slower models that wait for additional packets and use richer features. A queue-centric runtime maintains per-flow state, performs asynchronous feature joining, and uses brokered, flow-ID-keyed streams to distribute workload across heterogeneous workers.FlowWise serves 76.3% of flows within 16 ms, improving median end-to-end serving latency by 40.5x while increasing service rate and maintaining similar accuracy to always running the slow model. With thousands of packet-header features per flow, our scale-up benchmark sustains over 48.5k new flows per second on a single 16-core commodity CPU server, comparable to reported flow-arrival rates in city-backbone traces.

items.title: Fabrication and characterization of high-quality Nb/Al-AlO x /Nb cross-type Josephson tunnel junctions utilising CMP-based planarisation techniques
items.abstract: Abstract Josephson tunnel junctions (JJs) are the fundamental building blocks of today's most advanced superconducting electronic components, such as qubits and superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs). Given the ongoing demand for scalability of these devices on the wafer-scale, it is crucial to control the fabrication process as precisely as possible to ensure uniform quality and reproducibility. Today, window-type JJs are often used in the production of DC SQUIDs and while they are reliable and reproducible, they suffer from alignment inaccuracies caused by photolithography and unavoidable parasitic capacitances, thus limiting the energy sensitivity of DC SQUIDs. These problems can be circumvented by producing JJs with cross-type geometry, which allows for smaller junction areas and eliminates parasitic capacitances. Here we discuss the fabrication of Nb/Al-AlO x /Nb-based cross-type JJs, where the trilayer is embedded in sputter-deposited SiO 2 to allow for planarisation of structures and to ensure reliable insulation of the sidewalls of the bottom electrode. Instead of lift-off processes that can require processing times of several hours and potentially produce residual dielectric features along the structure edges that might compromise subsequent layers, we use chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) for the removal of excess SiO 2 . This reduces the duration of the planarization step from hours to minutes and yields smooth, uniform surfaces with a within-wafer non-uniformity of below 5%. The resulting process achieves a junction yield above 90% across 3 inch wafers. In addition, we discuss the influence of fabrication details on the quality and electrical properties of our JJs with different junction areas down to 1 µm × 1 µm distributed across the wafer and extract the junction specific quality parameters from their IV -characteristics. Across the junctions, the spreads are approximately 1% for gap voltage, below 3% for critical current, below 4% for the subgap-to-normal resistance ratio, and below 1% for characteristic voltage.

items.title: ExclaveFL: Verifiable Claims for Federated Learning using Exclaves
items.abstract: In federated learning (FL), data providers jointly train a machine learning model without sharing training data. This makes it challenging to provide verifiable claims about the trained model, e.g., related to the employed training data, data sanitization, or training algorithm—a malicious data provider can simply deviate from the correct training protocol without detection. Prior FL training systems have used trusted execution environments (TEEs) to protect the training computation, relying on the confidentiality and integrity of TEEs. TEE confidentiality, however, has been shown to be vulnerable to various attacks, e.g., via side channels. We describe ExclaveFL , a system for training FL models that establishes verifiable claims about models through fine-grained runtime attestation proofs. Since such proofs only require integrity, ExclaveFL generates them using exclaves , which are integrity-only execution environments without software-managed secrets, making them immune to data leakage attacks. ExclaveFL uses exclaves to attest data transformations during FL training, and the runtime attestation proofs then form an attested dataflow graph of the entire training computation. The graph is checked by an auditor to ensure that the trained model satisfies claims, e.g., about the use of data sanitization by data providers or aggregation by the model provider. Since exclaves require minor yet proprietary firmware changes, we evaluate a variant with similar performance but slightly weaker security guarantees on existing AMD SEV-SNP hardware. We show that ExclaveFL introduces less than 12% overhead compared to unprotected FL model training.

items.title: Enhancing Dielectric Breakdown Strength in BiFeO₃-SrTiO₃ Ceramics via Bi₂Ti₂O₇ Doping
items.abstract: Abstract (1- x )(0.7BiFeO₃-0.3SrTiO₃)- x Bi₂Ti₂O₇ ceramics (abbreviated as BFST- x BTO, where x = 0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, and 0.08) were synthesized via a solid-state reaction method. The BFST and BTO ceramic powders were separately prepared using the solid-state reaction approach. Subsequently, these two types of powders were homogeneously mixed to fabricate BFST- x BTO solid solution ceramics. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirms that BTO diffuses into the crystal lattice of BFST, forming perovskite solid solution ceramics. With the increase of BTO content, the average grain size of the ceramics decreases, while the band gap shows a corresponding increasing trend. Impedance analysis indicates that the conduction mechanism of the ceramics is dominated by oxygen vacancy hopping near the grain boundaries. Notably, the introduction of BTO leads to increased grain boundary density and an expanded band gap, which jointly contribute to the reduced dielectric loss and enhanced dielectric breakdown strength (E b ) of the ceramics. The E b , recoverable energy storage density (W rec ) and efficiency (η) for BFST without BTO doping are 140 kV/cm, 0.38 J/cm 3 and 10.67%. After BTO-doping, E b , W rec and η are all increased. The highest E b =420 kV/cm is obtained in BFST-0.04BTO ceramics. The W rec and η are 2.24 J/cm 3 and 34.74% for BFST-0.04BTO ceramics. With increasing BTO content to 0.08, The E b slightly decreases to 400 kV/cm, while the W rec and η increase to 3.38 J/cm 3 and 39.88%, respectively.

items.title: Emerging Perovskite Quantum Dots for Optoelectronic Sensing–Memory–Computing Neuromorphic Systems
items.abstract: Abstract With the explosive development of artificial intelligence (AI), unprecedented demands have been imposed on modern computing hardware. Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from inherent data throughput and energy efficiency bottlenecks due to physical isolation between computation and memory units. In this context, brain-inspired neuromorphic computing system enabled by emerging optoelectronic synaptic devices (OSDs) has emerged as a highly promising and transformative alternative, offering a viable pathway toward next-generation intelligent computing systems featuring parallelism, low power consumption, and high efficiency comparable to biological neural networks. Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) exhibit exceptional optoelectronic properties, making PQDs-based OSDs (PQDs-OSDs) a research hotspot. This review summarizes recent advances in PQDs-OSDs including the material characteristics and synthesis methods of PQDs, as well as the device structures, working mechanisms, and applications of PQDs-OSDs. We systematically introduce the applications of PQDs-OSDs in brain-inspired computing and artificial vision. Furthermore, the critical challenges of stability and scalability are comprehensively discussed, providing fundamental insights for advancing the application of PQDs-OSDs in optoelectronic sensing-memory-computing neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Dynamic Reprogramming Voltage Design and Optimization for 3D TLC NAND Flash Memory in Physical-Layer Storage Systems
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) TLC NAND flash memory serves as a core physical-layer storage component in high-performance data storage and transmission systems. Although reprogramming techniques effectively boost storage density and memory endurance, long-term data retention degradation and persistent cell loss severely impair the physical-layer reliability and channel stability. To alleviate these impairments during reprogramming operations, this paper proposes a dynamic write voltage design and optimization scheme for 3D TLC NAND flash memory in physical-layer storage systems. The proposed method extracts physical-layer channel parameters from real flash chips and integrates them into the threshold voltage distribution model to realize adaptive reprogramming voltage adjustment. Based on the measured channel characteristics, a dynamic reprogramming voltage strategy from MLC mode to TLC mode is constructed for reliable data refresh in SSD controllers.

items.title: Dispersive relaxation in indium tin oxide contacted silicon oxide memristive devices
items.abstract: Silicon oxide memristive devices exhibit volatile current transients in addition to non-volatile resistive switching. Such transients are candidate temporary states for neuromorphic systems, but their form depends on coupled processes in the oxide and its electrode interfaces. Here, we characterise the transient measured in devices with indium tin oxide (ITO) top contacts using constant-current stress, held-voltage measurements, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiling of stressed and pristine samples. The devices first undergo constant-current stress, during which their voltage fluctuates irregularly. Subsequent held-voltage measurements show a fast relaxation without the slow decay branch observed in the Au/Ti-contacted family. The XPS depth profiles show the same core-level positions away from the interface, and differ in the depth progression of the fitted O 1 s components, the stressed sample reaching the metal-oxide to silicon-oxide crossover earlier under the same programmed profiling sequence. With the slow branch absent, we measure and fit the residual relaxation without assigning a microscopic origin. It follows a stretched exponential whose exponent lies below unity over most of the bias range, and both its scale and dispersion vary with applied bias. A volatile device state should therefore be specified by its complete bias-dependent decay under stated measurement conditions, rather than by a single retention time.

items.title: Development and refinement of a FMECA framework for identifying patient safety risks in LLM-generated clinical summaries: a methodological pilot study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Claims that large language models (LLMs) improve clinical care are outpacing the evidence needed to support them, and there is a lack of structured methods to produce the safety-specific evidence required before their outputs are trusted in practice. Failure Mode, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) is medicine’s established route to this kind of proportional, pre-deployment safety evidence, but, to our knowledge, it has never been adapted to generative AI. This methodological pilot study aims to develop and refine the first FMECA framework for identifying and characterizing potential patient safety risks in LLM-generated clinical summaries. Methods An interdisciplinary panel ( n = 8) developed, through a two-round iterative expert consensus, a taxonomy of failure modes and adapted the standard FMECA dimensions (occurrence, severity, detectability) into 5-point ordinal scales. To refine the FMECA framework, 36 clinical summaries were generated by an open-weight LLM (GPT-OSS 120B) using data from Geneva University Hospitals: Three clinical reviewers annotated the summaries across two rounds. As exploratory secondary analyses, preliminary internal inter-rater reliability was assessed at the failure-mode, severity, and detectability levels, and internal usability was evaluated with an adapted System Usability Scale (SUS). Results From 78 candidate failure modes, the final taxonomy comprised 14 failure modes across six categories, with operational severity, detectability and occurrence scales. In the exploratory analyses, inter-rater agreement improved between rounds, reaching moderate-to-substantial agreement for failure-mode identification and good agreement for severity and detectability scoring; internal usability was rated good (SUS 79.2/100). Conclusions We propose a FMECA framework for the systematic identification and characterization of failure modes in LLM-generated clinical summaries. Occurrence and risk priority were deliberately not estimated, as the sample was designed for framework refinement: this taxonomy will highly benefit from large, empirical validations.
items.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

items.title: Design and implementation of a high-speed reversible arithmetic logic unit for power-efficient computing
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the design, simulation, and hardware validation of a high-speed, power-efficient reversible Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) architecture, implemented in Verilog HDL. The ALU consists of three modular blocks—Arithmetic, Logical, and Control Units—and employs reversible logic gates to minimize power consumption and information loss. The proposed design achieves a Total Reversible Logic Instruction Count (TRLIC) of 53, reflecting a 62.67% improvement over prior works. Functional verification was carried out through simulation in Xilinx Vivado and ISE 14.7, followed by FPGA prototyping on the NEXYS A7 (Artix-7) board, confirming accurate operation. Beyond FPGA validation, the design was synthesized and implemented as an ASIC using Cadence Genus and Innovus with the 90-nm CMOS technology, completing the RTL-to-GDSII physical-design flow. The ASIC implementation achieved a critical-path delay of 1.195 ns, with a reported switching power of 1.72 µW.

items.title: Deep learning‐based structure modeling of the Treponema pallidum proteome: Insights into pathogenesis and syphilis vaccine development
items.abstract: Abstract Treponema pallidum ssp. pallidum , the causative agent of syphilis, has a small proteome and encompasses numerous strains. Knowledge gaps remain in understanding the molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis of this bacterium, as well as the structure and function of the full complement of proteins encoded by T. pallidum . Here, an artificial intelligence‐based structure‐to‐function modeling workflow was used to investigate the complement of proteins encoded by T. pallidum . High‐confidence structure models were generated for 976 T. pallidum proteins, covering 99% of the proteome. Analysis of the generated models using the protein structure comparison server distance‐matrix alignment (DALI) enabled high‐confidence, structure‐based functional annotation of 877 T. pallidum proteins, including 240 of the 323 proteins of unknown function encoded by this pathogen. Additionally, 63 putative pathogenesis‐related proteins (PPRPs) and seven treponemal proteins with previously uncharacterized similarity to outer membrane proteins (OMPs) from Gram‐negative bacteria were identified. A workflow for B cell epitope (BCE) prediction identified 1133 surface‐exposed, host‐facing potential epitopes in known and predicted T. pallidum OMPs, of which 90 were prioritized based on bioinformatic analyses, biophysical properties, amino acid sequence conservation, and previous protein expression data. This work provides insight into T. pallidum pathogenesis through structure modeling‐based functional annotation, including characterization of proteins of unknown function. This study also informs syphilis vaccine design by identifying new potential T. pallidum OMPs, as well as host‐facing regions of T. pallidum OMPs that have conserved amino acid sequences in globally circulating strains.

items.title: Decoupling Metal Deposition from Contact Formation Enables Polarity Transformation in WSe2 Transistors
items.abstract: Polarity control in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor field-effect transistors (FETs) is essential for their integration into complementary logic circuits. However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V-1 s-1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V-1 s-1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

items.title: Crystallographic Design of Electrodeposited Copper for Ultra‐Low‐Temperature Cu‐Cu Direct Bonding
items.abstract: Low-temperature Cu-Cu direct bonding (<150°C) for 3D integration faces a severe bottleneck from interfacial voids caused by limited atomic diffusion. While nanocrystalline Cu (NC-Cu) has emerged as a promising bonding material owing to its high stored energy, the thermodynamic influence of initial crystallographic orientation remains unclear. Here, we systematically investigate the orientation-dependent bonding thermodynamics of NC-Cu thin films with (100), (111), and (101) orientations. Despite high internal energy, (100) and (111) Cu consume significant energy for internal defect curing (dislocation glide and twin annihilation), inducing void aggregation. Conversely, (101) Cu, despite not possessing the largest absolute total driving force, directs the largest fraction of its available positive driving force toward macroscopic grain-boundary migration, thereby achieving extensive interfacial-crossing growth and enhanced overall mechanical reliability. We demonstrate that reliable bonding requires targeted allocation of grain boundary energy, establishing a novel crystallographic design principle for advanced heterogeneous integration and solid-state joining technologies.

items.title: ConvNeXt ‐ FD : Fractal Dimension‐Regularized ConvNeXt for Robust Biomedical Image Segmentation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomedical image segmentation is a critical task in medical diagnosis and treatment planning, enabling precise delineation of anatomical structures and pathological regions. Despite significant advancements, challenges persist due to the inherent variability, noise and complex morphology present in diverse medical imaging modalities. This paper introduces ConvNeXt‐FD, a novel deep learning architecture for robust biomedical image segmentation, built upon a U‐Net‐like encoder‐decoder framework leveraging the powerful ConvNeXt backbone. Our approach integrates a hybrid loss function combining the Dice coefficient with a boundary‐aware regularization term inspired by a differentiable formulation of fractal dimension, designed to enhance the model's sensitivity to object boundaries and shape fidelity. We rigorously evaluate ConvNeXt‐FD across six distinct biomedical datasets: BUSI (breast ultrasound images), DDTI (thyroid ultrasound images), FluoCells (fluorescent cell images), IDRiD (diabetic retinopathy images for optic disc segmentation), ISIC2018 (skin lesion images) and MoNuSeg (nuclei segmentation). Experimental results demonstrate that ConvNeXt‐FD, particularly when initialized with ImageNet pre‐trained weights, achieves competitive and often superior performance compared to existing state‐of‐the‐art methods across various metrics, including Dice, Jaccard, Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity and False Positive Rate. The integration of ConvNeXt as a strong encoder, coupled with the boundary‐aware regularization, proves effective in capturing both high‐level semantic features and fine‐grained boundary details, leading to more accurate and reliable segmentations in challenging biomedical contexts.

items.title: Computational model of developmental self-assembly of a cortical microcircuit
items.abstract: Cortical microcircuits emerge from local developmental interactions, yet large-scale computational models typically prescribe connectivity rather than explain its formation. Here we use BioDynaMo to simulate the self-assembly of ~70,000 cortical neurons from 1,200 progenitors in 3D physical space through migration, neurite growth and contact-based synapse formation. With one calibrated filling fraction per connection type, the locally formed synapses reproduce experimentally measured connectivity across 64 connection types (mean absolute error 0.0062) without prescribing individual connections. The grown spiking networks sustain stable, inhibition-dominated activity, and the same developmental rules, given different targets, generate both a canonical cortical microcircuit and a visual-cortex variant. Inverting the migration programme produces a reeler-like column whose aberrant connectivity destabilises network activity. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic link between local developmental processes and the emergence of cortical anatomy, connectivity and function.

items.title: Comparative Study on the Translation Quality of "Three-Character Classic" by Large Language Models and Multimodal Large Models
items.abstract: With the widespread application of large language models (LLM) and multimodal large models (MLLM) in the field of machine translation, how to evaluate the translation quality of different models for ancient Chinese classics has become an urgent issue to be explored. This study takes the children's educational classic "Three Character Classic" as the research object, selects eight representative original sentences, and translates them into English using both LLM and MLLM. The translated texts are then quantitatively compared using the BLEU automatic evaluation tool. The aim of this study is to determine which type of model performs better in the English translation of classical Chinese texts and which model is more suitable for the translation tasks of Chinese classical literature. The study found that, here, fill in the actual experimental data: the BLEU and METEOR scores show which type of model performs better. This study provides empirical reference for AI-assisted English translation of Chinese ancient classics and also offers an empirical basis for the applicability of automatic translation quality assessment tools in the context of classical Chinese translation.

items.title: Code and data for: Electrode-area precision and odd-state quantization failure in neuromorphic memristive synapses
items.abstract: Simulation code and stored results for the Letter 'Electrode-area precision and odd-state quantization failure in neuromorphic memristive synapses'. Includes the interface-type memristor compact model, the precision-area law, the closed-form dead-weight fraction and SQNR, post-mapping of a trained network onto N conductance levels, hardware-aware training with a straight-through estimator (7 seeds), the clipping-threshold scan and device-to-device variability sweeps, with a numpy-only script that verifies the central numbers.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Chip‐Level Voltage Controlled Magnetic p‐Bits Array with Variation Compensation for Stochastic Neural Network Computation
items.abstract: The increasing computational and energy-efficiency demands of artificial intelligence are driving the development of new computing paradigms based on emerging memory devices. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) based on magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), benefiting from energy efficiency, CMOS compatibility, and fast sampling, show broad potential in stochastic neural networks. However, unavoidable device-to-device variations in MTJ switching probabilities hinder the realization of scalable p-bit chips. Here, we integrate a high-density array of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy MTJs (VCMA-MTJs) and employ a tail truncation strategy to compensate for their variations in probabilistic switching ranges, enabling chip-level p-bit functionality. Our VCMA-MTJ chip (VM-chip) successfully implements restricted Boltzmann machines (RBM) and deep belief networks (DBN) for image recognition, anomaly detection, image completion, and image generation, demonstrating the practical utility of this chip in stochastic neural networks. Furthermore, we propose a dual-control strategy that tunes both the amplitude and duration of the voltage pulse, significantly enhancing network performance and performing comparably to conventional software-generated pseudo-random numbers. Our work enhances the tolerance of probabilistic computing to variations in MTJ switching probabilities, offering flexibility in device selection and array integration. This approach may provide a promising pathway toward scalable p-bit hardware and cost-effective manufacturing in future probabilistic computing systems.

items.title: BinauralLM: spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation with large language model
items.abstract: Abstract Binaural audio is a practical spatial audio format for headphone playback and is widely used in immersive media such as games, VR/AR, and interactive multimedia. Currently, binaural audio is still largely obtained either by specialized recordings or by spatializing pre-recorded monaural signals, which limits flexibility for controllable content creation. While recent text-to-audio models can generate the required audio, most of them target monaural output or unconstrained stereo. They provide limited control over spatial attributes such as direction and motion. To address these challenges, we propose BinauralLM, a spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation framework with large language model (LLM). BinauralLM adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, we use a Qwen2.5 LLM to autoregressively generate coarse binaural token sequences conditioned on text and spatial prompts. To effectively couple semantic content with spatial cues, we introduce a spatial prompt encoder and an attention fusion module to produce a unified conditioning representation for binaural token generation. Second, we employ a flow matching model that takes the coarse binaural tokens as conditions and reconstructs high-quality binaural waveforms in the continuous domain. Experimental results on the BEWO-1M dataset demonstrate that BinauralLM achieves superior performance on standard text-to-audio metrics and binaural spatial metrics, and achieves higher MOS scores in perceptual evaluation, especially on spatialization quality. These results indicate that our proposed method offers an effective route to controllable and high-quality text-to-binaural audio generation.
items.venue: EURASIP Journal on Audio Speech and Music Processing

items.title: Biased Error Attribution in Multi-Agent Human–AI Systems Under Delayed Feedback
items.abstract: Human decision-making is often influenced by cognitive biases, especially under uncertainty and risk. Prior works have studied biases in single-step decision environments with immediate outcomes or in interaction with a single AI agent. However, less attention has been given to (1) cascaded settings with delayed outcomes, where decision at one step influences future system states and (2) to interaction with multiple AI agents. To study this, we designed a naval battle strategy game where participants interact with two AI advisors. We find asymmetric responses to positive and negative outcomes, with significant changes after negative outcomes. Participants failed to identify the actions responsible for failures and misattributed responsibility across AI agents, leading them to modify decisions steps weakly related to the true cause of poor performance. We refer to this behavior as bias in error attribution. Our findings show how cognitive biases can emerge in human-multi AI teams in cascaded settings.
items.venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting

items.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making
items.abstract: AIM: Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents’ clinical decision-making abilities. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction. RESULTS: The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p 85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

items.title: Anderson localization with single photons from a quantum emitter
items.abstract: Anderson localization of light is a fundamental emergent phenomenon in disordered systems. In arrays of coupled waveguides, it suppresses transport and causes photons to remain localized near the excitation site as coupling disorder increases. Here, we experimentally demonstrate Anderson localization using single photons emitted by a single-photon emitter in hexagonal boron nitride at room temperature. Despite the limited temporal coherence of the emitter, the photons undergo pronounced Anderson localization, evidenced by exponentially localized output intensity profiles in disordered waveguide lattices. Beyond the experimental demonstration, we develop a general theoretical framework for wave propagation in disordered tight-binding systems, showing that the configuration-averaged output intensity converges to a stationary spatial distribution at large propagation distances. In the case of off-diagonal disorder, this stationary profile is characterized by an effective localization length that exhibits a robust inverse-variance scaling with the disorder strength. These results establish defect-based room-temperature emitters as practical platforms for studying Anderson localization in integrated photonics and support their use in applications that exploit controlled disorder, including neuromorphic and quantum photonic architectures.

items.title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

items.title: An AI-powered trisomy 21 Research Assistant
items.abstract: Down syndrome, caused by trisomy 21, increases the risk of diverse co-occurring conditions. With more than 34,000 related publications indexed in PubMed as of early 2026, keeping pace with this expanding literature is challenging. While general-purpose large language models are widely used for information retrieval, they often rely on broad training data rather than specific evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves rigor and reliability of responses by linking model outputs to source texts. In research, source texts are peer-reviewed articles. Standard implementations treat all manuscript sections equally, allowing background text to rank as highly as experimental results. To focus model outputs on experimentally supported responses, we developed the T21 Research Assistant, a section-aware RAG system that prioritizes Results sections to ground responses in primary experimental evidence. The system draws exclusively from 1,789 open-access Down syndrome publications from PubMed Central, including 327 NIH INCLUDE-funded studies, and uses a multistage pipeline for query validation, retrieval, reranking, synthesis, and citation verification. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron models, it generates structured, cited responses. Evaluation using expert-curated questions demonstrated strong performance, achieving a BERTScore F1 of 0.712 and recall of 0.758, comparable to or exceeding leading proprietary and open-source models. T21 Research Assistant is available at: https://bioinformatics.cuanschutz.edu/t21-res-assi/.

items.title: Aligning heterogeneous DFT datasets: a graph neural network approach to cross-functional formation energies
items.abstract: Heterogeneous density functional theory (DFT) calculations, particularly plane-wave implementations, introduce systematic formation energy errors ranging from tens to hundreds of meV/atom, depending on the selection of exchange-correlation functionals, kinetic energy cutoffs, pseudopotentials, and dispersion corrections. As demonstrated by the MatPES dataset, identical structures can exhibit an average energy discrepancy of 107 meV/atom between PBE and r 2 SCAN calculations. Such method-dependent discrepancies hinder the integration of multi-source DFT data, greatly limiting the scale and quality of datasets for training robust materials AI models. Here, we resolve this fundamental data silo barrier via graph-based transfer learning. Leveraging 380,190 structurally paired PBE–r 2 SCAN entries from the MatPES database, we train a structure-aware graph neural network to predict cross-functional energy residuals and align inconsistent DFT energy scales. By adopting GPTFF model architecture, the model converts conventional PBE energies to r 2 SCAN-level accuracy with a mean absolute error of 14.3 meV/atom, compared with 18.2 meV/atom achieved by CHGNet. This versatile approach effectively upgrades massive legacy PBE datasets to high-precision r 2 SCAN standards. It enables reliable predictions of phase stability, battery voltage profiles, and reaction thermodynamics, while allowing the integration of multi-source DFT data to advance the development of high-performance materials foundation models.

items.title: Adjusting Nucleation Chemistry for the Atomic Layer Deposition of Antimony Selenide on Metal Oxide Surfaces
