items.title: Editorial: Big data mining and artificial intelligence in earth science
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for geoscience uses intelligent algorithms to extract concealed patterns from big Earth data, enabling more accurate predictions and decisions in scientific discoveries and applications, such as Earth's evolution, geological modeling, environmental monitoring, hazard mitigation, and resource exploration (Zhou et al., 2018(Zhou et al., , 2026)). Its evolution has followed a clear paradigm transition-from early expert systems through data-driven machine learning, to the current physics-informed, knowledge-data dual-driven approaches (Zhou et al., 2018;Zuo et al., 2023;Cheng et al., 2025). This progression is not merely incremental; it is fundamentally reshaping geoscience by integrating big data analytics with machine learning algorithms, and in doing so, redefining the practices of many researchers and engineers in their daily work (Zuo et al., 2023;Zhou et al., 2026). This is the reason why this special topic issue comes to exist here. It is devoted to showcase recent advances in the research and application of AI across many geoscience disciplines. It highlights innovative methodologies in data science, machine learning, and 2 / 14 generative AI technologies that address the integration and interpretation of multidisciplinary geoscientific data.The special issue is also initiated to commemorates the 10th anniversary of the Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences, established under the Chinese Society for Mineralogy, Petrology and Geochemistry in 2016, with Professor Zhou Yongzhang, then the awardee of the IAMG Felix Chayes Prize, as its inaugural Chair (Zhou et al., 2026). This marked the first organized effort in China to promote AI and big data research in mineralogy, petrology and geochemistry, and was among the earliest such professional bodies worldwide. In 2018, the committee published the textbook Big Data Mining and Machine Learning for Earth Science (Zhou et al., 2018). In April 2026, the 10th China Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences was held at Hefei, drawing over 1,200 participants-a clear indicator of the rapidly growing interest in intelligent geoscience.Featuring 18 original contributions, this special issue focuses on three transformative areas: intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits, intelligent sedimentary and reservoir evaluation, and intelligent prediction of Earth processes and geological systems. The methods span from conventional machine learning to deep learning, knowledge graphs, large language models (LLMs), and beyond, reflecting both the breadth and depth of current AI-driven geoscience research.The intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits is revolutionizing mineral exploration through the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced remote sensing. These technologies synthesize extensive geological, geophysical, and geochemical datasets to identify concealed mineralization patterns with exceptional precision. Predictive algorithms refine target selection, thereby reducing drilling costs and minimizing environmental footprint. Real-time fusion of drone and satellite imagery enables dynamic 3D modeling of subsurface structures. This intelligent approach not only accelerates discovery rates but also mitigates risks in structurally complex terrains. Ultimately, such systems empower geologists to make data-driven decisions, transforming traditional exploration into a sustainable, efficient, and scientifically rigorous pursuit for securing critical metal resources. This collection showcases recent advances in intelligent prospecting for solid metal deposits, underscoring a paradigm shift toward data-driven, multi-method integration. Wang et al. (2026) improve the interpretability of convolutional neural networks by applying SHAP and partial dependence plots, revealing apparent resistivity as the primary controlling factor in iron ore mapping. Their case study focuses on the Yemaquan iron ore concentration area in Qinghai Province, northwestern China, and successfully delineates several high-potential targets within the region. Zhao et al. (2026) employ LLMs to rapidly construct knowledge graphs for tungsten deposits, thereby enhancing reasoning capabilities and facilitating the extraction of prospecting indicators. Their study centres on methodological innovations for efficient knowledge graph construction in the mineral resource domain, proposing an LLM-driven framework guided by domain-specific geological knowledge. The framework is applied to a case study at the Dajishan Tungsten Mine in China. The results demonstrate that the LLM-integrated knowledge graph not only substantially accelerates the speed and scale of information integration but also enables deeper extraction of prospecting insights, highlighting its strong application potential. Zeng et al. (2026) apply co-simulation (Plurigaussian + turning bands) to jointly model grade and lithology, capturing spatial uncertainty in gold deposits. The method explicitly captures both auto-correlations and cross-correlations between variables, enabling realistic spatial reproduction of orebody geometry and internal heterogeneity. Results show that the outputting three-dimensional stochastic models effectively represent the spatial anisotropy and variability of mineralization, accurately delineating orebody continuity and its lithological controls. Shan et al. (2026) combine FLAC3D numerical simulation with machine learning, integrating chemical reactions and strain to predict gold targets. The study selects the Sanshandao-Haiyu gold belt as a case study to investigate the integrated application of these two approaches for deep mineral exploration, which remains poorly understood. First, chemical reactions are incorporated into FLAC3D via a custom-developed program to calculate the mineralization rate. Subsequently, the authors employ machine learning techniques to integrate simulation outcomes (i.e., volumetric strain and mineralization rate) with fault morphology in different combinations, constructing four predictive models for comparative validation. Based on the predictions, two prospective targets are delineated. Gao et al. (2026) propose a CPA attention mechanism for cross-regional knowledge graphs, achieving high F1-scores in complex entity extraction. This study proposes a novel knowledge graph construction and application framework centered on a Content-Position Attention (CPA) mechanism. The resulting knowledge graph system enables intelligent information retrieval, multi-dimensional correlation analysis, and mineralization potential prediction, demonstrating its practical effectiveness in supporting cross-regional resource management and intelligent decision-making. It offers a replicable technical pathway for knowledge management and decision analysis in the mineral resource domain.Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent systems-ranging from explainable deep learning and LLM-driven knowledge engineering to stochastic simulation and physics-informed machine learning-are making exploration more accurate, interpretable, and efficient, while addressing data heterogeneity and uncertainty in three-dimensional and cross-regional contexts.The intelligent evaluation of sedimentary reservoirs is revolutionizing hydrocarbon exploration through the integration of machine learning, deep learning, and automated seismic interpretation. These technologies synthesize multi-scale datasets-including well logs, core photographs, seismic attributes, and depositional analogs-to predict porosity, permeability, Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent approaches-encompassing unsupervised deep learning, hybrid inversion, semantic-guided simulation, and augmented experimental data-substantially enhance predictive accuracy, geological interpretability, and uncertainty quantification. They enable rapid, automated, and reproducible workflows that minimize subjective bias and computational overhead, while offering robust frameworks for reservoir characterization, dynamic management, and exploration in complex, data-scarce settings.Intelligent prediction of Earth systems and geological processes is revolutionizing geoscience by integrating multi-source data, physics-informed modeling, and advanced machine learning. Satellite remote sensing, ground-based geophysical surveys, and real-time sensor networks generate vast spatiotemporal datasets that, when processed by convolutional and recurrent neural networks, enable increasingly accurate forecasting of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides, and surface deformation. Hybrid approaches that embed physical conservation laws into deep learning frameworks enhance generalization beyond purely statistical correlations, while uncertainty quantification through ensemble methods and Bayesian inference delivers robust risk assessments. For long-term geological evolution, generative models and digital twin simulations reconstruct paleoenvironments and project future changes in hydrology, erosion, and sediment transport under climate forcing. Automated pattern recognition in seismic waveforms, ground-penetrating radar, and borehole logs accelerates hazard mapping and resource characterization. These intelligent systems reduce subjective interpretation, enable near-real-time early warnings, and support sustainable land-use planning. By bridging observations, theory, and computation, they transform traditional qualitative geology into a quantitative, predictive, and adaptive science for mitigating natural risks and managing Earth's resources.In this collection, the intelligent prediction of Earth sciences and geological processes encompasses diverse applications-from groundwater and atmospheric CO₂ to reservoir characterization and rock mechanics-all unified by data-driven, hybrid, and interpretable methodologies. Li et al. (2026) Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent prediction-via foundation models, bidirectional recurrent networks, physics-informed deep learning, ensemble algorithms, and optimized machine learning-strengthens accuracy, interpretability, and generalization under varied data constraints and across scales. They turn raw observations into actionable forecasts for resource management, carbon neutrality, geotechnical engineering, and hydrocarbon exploration, while prioritizing uncertainty quantification and feature importance analysis to build confidence and ensure practical relevance.Revealing prominent research frontiers and distinctive textures in AI for Geoscience, this special issue can serve as a valuable reference and the catalyst practitioners of data-intensive geoscience research. Nevertheless, we are aware that the papers do not comprehensively cover the entire field of AI in geoscience. Stepping back from a future vantage point, it is clear that many unresolved challenges remain, calling for persistent scientific investigation and innovation. Among them are included: Data heterogeneity and scarcity: Geoscientific data come from diverse sources (seismic, well logs, satellite, laboratory) with varying formats, resolutions, and quality. Many critical regions lack sufficient labeled samples, limiting the training of robust deep learning models and causing overfitting.Interpretability and trust: Deep learning models often act as "black boxes," making it difficult for geologists to validate predictions against physical principles. This hinders adoption in high-stakes decisions like drilling or hazard warning, where explainability is as important as accuracy (Zuo et al., 2023).Generalization across space and time: A model trained on one mineral deposit, basin, or geological setting frequently fails when applied to another due to differing tectonic histories, lithologies, or fluid properties. Transfer learning and domain adaptation remain open problems in geosciences.Computational and operational costs: Processing large-scale 3D/4D datasets (e.g., full-waveform inversion, climate simulations) demands massive computing resources.Real-time deployment in field operations is often impractical, and energy consumption raises sustainability concerns.As we look ahead, greater scientific attention should be directed toward the following issues, all of which are essential to advancing AI for geoscience (Zuo et al., 2023;Cheng et al., 2025;Zhou et al., 2026).Physics-informed and hybrid modeling: Embedding physical conservation laws (mass, momentum, energy) into neural networks will produce predictions that are both data-driven and physically consistent, reducing data dependence and improving extrapolation capabilities.Foundation models for Earth systems: Large pre-trained models based on multi-modal Earth data (imagery, time series, text) can be fine-tuned for diverse downstream tasks-from mineral mapping to earthquake forecasting-to offer a unified intelligence backbone for geoscience.Real-time digital twins: Integrating AI with continuous sensor streams and high-performance computing will enable dynamic digital replicas of subsurface reservoirs, volcanic systems, or coastal zones, supporting near-real-time hazard response and adaptive resource management.Human-AI collaboration and democratization: Future systems will prioritize interactive visual analytics and natural language interfaces, allowing geologists to query, question, and refine AI outputs. Open-source platforms and cloud-based toolkits will lower barriers, fostering global collaboration and equitable access to intelligent geoscience.

items.title: Echoes of Intelligence: What AI Could Learn From Bats
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid progress of deep learning has been driven in part by general principles of biological information processing, yet current AI systems still fall short of biological intelligence in critical ways such as integration of the computational and physical domains, i.e., embodied AI, and achieving autonomy in complex environments. This perspective argues that bat biosonar offers a particularly valuable model system for advancing embodied AI and autonomy in complex environments beyond the currently dominating vision‐centered and data‐intensive paradigms. Bats navigate dense and dynamic environments based on sparse trains of clutter echoes with random waveforms. These capabilities suggest alternative computational principles for perception and action: exploiting statistical rather than deterministic signal structure, extracting task‐relevant information from low‐bandwidth streams, and integrating morphology, actuation, and neural processing into closed‐loop embodied intelligence. This perspective reviews how bat biosonar differs from engineered sonar, identifies desirable capabilities that could inspire next‐generation autonomous systems, and outlines future research directions for deciphering and reproducing bat‐like intelligence through multimodal biological data, machine learning, neuromorphic processing, and biomimetic robotic platforms. By framing bat biosonar as a model for dynamic embodied intelligence, this perspective highlights a path toward AI systems that are more robust, parsimonious, and highly capable in real‐world environments.

items.title: Design of an ultra low voltage VDBA using bulk driven quasi floating gate techniques for high order biosignal processing
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a high-performance ultra-low-voltage (ULV) voltage differencing buffered amplifier (VDBA) operating from a 0.5-V supply. Consisting of an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) followed by a voltage follower (VF), the proposed VDBA combines bulk-driven (BD) and bulk-driven quasi-floating-gate (BD-QFG) MOS techniques to overcome threshold-voltage limitations and enhance the performance of subthreshold circuits. Designed in the Cadence Virtuoso environment using the TSMC 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed VDBA consumes only 370 nW and occupies 0.022 mm 2 area. Its applicability is demonstrated through a fifth-order Butterworth low-pass filter for ECG signals, achieving an electronically tunable cutoff frequency from 73.65 to 557.8 Hz, 1.1% THD for a $$\:100{\text{}\text{mV}}_{\text{p-p}}$$ input signal, and a 44 dB dynamic range. Monte Carlo and PVT analyses confirm the robustness of the proposed design, while experimental implementation using the commercially available LM13700 further validates the proposed filtering approach.

items.title: Design of an X-Band 50-W, 12-Way GaN HEMT Power Amplifier Using an Integrated FET Process
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and measurement of a 50W-class GaN HEMT power amplifier for X-band radar and satellite communication systems. To overcome single-device output limitations and achieve high integration, a 12-way parallel combining structure based on an Integrated FET process was proposed. The amplifier features integrated 4-way and 12-way divider/combiner stages within the chip to minimize loss. Phase and amplitude imbalances were resolved, achieving <0.4 dB amplitude error and <1° phase error. Alumina and Taconic RF-35 substrates were used for the RF and bias circuits, respectively, to ensure stable DC supply and high isolation. Evaluated at 10 GHz with a 25 us pulse width and 10% duty cycle, the fabricated amplifier demonstrated 47.78 dBm (approx. 60 W) output power, 44.11% PAE, 16.72 dB small-signal gain, and 12.76 dB large-signal gain, satisfying all design goals. This topology is applicable to next-generation high-power RF systems.
items.venue: The Transactions of The Korean Institute of Electrical Engineers

items.title: Design and Performance Analysis of Novel Single-Fin Core Shell Junctionless FinFET (CS-JL-FinFET)
items.abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling of conventional field-effect transistors intensifies short-channel effects, leakage current, degraded electrostatic control and mobility-related limitations, motivating the development of alternative device architectures with improved carrier transport and gate controllability. In this work, a single-fin core-shell junctionless FinFET (CS-JL-FinFET) is proposed using three-dimensional technology computer-aided design simulations. The proposed device employs core-shell doping to modify the internal electrostatic potential, carrier distribution and gate-to-channel coupling while retaining the junctionless operating principle. A conventional single-fin JL-FinFET with identical fundamental dimensions, material system, gate work function, bias conditions and simulation methodology is employed. The electrostatic and transport characteristics are evaluated through transfer and output characteristics, potential and electric-field distributions, transconductance, output conductance, capacitance, temperature-dependent behavior, intrinsic gain, Early voltage and circuit-level inverter operation. At the nominal operating condition, the proposed CS-JL-FinFET achieves an ON-state current of \(\:{10}^{-5}\)A/µm and an OFF-state current of \(\:{10}^{-16}\)A/µm, resulting in an \(\:{I}_{on}/{I}_{off}\:\)ratio of \(\:{10}^{11}\), compared with \(\:{10}^{10}\)for the conventional JL-FinFET. The proposed device also shows a subthreshold slope of 64 mV/dec, compared with 82.7 mV/dec for conventional JL-FinFET while the peak transconductance is reported to improve by 60-67%. The enhanced current modulation by increased output conductance, resulting in lower output resistance, intrinsic gain and Early voltage than the conventional device. Resistive-load inverter shows successful voltage inversion with a 0-0.5 V input swing. These results establish core-shell doping engineering as a promising approach for enhancing the current-driving and switching characteristics of nanoscale junctionless FinFET.

items.title: Deep operator networks for surrogate modeling of cyclic adsorption processes with varying initial conditions
items.abstract: Deep Operator Networks are emerging as fundamental tools among various neural network types to learn mappings between function spaces, and have recently gained attention due to their ability to approximate nonlinear operators. In particular, DeepONets offer a natural formulation for PDE solving, since the solution of a partial differential equation can be interpreted as an operator mapping an initial condition to its corresponding solution field. In this work, we applied DeepONets in the context of process modeling for adsorption technologies, to assess their feasibility as surrogates for cyclic adsorption process simulation and optimization. The goal is to accelerate convergence of cyclic processes such as Temperature-Vacuum Swing Adsorption (TVSA), which require repeated solution of transient PDEs, which are computationally expensive. Since each step of a cyclic adsorption process starts from the final state of the preceding step, effective surrogate modeling requires generalization across a wide range of initial conditions. The governing equations exhibit steep traveling fronts, providing a demanding benchmark for operator learning. To evaluate functional generalization under these conditions, we construct a mixed training dataset composed of heterogeneous initial conditions and train DeepONets to approximate the corresponding solution operators. The trained models are then tested on initial conditions outside the parameter ranges used during training, as well as on completely unseen functional forms. The results demonstrate accurate predictions both within and beyond the training distribution, highlighting DeepONets as potentially efficient surrogates for accelerating cyclic adsorption simulations and optimization workflows.
items.venue: Advances in Continuous and Discrete Models

items.title: Cumulative‐Stress‐Resilient Microelectromechanical Switches for Extreme Environment Applications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable electronics capable of operating under various and cumulative extreme environmental stressors remain a major challenge for space, nuclear, and defense systems. Here, we report a microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) switch that maintains reliable operation after cumulative exposure to radiation, extreme temperatures, and mechanical shock and vibration. A thermomechanically engineered suspended structure minimizes temperature‐induced deformation across a wide temperature range while maintaining mechanical stability under shock and vibration. Radiation‐tolerant structural and contact materials are selected based on their electrical, chemical, and mechanical stability under gamma and proton irradiation. The fabricated switch maintains functional electromechanical switching after sequential exposure to mechanical shock and vibration up to 2900 g and 2000 Hz, 1 Mrad gamma irradiation, temperatures from 4 to 450 K, and 100 MeV proton irradiation at a fluence of 10 12 p/cm 2 . Following cumulative exposure, endurance testing across 16 devices yielded a median of 1.03 × 10 6 cycles to the first loss of actuation, with individual devices operating for several million cycles.

items.title: Cross-lingual consistency of large language models: a six-language ICD-11 coding benchmark and evaluation methodology
items.abstract: Does a large language model (LLM) give the same label to the same content when that content is written in a different language? This cross-lingual consistency is not the same thing as accuracy, yet it has rarely been measured for tasks with a fixed label set. We present a benchmark and an evaluation method for it, using ICD-11 coding as the test case, in which a model reads an official disease definition and returns a code. The resource pairs 300 ICD-11 entities from 23 chapters with their official World Health Organization (WHO) definitions in English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Arabic and Russian. Because these are official translations, what the benchmark measures is consistency across the official ICD-11 language editions rather than pure language invariance. We grade predictions at four code levels, check every predicted code against the ICD-11 release, and measure agreement across languages with chapter-level Krippendorff’s alpha, treating the languages as raters. Across six current models (10,800 calls), chapter accuracy ranged from 14.3% to 83.6%, or from 9.3% to 63.2% if codes that do not exist in ICD-11 are counted as wrong, and chapter-level alpha from 0.48 to 0.92. The two measures did not always move together. One model was fairly consistent (alpha = 0.71) but reached the correct chapter in only 24% of cases, and on the items where all six languages agreed it was wrong twice as often as right. A repeated-sampling control showed that the differences between languages are larger than run-to-run variation. Agreement across languages alone cannot show that a model is correct, and we argue that both properties should be reported, at the same granularity, for any multilingual system that chooses from a fixed label set. The item set, prompts, scoring code and per-call logs are released.
items.venue: Northern European Journal of Language Technology

items.title: Cranio-Diff: Diffusion-based Cross-domain Craniofacial Reconstruction with 2D X-ray Skull
items.abstract: Abstract The identification of unknown human remains is a persistent humanitarian and forensic challenge. In forensic investigations, it becomes even more challenging when common biometric DNA identifications, such as soft-tissue or hair strands are not present, as they degrade with time. To narrow down the process of identification, few attempts have been made to identify an individual by reconstructing a face from the given skeletal remains ( i.e., skull) using generative AI models, such as CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, and diffusion models. However, they fail to effectively capture semantic information in craniofacial reconstruction, due to a mismatch in the alignment of structural information across modalities. To address this issue, we propose \textit{Cranio-Diff}, a diffusion-based framework for craniofacial reconstruction from 2D X-ray skull images. The proposed approach integrates skull-conditioned structural guidance through ControlNet with biometric text prompts to generate a face. The proposed \textit{Cranio-Diff} method is evaluated on skull-face dataset obtained from X-ray scans of 120 subjects in lateral and frontal views. To enable controlled evaluation, each face image is artificially synthesized across three age groups (25, 45, 65) and three BMI variations $\pm10\%$, yielding 4320 paired samples. This dataset is also curated across different facial modalities ( RGB and sketch) with different appearance conditions (hair and without hair). To the best of our knowledge, this is the only X-ray-face dataset with this magnitude. Extensive experiments showed that the proposed method achieves improved performance over the recent existing approaches in both generated image quality and retrieval task. Finally, to evaluate the performance of our proposed method, we have evaluated the quality of the generated image using FID, SSIM, LPIPS score. Additionally, retrieval performance is evaluated using recall@k, mAP@k and MRR@k. Obtained experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can be used as an alternate tool in providing aid in forensic investigations.

items.title: Crack–Defect Landscapes Enable Multimodal Memristive Switching in WS 2 Mono‐Bilayers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT While nano or micro cracks are often unavoidable during the scalable growth of 2D materials, their role and interactions with vacancies in facilitating variable memristive switching are generally overlooked in device applications. Addressing device‐to‐device and cyclic variability in 2D memristor demands a mechanistic understanding of vacancy dynamics and their conduction pathways. We unveil how point defects and intergranular cracks modulate dynamic memristor behavior in mono‐bilayer WS 2 lateral devices associated with varied sulfur vacancy concentrations, ranging from nearly pristine to ∼10 14 cm −2 , as confirmed by aberration‐corrected electron microscopic and spectroscopic investigations. The crack boundaries act as preferential sites for vacancy migration and charged species, facilitating resistive switching in polycrystalline like WS 2 mono‐bilayers. The observed conductance switching originate from Schottky barrier modulation at the WS 2 metal interface and the redistribution of vacancies within the channel. To enhance the device performance, controlled thermal annealing in distinct environments has been performed. The devices exhibited distinguishable switching for 800 cycles with consistent resistance ratios followed by onset of toggling state and later collapsing to trap state. These findings establish a direct correlation between atomic‐scale defects and memristive performance, providing fundamental insights into vacancy–crack interactions that govern charge transport and stability in 2D materials.

items.title: Construction, editorial practice, and AI-assisted evaluation of the Chinese Medical Research Reporting Specification Checklist System
items.abstract: With the development of academic publishing and the iteration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, the submission volume of Chinese journals has been increasing continuously, which imposes an increasingly heavy workload for peer review, editorial processing, and proofreading in academic journals. This study aimed to construct a localized, easy-to-operate, and efficient Chinese Medical Research Reporting Specification Checklist System (referred to as the Disclosure Checklist), apply it to editorial practice, and explore the accuracy, consistency and stability of AI Large Language Models (LLM) in the review of disclosure items. Based on the 10 core reporting checklists of the guidelines from the EQUATOR Network, we optimized them using the Delphi expert consultation method to better adapt to the Chinese context, and classified their recommendation levels using a 5-point Likert scale, and finally optimized into 9 types. The Kimi 2.5 fast model was used to review the reporting items in the original manuscripts and published manuscripts of two journals, and the paired t -test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare the improvement in reporting completeness between the two versions of manuscripts. Different research types of papers were selected and independently reviewed three times by the Kimi 2.5 fast model. The Friedman test was used to compare overall accuracy across the three review rounds, with post-hoc pairwise comparisons performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test at the level of study-design categories, and the Krippendorff's Alpha, and Gwet's AC1 tests were used to assess the consistency and stability of the three sets of results. R version 4.5.2 was used for statistical analysis. A total of 9 types of Chinese medical research reporting guideline checklists were optimized, including 281 items. The evaluation of 115 articles published after revision using the 8 types of checklists (meta analysis checklist was excluded) revealed that reporting quality scores were 4.12 points (95% CI: 3.42–4.82) higher in the published version than in the original manuscript, with the lower confidence limit indicating a minimum improvement of 3.42 points, a difference that is clinically meaningful for editorial quality assessment [Cohen's d = 1.08, Rosenthal's r = 0.736(0.639, 0.810)]. The Kimi 2.5 fast model reviewed 900 checklist disclosure items across 8 types of biomedical papers, with manual verification. The overall accuracy of the three rounds of review ranged from 72.67% to 75.78%, and did not differ significantly across rounds, while Krippendorff's Alpha was 0.635 (95% CI: 0.602–0.669), and Gwet's AC1 was 0.663 (95% CI: 0.631–0.691), all falling within the "moderate-to-substantial" agreement range. The Kimi 2.5 fast model shows certain potential in assisting the review of disclosure items in Chinese medical research articles, but optimization for error-prone items to further improve accuracy and consistency is still required. This study provides support for the future development of domain-specific intelligent agents for disclosure checklist review in Chinese medical journals. It is expected that in the near future, stable, accurate and reliable review AI models can be embedded into journal submission and peer review systems, so as to improve editorial efficiency, reduce the workload of reviewers, and enhance the transparency and quality of papers.

items.title: Compact convolutional neural networks for AI-based drone detection system
items.abstract: The increasing use of first-person-view drones in modern conflicts has created a demand for compact and reliable detection systems capable of operating in complex electromagnetic environments. These drones continuously transmit video signals through onboard video transmitters, generating radio-frequency emissions that can be exploited for early detection. This study investigates the use of lightweight convolutional neural networks for automated detection of drone signals captured by a software-defined radio-based electronic warfare framework. Samples are converted into rasterized time-domain images, providing a computationally efficient input representation suitable for embedded systems. Several custom model architectures were designed and benchmarked in terms of accuracy, model size, and inference performance using a dataset containing approximately 40,000 labeled images. In addition to offline testing, the models were integrated into a GNU Radio signal processing chain for real-time evaluation. Under the evaluated conditions, the compact models achieved high detection accuracy while maintaining small model size and low inference latency, supporting the feasibility of embedded radio-frequency monitoring.

items.title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"
items.abstract: Self-assembled networks of nano-objects have attracted growing interest as physical substrates for brain-inspired computation. The work of Milano et al. 1 is a valuable study of the dynamics of memristive networks of nanowires. The experimental data presented by the authors are comprehensive and of high quality, providing extensive material for validating stochastic conductance models in such systems. The compact Markovian model proposed in ref. 1 , formulated as a stochastic differential equation of the Itô type that combines deterministic return to equilibrium with random components (Gaussian noise and jumps), allows for the description of certain aspects of the dynamics and an assessment of the impact of stochasticity on computational capabilities within the reservoir computing paradigm. However, closer examination of the data from ref. 1 reveals that each key aspect of the conductance dynamics (deterministic relaxation, jump process, and Gaussian fluctuations) exhibits non-Markovian properties, which calls into question the original stochastic model and suggests a need for its fundamental revision.

items.title: Beyond the Syntax: Do Security Experts Trust LLMs for NIDS Rule Engineering?
items.abstract: As network threats evolve, manual Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) rule engineering has become a critical operational bottleneck. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for automating this process, their ability to produce production-ready rules remains unvalidated. This paper presents a human-centered investigation into LLM-based NIDS rule engineering, formalizing a context-aware generation framework and evaluating it through an exploratory user study with 10 domain experts. Our evaluation reveals a syntax-semantics paradox: although LLMs generate syntactically correct rules, experts find them only partially practically useful due to low specificity and logic hallucinations in 12% of cases. While the system received a favorable SUS score of 67, practitioners remain skeptical of its autonomous capabilities, viewing LLMs as support tools for drafting and verification rather than independent generators. Finally, our statistical analysis indicates that while large-scale models (≥ 70B) consistently produce syntactically valid rules, small models (≤ 4B) are largely ineffective for IDS rule generation.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: Balancing Performance and Energy Efficiency: A Comparative Review of Near-Data Processing, Heterogeneous Cores, Persistent Memory Controllers, and Chiplet-Based Disaggregated Memory
items.abstract: Computers keep getting faster, but moving data between memory and the processor can now cost more time and energy than the computation itself. This paper presents a comparative review of four architectural directions that try to deal with this problem: near-data processing (NDP), heterogeneous core integration, persistent memory controllers, and chiplet-based disaggregated memory. NDP moves part of the work to where the data already sits, so fewer transfers are needed. Heterogeneous processors mix fast cores with frugal ones and give each task to whichever suits it better. Persistent memory controllers manage memory that keeps its contents without power, so they have to balance durability, write endurance, and latency. Chiplet and disaggregated designs break a system into smaller pieces that can be scaled separately, but they bring interconnect delays, coherence problems, and harder software management. Recent survey literature was reviewed and compared in terms of performance, energy efficiency, scalability, reliability, programmability, and cost. The review finds that no single approach wins on every workload. NDP fits data-heavy tasks built from simple operations, heterogeneous cores fit mixed workloads, persistent memory fits applications that need durable state, and chiplets fit systems that have to grow in flexible ways. The most promising path is to combine them through coordinated hardware and software design and to measure energy at the whole-system level. Gaps remain in shared benchmarks, workload-aware scheduling, and cross-layer evaluation.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Atomistic understanding of hybrid bonding in Cu interfaces using multiscale microscopy
items.abstract: Achieving wafer-scale reliability in Cu–Cu hybrid bonding remains challenging due to process-induced non-uniformities and the limited understanding of buried interfacial contamination. Here, we employ a correlative multiscale microscopy framework combining scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom probe tomography (APT) to investigate bond degradation from the wafer center to the edge. We observe progressive bond deterioration characterized by interfacial delamination, reduced Cu grain size, and the formation of a nanometer-scale amorphous interlayer. While such interlayers have been widely observed in hybrid bonding, their chemical nature has remained largely unresolved. APT directly reveals that the interlayer consists of Si-, C-, and N-bearing species consistent with contributions from the adjacent SiCN dielectric, together with Cu oxide and organic-related contaminants. By correlating interlayer chemistry and thickness with microstructural evolution, we establish a direct link between interfacial contamination, suppressed cross-interface grain growth, and bond degradation. Furthermore, we observe a progressive thickness-dependent degradation, where interfacial thickening from ∼1 to 2 nm at the center to ∼2 to 3 nm in the donut region is accompanied by deterioration in mechanical bond integrity and localized delamination. These findings provide atomistic insight into the chemistry governing hybrid bond reliability and establish quantitative guidelines for process optimization toward wafer-scale integration.

items.title: Applications of Directed Self-Assembly Lithography in Advanced Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: As semiconductor devices continue to scale down, conventional lithography technologies face increasingly severe challenges in resolution, stochastic defect control, and manufacturing cost. Block copolymer (BCP) directed self-assembly (DSA), which offers molecular-scale control over pattern formation and compatibility with existing lithographic processes, has emerged as a promising complementary nanopatterning technology for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This review summarizes the microphase-separation mechanisms of DSA, major guiding strategies including graphoepitaxy and chemoepitaxy, and pattern-transfer techniques such as dry and wet etching and sequential infiltration synthesis (SIS). In terms of device applications, particular emphasis is placed on recent progress in DSA for Fin Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) fin patterning, silicon nanostructures, high-density contact holes, memory devices, two-dimensional semiconductors, and Complementary Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor (CMOS) optoelectronic devices. Key challenges, including defect control, process-window optimization, pattern transfer, and wafer-scale manufacturing, are further discussed, together with future directions involving the integration of DSA with extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, advanced etching, and data-driven process optimization. This review aims to outline the technological evolution of DSA from nanoscale self-assembly toward integration into advanced semiconductor manufacturing and to provide a reference for high-resolution patterning at advanced technology nodes.

items.title: Analysis of changes in the electrical parameters of cement composites under the simultaneous action of direct current and chloride ions
items.abstract: Purpose. The aim of this study is to investigate changes in the electrical parameters of cement composites subjected to the simultaneous action of direct electric current and chloride ions, as well as to establish the patterns of variation in electrical conductivity and equivalent electrical resistance during long-term ion electromigration. Methodology. Experimental studies were carried out on cement-sand mortars. Cylindrical specimens were exposed to a 0.35 mol/L sodium chloride solution and to water under conditions of forced passage of a pulsed direct current through the specimens with continuous monitoring of current intensity and voltage. The state of the system was evaluated based on the analysis of current intensity, voltage, and the calculation of equivalent electrical resistance according to Ohm’s law. Findings. The presence of chloride ions was found to significantly increase the electrical conductivity of the cement composite. The stabilized current intensity in specimens exposed to the NaCl solution was approximately 38 mA, whereas in the specimens stored in water it was only about 7.4 mA. Accordingly, the equivalent electrical resistance decreased from approximately 4050 Ω to 785 Ω. During long-term exposure, an initial increase in current intensity followed by its gradual decrease was observed, indicating an increase in system resistance caused by chloride ion migration and their partial binding by cement hydration products. Originality. The study established the regularities of changes in current intensity and equivalent electrical resistance under the influence of electromigration processes and chloride binding within the porous structure of cement stone. New data were obtained on the manifestation of polarization processes in cement composites under cyclic electrical loading. Practical value. The obtained results can be used to assess the durability of concrete and reinforced concrete structures operating under chloride-containing environments and stray current conditions typical of transport infrastructure facilities, bridges, tunnels, and hydraulic engineering structures.
items.venue: Bridges and tunnels Theory Research Practice

items.title: Alternative origins of polarity in compressively strained SrTiO3-RENiO3 capacitors
items.abstract: Since its original prediction 25 years ago, room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3 remains an ongoing pursuit. In this work, we investigate the structural, electrical, and electromechanical properties of highly strained epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors with rare earth nickelate electrodes. The SrTiO3 layers experience compressive strains up to −3% and exhibit pronounced tetragonality, comparable to that of bulk PbTiO3. Variable-temperature electrical measurements and room-temperature piezoresponse force microscopy reveal butterfly-shaped capacitance–voltage hysteresis and domain-like electromechanical response typical of ferroelectric materials. However, the overall behavior is inconsistent with a stable ferroelectric state. We therefore propose an alternative mechanism for the observed polarity in our samples based on spatially inhomogeneous internal fields. Our first-principles calculations show that such fields may arise from charge discontinuities between the formally charged NdNiO3 layers and charge-neutral SrTiO3 layers.

items.title: Adaptive low-power Electronic Control Unit operation through priority-based interrupt-driven Controller Area Network mechanism
items.abstract: The increasing number of Electronic Control Units (ECUs) in modern vehicles contributes to auxiliary electrical power demand, particularly when non-critical controllers remain active during periods of limited communication. This work proposes a priority-based adaptive ECU power-management framework using Controller Area Network (CAN) communica-tion, ECU functional criticality, interrupt-driven state transitions, and inactivity monitoring. ECUs are classified into high-critical, moderately critical, and low-critical categories to determine their eligibility for active, idle, and controlled sleep operation. The framework additionally considers communication throttling and reduced workload operation for eligible non-critical functions while excluding safety–critical ECUs from inactivity-triggered sleep control. A time-dependent energy model is formulated to account for ECU activity, sleep duration, workload, wake-up events, and transition energy. The framework is evaluated using a representative four-node analytical case study. Under the selected power and operating assumptions, the case study yields an estimated 26.5% reduction in auxiliary ECU power consumption. This value represents an analytical proof-of-concept rather than experimentally validated automotive performance. Future work will focus on large-scale CAN simulation, Hardware-in-the-Loop validation, and automotive-grade hardware implementation.

items.title: ABACUS: Adapting Unified Foundation Model for Count Image Understanding and Generation
items.abstract: We present ABACUS, a unified vision-language model that jointly addresses object counting, crowd counting, referring-expression counting, and count-faithful image generation within a single 3B-parameter model. ABACUS introduces three contributions: density-aware adaptive zooming paired with an objectness map from multi-head self-attention decomposition to spatially ground count predictions; a boundary-aware count policy trained via GRPO with nested local, boundary, and global rewards to eliminate over- and undercounting at crop boundaries; and a cycle-consistent GRPO strategy in which the frozen understanding branch scores generated candidates on count-deviation and aesthetic quality, closing the understanding-generation synergy gap without any external critic or annotation. ABACUS achieves state-of-the-art results across seven benchmarks spanning object counting (FSC-147, CARPK), crowd counting (ShanghaiTech A/B), referring-expression counting (REC-8K), count-faithful generation (CoCo-Count, T2I-CompBench, GenEval), and count reasoning (CountQA), surpassing both task-specific specialists and larger generalist models. Project page is at https://mondalanindya.github.io/pages/ABACUS/.

items.title: A thermodynamic and phase-field framework for domain nucleation and polarization switching in Al1− x Sc x N
items.abstract: Uniaxial wurtzite ferroelectrics have emerged as promising candidates for non-volatile memory applications; however, their large coercive fields remain a major challenge for device operation. Reducing the coercive field requires a fundamental understanding of the role of domain nucleation during polarization reversal, where polarization discontinuities at the domain walls are expected to strongly modify the nucleation energy barrier. Here, we develop a thermodynamic framework for inversion domain nucleation and polarization switching by combining classical nucleation theory with phase-field simulations. Using Al0.7Sc0.3N as a representative system, we demonstrate that the polarization discontinuity associated with inclined domain walls produces large local electrostatic potentials and electric fields, leading to high energy barriers for nucleation and highly anisotropic nucleation morphology. By explicitly incorporating electrostatic interactions among ionized dopants, electronic carriers, and bound charges arising from polarization discontinuities at domain walls, we find that the availability of free electronic carriers reduces the energy barrier for nucleation and brings the predicted coercive field closer to experimentally observed values and below dielectric breakdown limits. By explicitly incorporating the nucleation process, phase-field simulations capture the electric-field-driven evolution of domain nucleation and growth, enabling quantitative investigation of switching kinetics, providing a powerful approach for understanding and predicting polarization-switching behavior and long-term reliability in ferroelectric memory devices.

items.title: A plane bipartite graph whose only Fries structure is not a Clar structure
items.abstract: A plane bipartite graph whose only Fries structure is not a Clar structure. A perfect matching of a plane bipartite graph makes a bounded face alternating when the face's boundary edges alternate between matched and unmatched; the Fries number is the most alternating faces in one perfect matching, and the Clar number the most pairwise vertex-disjoint alternating faces in one perfect matching. Bérczi-Kovács and Frank (Discrete Mathematics, 2024) write that the conjecture that a plane graph has a largest Clar set extending to a largest Fries set is still open for general perfectly matchable bipartite plane graphs. This record gives a counterexample: an 11-square polyomino (two vertical bars of four squares joined by a horizontal bar of five) with 116 perfect matchings, Fries number 8 reached by exactly one perfect matching whose alternating squares contain at most 4 pairwise disjoint ones, and Clar number 5. check_fries_clar.py verifies this by listing every perfect matching. Claude (Anthropic), a large language model, assisted this work under my direction: it wrote and ran the search and checking code, checked the results and the literature, and assisted with the writing throughout; the text is my own and I take full responsibility for it.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A data-efficient PINN-Bayesian optimization framework for state variable active filter design
items.abstract: Designing an analog active filter is rarely a single-target exercise: cutoff frequency, quality factor, gain, power draw, total harmonic distortion (THD), and sensitivity to component spread all have to be pulled into line at once. In practice, this still means loop after loop of SPICE runs and manual tweaking, which eats up design time and computing budget alike. This paper instead builds a Bayesian Optimization loop around a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate to automate the synthesis of State Variable Filters (SVFs). Adaptive sampling of the design space, LTspice-based circuit simulation, PINN surrogate modeling, and Bayesian Optimization are brought together so that optimal component values can be located with far fewer costly simulation runs. By incorporating the governing circuit relationships, analytical transfer function, frequency–response characteristics, and stability constraints into PINN training, the proposed surrogate captures the nonlinear relationship between component values and filter performance while maintaining physical consistency. That trained surrogate then drives the Bayesian search, quickly narrowing in on Pareto-optimal filter configurations across cutoff frequency accuracy, passband gain, quality factor, power consumption, THD, and sensitivity. The resulting design reached a cutoff frequency of 10.01 kHz, a gain of 0.998, a quality factor of 0.709, an estimated active-filter power of 12.4 mW, THD of 0.32%, and a sensitivity index of 0.048, with Bayesian Optimization converging in 37 iterations and an average run time of 42.8 s. Benchmarked against Random Search, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Differential Evolution, the proposed framework consistently reached lower objective values than any of them. A TL084-based hardware prototype backed up the simulation results as well: measured cutoff frequency, gain, and phase response tracked the LTspice predictions closely, and the absolute THD deviation came in at just 0.04%. Taken together, these results point to a PINN-assisted Bayesian Optimization framework that is efficient, scalable, and well suited to next-generation computer-aided design of analog and mixed-signal circuits.
items.venue: Engineering Science and Technology an International Journal

items.title: A Study on the Design and Control of a 6.6-kW Three-Phase Interleaved Totem-Pole PFC for OBC Applications
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, control, and experimental verification of a 6.6-kW three-phase interleaved Totem-Pole power factor correction (PFC) converter for on-board charger (OBC) applications. Three parallel PFC phases are operated with PWM carrier phase shifts of 0°, 120°, and 240° to distribute the input current and reduce the synthesized input-current ripple. SiC MOSFETs are employed for high-frequency switching operation. A digital control system consisting of output-voltage and input-current control loops, a Second-Order Generalized Integrator Phase-Locked Loop (SOGI-PLL), a notch filter, and duty feed-forward was implemented for stable DC-link voltage regulation and input-current control. A 6.6-kW prototype operating with a 220-Vrms input and a 400 V DC-link voltage was developed. Compared with the two-phase interleaved configuration under the same Boost inductance and switching frequency conditions, the three-phase interleaved configuration reduced the maximum input-current ripple from 3.4 A to 2.28 A, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 32.9%, while increasing the ripple frequency from 140 kHz to 210 kHz. The threephase interleaved configuration exhibited an input-current THD up to 3.871 percentage points lower than that of the two-phase configuration while maintaining a comparable power factor. At rated load, the developed converter achieved an input-current THD of 5.438%, a power factor of 0.996, and an efficiency of 97.978%.

items.title: A Non‐Volatile Heterogeneous Quantum Dot III‐V/Si DFB Laser With Optical Memristive Behavior
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, we introduce a non‐volatile heterogeneous quantum dot (QD) III‐V/Al 2 O 3 /Si distributed feedback (DFB) laser exhibiting optical memristive behavior. The device operates in the O‐band (∼1300 nm) with a threshold current density of 234 A/cm 2 and a side‐mode suppression ratio exceeding 48 dB. Co‐integrated Al 2 O 3 ‐based memristors produce bipolar resistive switching, yielding non‐volatile wavelength shifts of ∼46 pm and ∼ 17 dB peak power contrast with zero static holding power. The III‐V/Al 2 O 3 /Si heterojunction memristor I – V hysteresis is also modeled. This new device enables simultaneous coherent light generation and persistent optical state storage, establishing a new class of active photonic memory for neuromorphic and reconfigurable wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) applications.

items.title: A Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional Neural Network Applications
items.abstract: Abstract The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

items.title: A Deep Digital Multilayer Processor Architecture with Projection-Enforced Manifold Admissibility
items.abstract: Fully Digital Implementation: The architecture shifts from analog memristive crossbars to standard-cell digital CMOS logic, eliminating analog thermal drift, write-endurance wear, and process-voltage-temperature variations while ensuring strict bit-level determinism. Low-Rank Factorized Projection: By projecting input vectors onto the ten-dimensional physical symmetry manifold using a two-stage matrix decomposition, the processor slashes multiplier logic by over forty times compared to full dense evaluation while maintaining single-cycle execution. Synchronous Digital Shunt-on-Error: A parallel subtraction tree continuously calculates the geometric distance between the current state and the admissible manifold, instantly clearing the pipeline and suppressing invalid data if noise or corruption exceeds the safety threshold. Exact Integer Arithmetic Unit: Floating-point units are completely replaced by dual-integer datapaths operating over an algebraic integer ring, using hardwired shift-and-add logic to execute exact complex algebra with zero mantissa rounding, no denormal stalls, and zero numerical drift over arbitrary run lengths. Multilayer Associative Memory: High-speed on-chip spline lookup tables combined with a high-order polynomial associative memory engine trap computational states into discrete topological basins, storing hundreds of millions of distinct patterns without crosstalk or hallucination. Bufferless Direct Interconnect: Processing nodes communicate across an eight-hundred-sixty-one lane direct static mesh with eighty dedicated connections per node, achieving an aggregate throughput exceeding twenty-seven terabits per second with zero packet collision, no arbitration logic, and identical median and tail latencies. Symmetrical Phase Clocking: Die-wide timing is locked across seventy-two discrete sectors via a circulating shift-register ring and balanced distribution tree, suppressing phase jitter and eliminating clock skew across large silicon areas. Silicon Profile: Designed for modern four-nanometer fabrication, a monolithic core integrates roughly forty million standard gates onto an area of approximately eleven square millimeters, operating at eighteen watts under standard cooling solutions.

items.title: 3-Fazlı Modüler Çok Seviyeli Güç Faktörü Düzeltici Dönüştürücünün Dinamik Modellenmesi ve Pasif Parametre Optimizasyonu
items.abstract: Bu çalışmada, sanayi uygulamalarında yüksek güç kalitesi ve verim sağlayan 3-fazlı Modüler Çok Seviyeli Güç Faktörü Düzeltici (MMC-PFC) dönüştürücü sisteminin analitik tasarımı ve performans analizi gerçekleştirilmiştir. Çalışmanın temel amacı, aktif bir Sirkülasyon Akımı Bastırma Kontrolcüsü (CCSC) kullanılmaksızın, pasif bileşen boyutlandırma kriterleri ve rezonans yönetimi ile sirkülasyon akımlarını sınırlandırmak, alt modül kapasitör gerilim salınımlarını sınırlandırmak ve standartlara uygun şebeke akım kalitesi elde etmektir. Sistem mimarisinde anahtarlama kayıplarını minimize etmek adına Silisyum Karbür (SiC) MOSFET yarı iletken teknolojisi tercih edilmiş; alt modül kapasitansı ile kol ve şebeke indüktansları enerji salınımları ve rezonans kısıtları doğrultusunda analitik olarak boyutlandırılmıştır. Üst seviye kontrolde eksenli çift döngülü PI denetleyici ile birim güç faktörü ve kararlı DC bara gerilimi hedeflenirken, alt seviyede PSC-PWM modülasyonu ve hücre gerilim dengeleme algoritması uygulanmıştır. Gerçekçi parazitik bileşen parametrelerini içeren MATLAB/Simulink benzetim modellerinden elde edilen bulgular; nominal tam yük ve hafif yük işletim noktalarında DC bara geriliminin kararlılıkla korunduğunu, hücre gerilim dalgalanmalarının emniyet sınırları içerisinde kaldığını ve şebekeden birim güç faktörüne yakın, düşük THD değerli sinusoidal akım çekildiğini doğrulamıştır. Elde edilen sonuçlar, önerilen pasif boyutlandırma ve kontrol yaklaşımının karmaşık aktif sirkülasyon kontrolörlerine ihtiyaç duymadan yüksek performanslı bir MMC-PFC yapısı sunduğunu göstermektedir.

items.title: simantalahkar/lammpskit: LAMMPSKit v1.2.1
items.abstract: LAMMPSKit v1.2.1 LAMMPSKit is a Python toolkit for post-processing and analysing molecular-dynamics simulations run with LAMMPS. It was built for simulations of HfTaO-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) devices. It tracks how conductive filaments form and evolve, analyses atomic, charge and displacement distributions, and produces publication-ready plots. This release is an archived snapshot of the code as of 29 July 2025, tagged v1.2.1. It is the version that matches the published PyPI package and Docker image below. What the package does Filament analysis: OVITO-based cluster analysis that tracks filament connectivity, gap, size and height over time (lammpskit.ecellmodel.filament_layer_analysis). Distributions: atomic, charge and displacement distributions by element and position (lammpskit.ecellmodel.data_processing). Trajectory input: readers for LAMMPS trajectory and displacement files (lammpskit.io), with input validation and descriptive error messages (lammpskit.config). Designed for large trajectories (more than 1M atoms, more than 10K frames). Plotting: publication-ready time-series and comparison plots with central control of fonts and styles (lammpskit.plotting). Example workflow: usage/ecellmodel/run_analysis.py runs four analyses: filament evolution, displacement by species, charge distribution and atomic distribution under different voltages. Changes in v1.2.1 (since v1.2.0) Improved the reliability of the GitHub Actions status and coverage badges, and added automated coverage-badge generation to the CI pipeline. Added a fail-safe Codecov upload that runs on Python 3.12 only, to avoid duplicate uploads. Fixed the tests badge so it points to the docker-ci.yml workflow. Updated version references across the documentation and configuration files. No change to the analysis, I/O or plotting code is recorded for this release; see CHANGELOG.md for the full history, including 1.0.0 (modular restructuring, timeseries plotting module, configuration system, extended test suite with visual regression tests). Install and run PyPI: pip install lammpskit==1.2.1 (requires Python 3.12 or later; NumPy, Matplotlib and OVITO 3.12.4 or later) Docker: docker pull simantalahkar/lammpskit:1.2.1 Documentation: https://lammpskit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ Citation If you use LAMMPSKit in your research, please cite the paper that describes the simulations it was built for: S. Lahkar et al., Decoupling Electric Field and Temperature-Driven Atomistic Forming Mechanisms in TaOx/HfO2-Based ReRAMs using Reactive Molecular Dynamics Simulations, arXiv:2505.24468 (2025), https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2505.24468 To cite this exact software version, use the DOI that Zenodo assigns to this release. Related software The simulations analysed with LAMMPSKit were run with the integrated CTIP–EChemDID package for LAMMPS: https://github.com/simantalahkar/LAMMPS-CTIP-EChemDID Licence GPL-3.0-or-later. Author: Simanta Lahkar.

items.title: Xenosophy: preregistrations of the next phase
items.abstract: Preregistration of the test of generation announced in "Xenosophy: Asking About Contact When No Common Frame Is Guaranteed" (version 0.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23816129). The test asks whether the approach's procedures of variation, applied to its distinctions, lead an AI analyst to hypotheses about a published study's object that AI judges rate as testable and absent from the field more often than hypotheses given under a plain instruction to be bold, or under a generic list of heuristics. A further arm tests the practice of the author's laboratory as a whole, reported as a black box, against the plain instruction. The cases are drawn from listed pools by euro reference rates published after this record is made public. The document fixes the design, the rules of scoring and what counts against the approach before any case is drawn; it may add conditions to those of the announcement, never weaken them. Use of AI. The design and every decision in it are the author's. The document was drafted under the author's decisions by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), which also compiled the pools, compiles one of the lists of the field record and takes part in the tally; it is not independent of the test. The test uses AI systems as analysts (ChatGPT; Claude Opus 5.5), judges (GLM, Qwen; Gemini in reserve), the source of a control and a parallel tallier (DeepSeek), a compiler of the field record (Perplexity), and a tallier used only if the tallies diverge (Kimi). No AI system is an author or contributor.

items.title: When Is High-Bandwidth Flash Cost-Effective for LLM Inference?
items.abstract: Can high-bandwidth flash (HBF) make LLM inference cheaper than adding GPUs? By storing weights closer to the GPU than SSD, HBF may reduce the number of GPUs needed for model capacity. However, this integration is only justified if it meets service targets and its cost is recovered. We simulate this integration using public component data across nine dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, five workloads, two GPU platforms, and 1--100 GPUs. At fixed demand, HBF reduces the minimum GPU count to meet a service target in 98 of 468 comparisons; majority of them are paused and short sessions, 63 remain cost-effective at half a GPU price per HBF stack. For single short-chat users, HBF enables large MoEs, e.g. DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2, to meet a relaxed service target on one RTX~4090 GPU, where conventional serving fails. At fixed GPU count, HBF improves throughput in 48\% of matched comparisons below 16 GPUs and 13\% at larger counts. Even at 100 RTX~4090-scale GPUs, cascaded HBF raises offline throughput by 16.4--26.5$\times$ for three large MoEs. We found savings and throughput gains arise in different scenarios.

items.title: Vishal442005/PI-S4M-Transdermal-CPS: v1.0.0: Physics-Informed Selective State-Space Transdermal CPS
items.abstract: PI-S4M v1.0.0: Physics-Informed Selective State-Space Modeling for Transdermal Control We are pleased to announce the initial open-source scientific release of PI-S4M, an end-to-end Cyber-Physical System (CPS) for closed-loop transdermal drug delivery. Key Highlights Multi-Frequency Metrology: 25-frequency tetrapolar RF-BIS (100 Hz–1 MHz) with active bootstrap guarding and real-time Kramers-Kronig causality audit ($\chi_{\text{KK}}^2 = 1.46 \times 10^{-5}$, well within the IEEE TIM 0.15% limit). CWT-RLS Adaptive Denoising: Continuous Wavelet Transform and Recursive Least Squares filter decoupling ambulatory motion artifacts (>75% artifact suppression). Physics-Informed SSM Surrogate: Discretized selective continuous state-space model learning non-Fickian anomalous diffusion with $O(N)$ linear recurrence (2.8 ms latency on ARM Cortex-M4). Conformal CC-MPC Actuation: Finite-sample distribution-free uncertainty intervals (95% PICP) maintaining drug flux strictly within the therapeutic window while enforcing thermal tissue safety ($T_{\text{skin}} \le 41.5^\circ\text{C}$). Hardware Efficiency: INT8 quantized deployment consuming only $15.8\ \mu\text{J}$ per inference on an ARM Cortex-M4 ($35.4\text{ KB}$ Flash, $18.5\text{ KB}$ SRAM), enabling >800 days of autonomous battery life on a single CR2032 coin cell. What's Included in This Release Complete source code (src/): forward electro-diffusion PDE solver, CWT-RLS filter, K-K audit engine, PI-S4M architecture, and CC-MPC optimizer. Reproduction & benchmark scripts (scripts/). Simulation configurations (config/sim_config.yaml). Pytest test suite (tests/). Native, 100% editable Microsoft PowerPoint architecture presentation (architecture/Research1_Architecture.pptx) and 300 DPI vector schematics.

items.title: Vertical GaN Trench MOSFET‐Based Devices for Multifunctional Optoelectronic Logic Gates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of optoelectronic technology has highlighted the potential of optoelectronic hybrid logic circuits in low‐power logic circuits. While two‐dimensional (2D) materials are commonly used in traditional optoelectronics, challenges remain in device stability, mass production, and integration efficiency with existing semiconductor technologies. To meet the demand for high‐performance materials in optoelectronic logic gates (OELGs), this study develops GaN‐based OELGs with high responsivity and low power consumption, aiming to overcome limitations of conventional devices and address future optoelectronic integrated system requirements. Through optimization strategies including trench etching, damage repair and vertical structural design, the developed GaN MOSFETs demonstrate exceptional performance: a responsivity ( R ) of 2.1 × 10 4 A/W, a photo‐to‐dark current ratio (PDCR) exceeding 10 7 , and rapid response speeds ( τ rise / τ fall of 2.0 ms/1.1 ms). The optical communication module validates their feasibility in communication transmission, providing crucial experimental evidence for optoelectronic logic gate research. The successfully developed OELGs operate stably under basic logic states, confirming their viability in next‐generation photonic logic computing circuits. This work demonstrates a proof‐of‐concept GaN trench MOSFET platform for optoelectronic logic operations. It exhibits photogain with millisecond‐scale response and a clear gain–speed trade‐off, showing promising potential for photonic logic circuits and ultraviolet optical signal processing.

items.title: Verify Before You Fetch: Reliable KV Cache Compression for LLM Inference
items.abstract: Long-context applications, long-lived agents, and multi-agent systems require large language models (LLMs) to process and retain extensive information. In these settings, the KV cache can exceed GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity, necessitating offloading to host memory, where CPU-to-GPU transfers can dominate inference latency. While KV cache compression can reduce data movement, query-agnostic compression that guarantees accurate attention for arbitrary queries is extremely challenging, if not impossible. We introduce VerKV, a hybrid approach that provides $(ε, δ)$ guarantees for approximating attention on any given query. VerKV maintains a compact set of query-agnostic pivotal tokens on the GPU, together with a token-level sketch of the full KV cache, while retaining the complete cache in CPU memory. We introduce a novel stochastic sampling procedure, PoissonComp, to select the pivotal tokens. At inference time, our proposed KVFetch algorithm uses the pivotal tokens and the sketch to estimate the relative error of the resulting attention computation. If the estimate satisfies a user-specified $(ε, δ)$ tolerance, inference proceeds without accessing host memory. Otherwise, VerKV performs query-aware retrieval to fetch additional tokens from the CPU, refining the attention computation to meet the required tolerance. Thus, VerKV enables attention with bounded approximation error while minimizing CPU-to-GPU transfers. We show that PoissonComp outperforms state-of-the-art approaches to KV cache compression. Combined with KVFetch, it achieves near-dense performance (90-100% of dense quality at 32K context length, averaged over RULER and LOFT), using Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Ministral-3-8B, while reducing the GPU memory footprint by 8-32x and keeping CPU-to-GPU memory fetches within 2-23% of the cache per generated token, depending on the model.

items.title: Told the Answer Is Not Taught to Reason: What On-Policy Self-Distillation From Privileged Context Transfers to a Language Model, Why Its Gains and Losses Divide Along Whether the Student Can Ever Hold What the Teacher Was Told, and the Controls That Would Separate Three Signals Under One Loss
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research On-policy self-distillation trains a language model on its own samples against the token distribution of the same model shown something the student never sees: a reference solution, a final answer, execution feedback or a demonstration. Early 2026 reports credited the recipe with matching reinforcement learning at a fraction of the sampling cost. Later 2026 studies report the opposite on thinking models: accuracy falls by up to 17 percent relative on competition mathematics, by up to 40 percent in another study, and agents trained this way can end below their untrained base. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the disagreement is not about the method but about three signals that one loss carries at once. A mode signal comes from the teacher's prompt format and reasoning mode; a behaviour signal comes from the confidence, brevity and absence of checking that knowing the answer licenses; an information signal comes from the content of what the teacher was told. On mathematics with students trained in non-thinking mode, ablations that shuffle or delete the privileged content show that the reported gain does not come from that content, and that the gain measured in the student's own non-thinking mode is largely the mode signal. Marker counts and per-token loss attributions show that much of the reported harm is the behaviour signal. The paper argues, using the imitation-gap results from robot and control learning, that the behaviour signal is safe to transfer only when the student can come to hold the information - in its weights, because the information recurs across instances, or in its own context before the step that needs it. Per-problem answers to unseen problems meet neither condition. The paper consolidates 34 published values in a table and a figure, states a reading procedure, sorts 17 published repairs by the signal each removes, and names six measurements that would settle what remains open.
